<deliverable>A coverage matrix: | Endpoint | Inputs read | Validation | Verdict | Evidence (quoted code) |, followed by the systemic-gap findings and a prioritized gap list ordered by exploitability (public unauthenticated first).</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every PARTIAL/MISSING verdict quotes the unvalidated use-site line.
- No verdict rests on 'the route looks fine' — evidence or UNRESOLVED with the missing file.
- The gap list contains findings only; fix suggestions limited to one sentence each.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A per-endpoint coverage matrix with quoted evidence for every verdict, systemic-gap findings (non-strict schemas, unvalidated params/webhooks, double parsing), and an exploitability-ordered gap list.

prompts.title: Idempotent Background Job Worker with Retry & Backoff
prompts.description: Implement a queue worker that is idempotent, retries with backoff, and routes poison messages to a dead-letter queue, with concurrency and shutdown semantics pinned down.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement a worker for the {{queue_name}} queue in {{queue_system, e.g. 'BullMQ on Redis / Celery / SQS + Node consumer'}} that processes {{job_type, e.g. 'invoice-generation'}} jobs.</goal>
<rationale>Jobs are delivered at-least-once and the current handler sends duplicate {{side_effect, e.g. 'emails'}} whenever a retry occurs; idempotency is the whole point of this task.</rationale>
<boundaries>Use the existing queue client in {{queue_client_file}}; do NOT add a new queue library. Do NOT change the producer/API side. Handler logic in {{existing_handler_file}} is correct for the happy path — reuse it, don't rewrite it.</boundaries>
</task>

Requirements:
- Idempotency: derive an idempotency key from {{key_source, e.g. 'job payload's invoiceId'}}; before executing the side effect, check-and-record it in {{idempotency_store}} so a redelivered job is a no-op. State explicitly what happens if the process crashes between the side effect and the acknowledgment.
- Retry policy: {{retry_spec, e.g. '5 attempts, exponential backoff 1s→5m with jitter'}}; retryable vs. permanent failure distinguished by {{failure_classification, e.g. '5xx/network = retry, 4xx/validation = permanent'}}.
- Poison messages: after final attempt, route to {{dlq_name}} with the original payload, attempt count, and last error; never silently drop.
- Concurrency: {{concurrency_limit}} jobs per worker; no unbounded in-flight promises.
- Graceful shutdown: on SIGTERM stop fetching, let in-flight jobs finish up to {{grace_period}}, then requeue/abort.

<contract>
<deliverable>{{worker_file}} complete; anchored edits for worker registration; tests in {{test_file}} covering: duplicate delivery no-op, retry-then-succeed, permanent failure to DLQ, and shutdown with an in-flight job (may be a scripted/manual verification if the test framework can't do it — say which).</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- {{test_command}} passes, output pasted verbatim.
- No at-most-once assumptions anywhere: every side effect is guarded by the idempotency check.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

State the delivery semantics of {{queue_system}} accurately (verify against the installed version in {{package_manifest}}) — do not assume exactly-once.
prompts.expectedOutput: A worker with idempotency-key check-and-record, classified retry/backoff, DLQ routing with context, bounded concurrency, graceful shutdown, four behavior tests, and accurate at-least-once reasoning including the crash window.

prompts.title: Diagnose Failing/Stuck Background Jobs from Evidence
prompts.description: Verbatim-evidence debugging prompt for jobs that fail silently, retry-storm, or stall, requiring root-cause localization before any fix.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Find the root cause of {{symptom, e.g. 'email jobs piling up in the queue with zero processed since Tuesday'}} and propose the minimal fix.</goal>
<rationale>{{impact, e.g. 'Password-reset emails are not being delivered; users are locked out.'}} Prior guesses have already cost us a day — work from evidence only.</rationale>
<boundaries>Diagnostic-first: do NOT propose code changes until the root cause is localized and distinguished from downstream symptoms. When a fix is proposed, it must be the smallest change that addresses the root cause, not a worker rewrite.</boundaries>
</task>

<environment>
{{runtime_and_versions, e.g. 'Node 20.11, BullMQ 5.34.1, Redis 7.2 (from package.json + redis-server --version)'}}
Queue/job configuration: {{queue_config_paste}}
Deployment: {{deploy_context, e.g. '2 worker replicas on ECS, deploy happened Monday 18:00'}}
</environment>

<evidence>
{{verbatim_logs_and_errors, e.g. 'worker stderr excerpt, failing job's stacktrace from the queue UI, redis INFO memory excerpt'}}
</evidence>

Method:
1. Restate the failure signature from the evidence (what exactly is observed), then list candidate causes that fit ALL of it — explicitly discard candidates that contradict any piece of evidence.
2. Identify which checks would discriminate between the surviving candidates (commands I can run), ordered cheapest-first.
3. If the evidence already isolates the cause: name it, quote the log line(s) that prove it, and give the minimal fix.
4. If it involves a library behavior, verify against the installed version in <environment> before asserting how the library behaves — version-drift is a live suspect here.

<contract>
<deliverable>Failure signature; candidate list with evidence-based eliminations; discriminating checks OR root cause with quoted proof; minimal fix (anchored edit) + how to verify it resolved (what metric/log line changes).</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>Every causal claim cites a quoted log line or a runnable check. Anything not yet provable is labeled HYPOTHESIS, not asserted.</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A restated failure signature, candidate causes with evidence-based eliminations, cheapest-first discriminating checks or a proven root cause with quoted logs, a minimal anchored fix, and a verification signal.

prompts.title: File Upload Handler with Size, Type, and Storage Guards
prompts.description: Build a file upload endpoint that enforces size limits, sniffs real content type, stores outside the webroot with generated names, and cleans up temp files.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement POST {{upload_path}} in {{framework}} accepting {{file_kinds, e.g. 'profile images (jpeg/png/webp), max 5 MB'}}, storing to {{storage_backend, e.g. 'local disk under /data/uploads (not webroot) / S3 via existing client'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Uploads are the classic RCE/DoS vector: extension-only checks, unbounded sizes, and webroot storage are the three failure modes this task must avoid by design.</rationale>
<boundaries>Use only {{allowed_packages, e.g. 'the multipart parser already in package.json'}}; no new dependencies. Do NOT modify other routes. Must preserve: existing auth middleware on the route.</boundaries>
</task>

Requirements:
- Enforce the size limit at the parser/stream level so oversized uploads are aborted mid-transfer, not after buffering the whole body in memory.
- Validate by content sniffing (magic bytes) or the parser's file-type check, not by client-supplied filename extension or Content-Type header alone.
- Generate the stored filename server-side (random/UUID + safe extension from the sniffed type); never use the client filename as a path component. State where path traversal is prevented.
- Store outside any directory served as static files (or with content-disposition/content-type forcing for S3) and say which you did.
- No secrets or absolute server paths in responses or logs; return the stored key/id only.
- On any failure after a partial write, clean up the partial/temp file.

<contract>
<deliverable>{{handler_file}} complete; registration as anchored edit; tests in {{test_file}}.</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Tests: valid file stored and retrievable by id; oversized rejected ({{test_method}}); wrong-content-type-with-image-extension rejected; filename '../../etc/x' cannot influence the stored path.
- Memory: handler does not load the full file into memory (say how — streaming/bus boy limits/multer limits with evidence from the code).
- {{test_command}} passes; paste output verbatim.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: An upload handler with stream-level size abort, magic-byte type validation, server-generated safe filenames, non-webroot storage, partial-file cleanup, and tests covering each acceptance criterion with verbatim output.

prompts.title: Streaming Large Payloads with Backpressure (Design + Implementation)
prompts.description: Advanced prompt for streaming large file exports/proxied responses with correct backpressure, error-mid-stream semantics, and memory bounds, requiring options-and-tradeoffs first.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement {{endpoint, e.g. 'GET /reports/:id/export.csv'}} in {{framework}} streaming potentially {{size_scale, e.g. '10M rows / several GB'}} from {{source, e.g. 'Postgres via cursor / S3 object'}} to the HTTP response without buffering the payload in memory.</goal>
<rationale>The current implementation buffers and dies at {{failure_point, e.g. '~500MB with OOM on the 512MB container'}}; correctness here means bounded memory under slow clients, not just 'works locally'.</rationale>
<boundaries>No new infrastructure. {{db_driver_or_sdk}} is already installed — verify the streaming/cursor API against the installed version before using it; do not invent streaming methods. Must preserve: existing auth check and the CSV header format in {{reference_file}}.</boundaries>
</task>

Before implementing, compare 2–3 viable approaches for {{framework}} (e.g. readable stream piped to response vs. async iterator writing chunks manually vs. framework-native streaming helper). For each: how backpressure is handled, how a mid-stream source error surfaces (headers already sent — status code is no longer changeable), and client-abort cleanup. Then pick one and state the deciding criterion.

Implementation requirements:
- Backpressure must be real: no .read() loops ignoring write() return values / drain events; memory stays bounded regardless of client speed — state the mechanism.
- Client disconnect: source resources (cursor, S3 stream, DB connection) are released; verify and describe the cleanup path.
- Mid-stream failure: define and implement the observable contract (e.g. truncated body + connection close), since 200 was already sent; document it in the handler comment.
- Response headers: correct content-type, and content-length omitted or streamed-encoding per the chosen approach.

<contract>
<deliverable>The options comparison (compact table), chosen approach + deciding criterion, {{handler_file}} complete, and a load test script or command sequence that demonstrates bounded memory ({{memory_probe, e.g. 'curl to /dev/null with --limit-rate 10k while watching process RSS'}}).</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Peak RSS during the probe stays under {{rss_budget}} while serving a {{payload_size}} response to a throttled client.
- Client abort leaves no leaked connection/cursor (state how you verified).
- {{test_command}} passes; paste outputs verbatim.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A compact options table covering backpressure/mid-stream-error/abort-cleanup per approach, a chosen mechanism with deciding criterion, the streaming handler with bounded memory and documented truncation contract, and a memory-probe verification with verbatim evidence.

prompts.title: General-Purpose PR Review with Findings Table
prompts.description: Baseline review of a single pull request producing an evidence-backed findings table, a verdict, and questions for the author.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review the pull request diff below and produce an evidence-backed findings report I can act on without re-reading every line myself.</goal>
<rationale>The change touches {{component_or_module}} and ships to {{environment}} on {{date}}. Defects found now are far cheaper than defects found in production.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Review ONLY the diff provided; do NOT invent or assume code that is not shown.
- Do NOT comment on formatting, naming, or style preferences unless I explicitly ask.
- Do NOT inflate severity to seem thorough; a correct "no findings" is a valid outcome.
</boundaries>
</task>

<diff>
{{paste_full_pr_diff_here}}
</diff>

<output_contract>
1. **Findings table** with columns: Severity (blocker / major / minor / info) | File:line | Issue | Why it matters | Suggested fix | Confidence (high / medium / low).
   - Every finding MUST quote the exact diff lines it refers to.
   - Confidence "low" means you are unsure — say so; never present a guess as fact.
   - If you cannot determine something from the diff, write UNKNOWN rather than assuming.
2. **Verdict summary** (2–4 sentences): approve / approve-with-comments / request-changes, plus the main risk of shipping this change even if you approve.
3. **Questions for the author**: anything the diff cannot answer on its own (intent, rollout, test coverage).
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every table row contains a quoted code snippet from the diff.
- No finding references code outside the provided diff.
- The verdict names at least one residual risk even when approving.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A findings table (severity × file:line × issue × why-it-matters × fix × confidence) with quoted diff lines, a 2–4 sentence verdict naming residual risk, and a questions-for-author list.

prompts.title: PR Triage and Risk Classification
prompts.description: Rapidly classify a PR by risk, blast radius, and required review depth so reviewers can route their attention where it matters.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Triage the pull request below: classify its risk, estimate its blast radius, and tell me how much review depth it actually needs.</goal>
<rationale>Our team reviews {{pr_count}} PRs per week with {{reviewer_count}} reviewers; misallocating deep review to trivial PRs and rubber-stamping risky ones is our biggest review failure mode.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Base every claim on the diff and metadata shown; do NOT speculate about code you cannot see.
- Do NOT rubber-stamp: even a "low risk" verdict must state what could still go wrong.
- Do NOT review the code itself in detail here; this is routing, not review.
</boundaries>
</task>

<pr_metadata>{{title, description, linked ticket, author, CI status}}</pr_metadata>
<diff_summary>{{files changed, insertions/deletions, or full diff if small}}</diff_summary>

<output_contract>
1. **Risk classification**: low / medium / high, with 2–4 quoted evidence points from the diff (e.g. "touches auth middleware: `verifySession(...)` in src/auth/guard.ts").
2. **Blast radius**: which subsystems, data paths, or user flows this change can affect; mark UNKNOWN for anything not determinable from the diff.
3. **Recommended review depth**: skim / standard / deep / specialist (security, performance, DB), and why.
4. **Hotspots**: the 1–3 hunks a reviewer must read line-by-line, quoted.
5. **Verdict line**: one sentence: risk + biggest residual unknown.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Risk level is justified by quoted evidence, not adjectives.
- Every claimed blast-radius item traces to a file or symbol in the diff.
- "Low risk" verdicts still name at least one thing that could go wrong.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A triage report: risk class with quoted evidence, blast-radius map (UNKNOWN where undeterminable), recommended review depth, 1–3 quoted hotspot hunks, one-sentence verdict.

prompts.title: PR Review Against Acceptance Criteria
prompts.description: Check whether a PR actually delivers its linked issue's acceptance criteria, using a per-criterion coverage matrix with quoted code.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Determine whether this pull request actually satisfies each acceptance criterion of its linked issue — with quoted code as proof.</goal>
<rationale>PRs here frequently implement the happy path and drift from the ticket; I need conformance evidence, not a general code-quality opinion.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Judge conformance ONLY against the stated acceptance criteria; do NOT add criteria of your own.
- Do NOT review style, performance, or security here unless a criterion demands it.
- If a criterion cannot be confirmed from the diff, mark it PARTIAL or UNVERIFIABLE — never assume it is met.
- Out-of-scope changes you notice: list them under "Scope creep"; do NOT review them.
</boundaries>
</task>

<issue>
{{issue title, description, and acceptance criteria, verbatim}}
</issue>
<diff>
{{paste_full_pr_diff_here}}
</diff>

<output_contract>
1. **Coverage matrix**: | Acceptance criterion | COVERED / PARTIAL / MISSING / UNVERIFIABLE | Evidence (quoted code from the diff) | Gap |
2. **Scope creep**: changes in the diff that serve no stated criterion, each quoted.
3. **Verdict**: ready / not-ready, plus the single most important gap.
4. **Questions for the author**: only where the diff is genuinely ambiguous about intent.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every COVERED row quotes the implementing code; no bare assertions.
- MISSING and UNVERIFIABLE rows state exactly what evidence is absent.
- The verdict follows mechanically from the matrix (any MISSING = not-ready).
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A requirement-coverage matrix (COVERED/PARTIAL/MISSING/UNVERIFIABLE with quoted code), a scope-creep list, a ready/not-ready verdict, and targeted author questions.

prompts.title: Design Document / RFC Review
prompts.description: Critique a design doc or RFC by stress-testing its options, failure modes, and unstated assumptions before implementation begins.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review the design proposal below and tell me whether it will hold up — before we spend implementation effort on it.</goal>
<rationale>Design mistakes cost 10–100x more to fix after code exists; the team needs honest challenge now, not validation. Push back wherever the proposal is weak — disagreeing with the author is explicitly welcome.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Critique the DESIGN, not the writing quality or formatting.
- Do NOT propose a full alternative architecture unless you first show the proposed one fails.
- Distinguish what the document says from what you infer; label every inference.
- If the document lacks information needed to judge a claim, say UNKNOWN and name the missing input.
</boundaries>
</task>

<design_doc>
{{paste RFC / design doc / ADR here}}
</design_doc>
<context>
{{constraints: team size, traffic, latency budget, existing stack, deadline}}
</context>

<output_contract>
1. **Claims table**: | Design claim | Supported / Unsupported / UNKNOWN | Evidence (quoted passage) | Risk if wrong |
2. **Alternatives the doc should have considered**: {{2-3}} options with pros, cons, and how each fails; a decision matrix weighted by {{your decision criteria}}.
3. **Failure modes**: the top 3 ways this design breaks under {{peak load / growth / team change}}, each traced to a specific design element.
4. **Verdict**: proceed / proceed-with-changes / rethink, and the criterion that decided it.
5. **Questions for the author**: decisions the doc made implicitly.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every critique quotes the passage it targets.
- The decision matrix uses my stated criteria, and the verdict names its deciding criterion.
- At least one genuinely hard question the author has not answered.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A claims table with quoted passages, 2–3 alternatives with a weighted decision matrix, top-3 failure modes, a verdict with deciding criterion, and hard questions for the author.

prompts.title: Cross-Cutting Architecture Review of a Diff
prompts.description: Review a diff for architectural integrity: layering, dependency direction, invariants, and drift from the system's stated design rules.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review this diff for architectural integrity: does it respect the system's layering, dependency rules, and stated invariants — or does it quietly erode them?</goal>
<rationale>Architectural decay happens one reasonable-looking PR at a time. Each individual change passes local review; the erosion is only visible when checked against global rules. This system is {{system_description}} and must remain maintainable by {{team_context}}.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Judge ONLY against the architecture rules and invariants provided; do NOT invent rules and then flag their violation.
- Do NOT review style, micro-performance, or test coverage — this pass is structural.
- Quote the exact diff lines that violate or strain a rule; no ungrounded "this feels coupled".
- If a rule cannot be evaluated from the diff alone, mark it UNKNOWN and say what additional file you would need.
</boundaries>
</task>

<architecture_rules>
{{layering/dependency rules, e.g. "UI never imports from data layer directly", "no new cross-service calls without an event", "public API of package X is frozen"}}
</architecture_rules>
<invariants>
{{must-preserve list, e.g. "billing writes stay idempotent", "tenant isolation enforced at repository layer"}}
</invariants>
<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>

<output_contract>
1. **Rule-violations table**: | Rule | Severity | File:line | Violation (quoted code) | Why it matters | Suggested remedy | Confidence |
2. **Invariant check**: each invariant: PRESERVED / STRAINED / BROKEN / UNKNOWN, with quoted evidence.
3. **Coupling introduced**: new dependency edges the diff creates (module → module), each quoted.
4. **Verdict**: architecturally sound / sound-with-reservations / violation, plus the cheapest change that restores integrity if violated.
5. **Questions for the author**.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every flagged violation maps to a stated rule AND quoted code.
- No rule is flagged that was not in my list.
- The remedy for the top violation is a concrete, minimal change — not a re-architecture.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A rule-violations table with quoted code, a per-invariant PRESERVED/STRAINED/BROKEN/UNKNOWN check, a new-coupling list, a verdict with the cheapest restoring change, and author questions.

prompts.title: API Contract Review
prompts.description: Review a new or changed API surface (endpoints, schemas, errors, versioning) for contract clarity, backward compatibility, and consumer impact.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review the API contract change below for correctness, backward compatibility, and consumer impact before it ships.</goal>
<rationale>This API is consumed by {{consumers: e.g. "our mobile apps (versions still in the wild), the partner integration, and the web client"}}; breaking a contract breaks clients we cannot redeploy.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Review the contract only: endpoints, request/response shapes, status codes, error bodies, versioning, pagination, auth requirements.
- Do NOT review the implementation behind the contract.
- Treat every compatibility claim as needing evidence from the spec/diff; mark UNKNOWN where the diff does not show the old shape.
- Do NOT flag hypothetical consumers I did not list.
</boundaries>
</task>

<api_change>
{{OpenAPI diff, route definitions, or endpoint code diff, verbatim}}
</api_change>
<existing_contract>
{{current API shape if separate, or "contained in diff"}}
</existing_contract>

<output_contract>
1. **Breaking-change table**: | Change | Breaking / Non-breaking / UNKNOWN | Affected consumer | Evidence (quoted spec lines) | Mitigation |
2. **Contract quality findings**: severity-ranked issues (ambiguous nullability, inconsistent error shape, missing rate limits, leaking internals), each with quoted evidence and a concrete fix.
3. **Error & edge-case surface**: which failure modes are representable by the contract and which are silently undefined.
4. **Verdict**: ship / ship-after-fixes / redesign, with the top compatibility risk stated even if shipping.
5. **Questions for the author**.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every breaking-change row cites quoted spec lines and a named consumer from my list.
- Compatibility verdicts never assume the old shape when it is not shown.
- At least the top risk appears in the verdict even on a "ship".
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A breaking-change table (consumer × evidence × mitigation), severity-ranked contract-quality findings with quoted lines, an error-surface analysis, and a ship verdict naming top risk.

prompts.title: Adversarial Review: Attack This Diff
prompts.description: Review-as-attacker: actively try to break the change — exploit inputs, abuse flows, escalate privileges — and report exploitable paths with reproduction sketches.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Attack this change. Your job is to find ways an adversary could exploit, bypass, or abuse exactly what this diff introduces — and prove each attack is real, not theoretical.</goal>
<rationale>This is authorized defensive review of our own codebase before merge. The change touches {{attack_surface: e.g. "the password-reset flow and the session service"}}; anything exploitable here ships to production behind {{exposure: e.g. "a public endpoint"}}.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Attack ONLY what the diff changes or newly exposes; pre-existing issues go in "Adjacent observations", clearly separated.
- Do NOT report a vulnerability class generically ("could be SQL injection") — demonstrate the concrete path through THIS code or mark it UNVERIFIABLE.
- Do NOT assume defenses that are not shown in the diff or the provided context; absence of evidence = note it as UNKNOWN, not as safe or unsafe.
</boundaries>
</task>

<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<relevant_context>
{{only the surrounding code needed to trace the attack path, e.g. route registration, middleware chain, schema}}
</relevant_context>

<output_contract>
1. **Exploitable findings**: | Severity | File:line | Attack (who, what input, what outcome) | Path through the code (quoted lines, step by step) | Reproduction sketch (request/payload) | Fix | Confidence |
2. **Failed attacks**: attacks you attempted to construct that the code defends against — quote the defending lines. (This prevents re-litigating settled ground.)
3. **UNKNOWN list**: attack paths you could neither confirm nor rule out, and the exact file/symbol you would need.
4. **Verdict**: safe-to-merge / merge-after-fixes / do-not-merge, plus the worst-case impact of the top finding.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every exploitable finding includes quoted code lines forming the attack path.
- No finding relies on an imagined attacker capability beyond {{threat_model: e.g. "an unauthenticated external user"}}.
- The verdict states worst-case impact even if merging.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: An exploitable-findings table with quoted attack paths and reproduction sketches, a failed-attacks section with defending lines quoted, an UNKNOWN list, and an impact-stated merge verdict.

prompts.title: Security Pass on Auth & Input-Handling Diffs
prompts.description: Focused security review of a diff that touches authentication, authorization, or user input handling, with defensive framing and evidence requirements.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Security-review this diff, which changes {{auth_or_input_area: e.g. "login rate limiting and the profile-update endpoint"}}. This is authorized defensive work on our own application; the goal is prevention before merge.</goal>
<rationale>Changes to auth and input handling are our highest-severity incident source; a missed check here becomes a breach, not a bug ticket.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Focus on: authorization checks on every new/changed path, injection and unsafe interpolation, secret handling, session/token lifecycle, and unvalidated input crossing a trust boundary.
- Do NOT do a general code-quality review; off-topic observations go in "Notes" only.
- Do NOT invent surrounding code; where enforcement might live outside the diff (middleware, framework defaults), mark it UNKNOWN and name what you would need to confirm it.
- Every finding quotes the vulnerable lines from the diff.
</boundaries>
</task>

<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<security_context>
{{auth model, framework, trust boundaries, e.g. "session cookie set by gateway; roles checked via requireRole middleware"}}
</security_context>

<output_contract>
1. **Findings table**: | Severity (critical / high / medium / low) | File:line | Vulnerability | Quoted code | Why it is exploitable | Suggested fix | Confidence |
2. **Checks verified present**: security controls you confirmed in the diff (quote them) — so the author knows what was examined, not just what failed.
3. **UNKNOWN assumptions**: defenses that might exist outside the diff, each with the exact symbol/file needed to confirm.
4. **Verdict**: merge / merge-after-fixes / block, with residual risk stated in all cases.
5. **Questions for the author**.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every finding and every verified control quotes code from the diff.
- Severity is not inflated: a missing rate-limit log is not "critical".
- UNKNOWN items name the specific file or symbol that would resolve them.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A severity-ranked findings table with quoted vulnerable lines, a verified-controls list (also quoted), an UNKNOWN-assumptions list with resolution targets, and a risk-stated merge verdict.

prompts.title: Dependency & Supply-Chain Diff Review
prompts.description: Review dependency changes (manifest + lockfile) for supply-chain risk: provenance, version pinning, transitives, and license or maintenance red flags.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review this dependency change for supply-chain and maintenance risk before we merge it into {{project_name}}.</goal>
<rationale>A dependency is unreviewed third-party code running with our privileges; package-name confusion, abandoned packages, and unpinned versions are real incident vectors, and model knowledge of packages has a training cutoff — so verify, don't recall.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Base findings on the manifest/lockfile diff and the registry data you can actually inspect (package metadata, publish dates, maintainers); do NOT invent package contents.
- Do NOT flag a package merely for being small or unfamiliar — name the concrete risk mechanism.
- Where you cannot verify something (e.g. no registry access), mark it UNKNOWN and give the exact command that would resolve it (e.g. `npm view <pkg> time maintainers`).
- Do NOT review application code in this pass.
</boundaries>
</task>

<dependency_diff>
{{package.json / requirements.txt / go.mod diff AND lockfile diff, verbatim}}
</dependency_diff>
<environment>
{{runtime versions, private registry config if any}}
</environment>

<output_contract>
1. **Risk table**: | Package@version | Change type (new / upgraded / downgraded) | Risk (typosquat pattern / unpinned range / stale maintenance / new transitive count / license) | Evidence | Verification command | Confidence |
2. **Transitive blast radius**: notable new transitive dependencies and what they can reach (network, fs, native code) — UNKNOWN if the lockfile does not show it.
3. **Pinning & integrity check**: are versions pinned and lockfile hashes present and consistent with the manifest?
4. **Verdict**: merge / merge-after-verification / reject, with the riskiest package named even if merging.
5. **Questions for the author**: why this package, why this version.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every risk row cites diff evidence or an explicit UNKNOWN plus a resolution command.
- No package is condemned on reputation alone; each has a named mechanism.
- The verdict names the single riskiest dependency regardless of outcome.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A package risk table with evidence and verification commands, transitive blast-radius notes, a pinning/integrity check, a verdict naming the riskiest package, and provenance questions.

prompts.title: Performance Pass on an Application Diff
prompts.description: Targeted performance review of a diff: N+1 queries, redundant work, re-render triggers, and unbounded growth — each tied to a realistic trigger condition.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review this diff for performance regressions and newly introduced hot spots in {{component_or_module}}.</goal>
<rationale>This code runs {{runtime_context: e.g. "on every dashboard page load for ~40k daily users"}}; regressions here are user-visible within a day and expensive to diagnose after the fact.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Only flag performance issues with a concrete trigger: name the input size, data volume, or call frequency that makes the code path expensive.
- Do NOT flag theoretical micro-optimizations (e.g. "map vs for loop") unless the path is provably hot.
- Do NOT propose caching, indexes, or batching as fixes without showing the quoted code path that needs them.
- Where cost depends on data you cannot see (row counts, payload sizes), state the assumption explicitly and mark the finding's confidence accordingly.
</boundaries>
</task>

<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<performance_context>
{{data volumes, request rates, latency budget, known slow paths}}
</performance_context>

<output_contract>
1. **Findings table**: | Severity | File:line | Issue | Quoted code | Trigger condition (what makes it slow) | Cost estimate (relative: per-request / per-row / per-render) | Suggested fix | Confidence |
2. **Load-bearing assumptions**: the data-volume or frequency assumptions your findings rest on.
3. **Benchmark request**: if any finding is medium confidence or lower, the minimal measurement that would settle it (endpoint + payload, or query + row count).
4. **Verdict**: ship / ship-after-fixes / block, with the worst realistic regression named even if shipping.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every finding names a concrete trigger condition; "could be slow" without a trigger is not a finding.
- Every suggested fix points at quoted code.
- The verdict names the worst realistic regression regardless of outcome.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A findings table (severity × quoted code × trigger condition × cost estimate × fix × confidence), load-bearing assumptions, minimal benchmark requests, and a verdict naming the worst realistic regression.

prompts.title: Hot-Path Algorithmic & Concurrency Review
prompts.description: Deep review of a performance-critical change: complexity claims, allocation behavior, and concurrency hazards, with each claim checked against quoted code.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Verify or refute the performance and correctness claims of this change to a hot path: {{hot_path_description}}.</goal>
<rationale>This path handles {{load_profile: e.g. "50k events/sec with a 20ms p99 budget"}}; the PR claims {{claimed_improvement}}, and an unverified "optimization" here previously caused a production incident.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Check every complexity or latency claim in the PR description against the actual code; quote the code that proves or breaks the claim.
- Do NOT accept benchmark claims without methodology; if no benchmark is provided, say NOT VERIFIED and specify the minimal benchmark needed.
- Do NOT suggest algorithmic rewrites as a first resort; prefer the smallest change that fixes a confirmed problem.
- Concurrency findings must name the interleaving that breaks (who runs first, what is observed); "race condition possible" without an interleaving is not a finding.
</boundaries>
</task>

<pr_description>{{claims, benchmarks if any}}</pr_description>
<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<load_profile>{{input sizes, concurrency level, allocation sensitivity}}</load_profile>

<output_contract>
1. **Claims verification**: | Claim | VERIFIED / REFUTED / NOT VERIFIED | Evidence (quoted code or missing benchmark) |
2. **Findings table**: | Severity | File:line | Issue (complexity / allocation / lock / interleaving) | Quoted code | Failure interleaving or input size | Fix | Confidence |
3. **Minimal benchmark spec**: the smallest experiment that settles each NOT VERIFIED claim (inputs, metric, pass/fail threshold).
4. **Verdict**: ship / ship-after-benchmark / ship-after-fixes / block, with worst-case behavior under stated load.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every VERIFIED claim has quoted code; every NOT VERIFIED claim has a benchmark spec.
- Every concurrency finding names a concrete interleaving.
- The verdict states worst-case behavior under {{load_profile}} even when shipping.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A claims-verification table (VERIFIED/REFUTED/NOT VERIFIED with evidence), a findings table with concrete interleavings or input sizes, minimal benchmark specs, and a worst-case-stated verdict.

prompts.title: Front-End Performance Quick Pass
prompts.description: Lightweight beginner-friendly check of a UI diff for the common front-end performance mistakes: re-render triggers, bundle growth, and unoptimized assets.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Check this UI change for the common front-end performance mistakes before I merge it.</goal>
<rationale>Our {{page_or_app}} already has a slow-load complaint history; this change touches {{files_or_components}} and I want a fast, focused pass rather than a full audit.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Only look for: unnecessary re-render triggers (new inline objects/functions passed as props, missing memoization on expensive subtrees), new heavy imports or bundle growth, unbounded lists rendered without virtualization, and unoptimized images/assets.
- Do NOT comment on code style or component organization.
- Do NOT flag anything without quoting the code and naming when it actually costs (which render, which load, how often).
- If you are unsure whether something is expensive, include it with confidence "low" and say what measurement would settle it.
</boundaries>
</task>

<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<context>{{framework and version, any performance budget}}</context>

<output_contract>
1. **Findings table**: | Severity (major / minor / info) | File:line | Issue | Quoted code | When it costs (render/load trigger) | Suggested fix | Confidence (high / medium / low) |
2. **Verdict**: 2–3 sentences: fine to ship or not, plus the biggest remaining risk.
3. **Questions for the author**: only if the diff is ambiguous about data size or render frequency.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every finding quotes code and names a concrete cost trigger.
- No findings outside the four listed categories.
- The verdict names at least one residual risk even when approving.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A short findings table limited to re-renders, bundle growth, unbounded lists, and assets — each with quoted code and a cost trigger — plus a 2–3 sentence verdict and optional questions.

prompts.title: Draft Kind, Specific, Actionable Review Comments
prompts.description: Turn raw review findings into inline PR comments that are kind to the author, specific about the code, and unambiguous about the requested action.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Convert my raw review findings into inline PR comments a teammate can act on without a follow-up conversation.</goal>
<rationale>Review comments here either get ignored (too vague) or create defensiveness (too blunt); the team standard is: kind to the person, direct about the code, explicit about the ask.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Each comment must quote or reference the exact code it concerns.
- Each comment must end with a clear ask: a specific change, an explanation, or a question — never a bare complaint.
- Do NOT use absolutes ("always", "never", "obviously") or anything that reads as a judgment of the author.
- Do NOT soften a blocker into sounding optional; required changes say "required" and why.
- Do NOT add praise padding; one sentence of genuine context is fine, filler is not.
</boundaries>
</task>

<raw_findings>
{{your rough notes / findings, e.g. "the retry loop in worker.ts has no backoff, will hammer the API"}}
</raw_findings>
<diff_context>
{{the diff or the relevant snippets the findings refer to}}
</diff_context>

<output_contract>
For each finding, one comment in this shape:
- **File:line** + quoted code
- **Comment body** (2–5 sentences): what the code does, why it is a problem in this context, the concrete ask
- **Severity label**: blocking / suggestion / question — with "blocking" used only for merge-gating issues
Then a one-paragraph **review summary** for the top of the PR: overall verdict, the 1–2 things that must change, and anything genuinely worth acknowledging.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every comment quotes code and ends with an explicit ask.
- No comment contains an absolute or an author-directed judgment.
- Blocking labels are reserved for merge-gating issues only.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: One comment per finding (file:line + quoted code + 2–5 sentence body ending in a concrete ask + blocking/suggestion/question label) plus a one-paragraph PR summary with verdict and must-changes.

prompts.title: Review Response: Answering Author Pushback
prompts.description: Draft responses when an author pushes back on review comments — resolving each thread with evidence, conceding where the author is right, and holding where they are not.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Draft my responses to the author's replies on this PR review, resolving each thread honestly: concede where the author's evidence is better, hold position where mine is.</goal>
<rationale>Review threads here either die unresolved or escalate into opinion wars; the goal is convergence on evidence — the code and its behavior — not on seniority or stubbornness.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Re-ground every response in the quoted code or the author's quoted counter-evidence; no appeal to preference or authority.
- If the author is right, say so plainly and withdraw the comment — do NOT hedge a concession.
- If you still disagree, state the specific behavior or input that demonstrates the problem, and propose the smallest change or test that would settle it.
- Do NOT restate the original comment in new words; each response must move the thread forward.
- Mark any thread that genuinely needs a third party or an offline decision instead of a reply.
</boundaries>
</task>

<original_comments>{{my review comments, verbatim}}</original_comments>
<author_replies>{{the author's replies, verbatim}}</author_replies>
<diff>{{the relevant code}}</diff>

<output_contract>
Per thread: | Thread | My position now (hold / concede / needs-evidence) | Draft reply (2–5 sentences, quoting code) | Proposed resolution (specific change, test, or offline decision) |
Then: **Open items** — threads still unresolved and what exactly unblocks each.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every draft reply quotes code or the author's evidence.
- Concessions are explicit, not hedged.
- Every unresolved thread names its concrete unblocking condition.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A per-thread table (position: hold/concede/needs-evidence, draft reply quoting code, proposed resolution) plus an open-items list with concrete unblocking conditions.

prompts.title: Pre-Submit Self-Review Checklist
prompts.description: Run before requesting review: verify the diff against its intent, check the checklist with evidence, and surface your own known weaknesses honestly.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Self-review my change before I request review: verify it does what I claim, catch what I have become blind to, and write the honest risk statement my reviewer deserves.</goal>
<rationale>Authors are the worst reviewers of their own diffs — intent blindness hides exactly the bugs a fresh reader sees. I want a forced evidence pass, not a reassurance pass.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Verify claims against the actual diff and command outputs, not against what I intended to write.
- Do NOT rubber-stamp: if any check cannot be verified, mark it NOT VERIFIED — never assume pass.
- Do NOT fix anything in this pass; report only.
- Do NOT review style or anything a linter already enforces.
</boundaries>
</task>

<intent>{{what this change is supposed to do, in your own words}}</intent>
<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<verification_outputs>{{test run output, build output, manual check notes — verbatim, or "not run"}}</verification_outputs>

<output_contract>
1. **Intent check**: does the diff actually implement the stated intent? Quote the code that does — or name what is missing.
2. **Checklist report**: | Check | PASS / FAIL / NOT VERIFIED | Evidence (verbatim output or quoted code) |
   - build/lint pass; tests pass; tests cover the changed behavior (quote the test); no debug leftovers (`console.log`, `TODO`, commented-out code — quote any found); no unintended files in the diff; migration/config/env changes documented.
3. **Self-identified risks**: the 1–3 things you are least sure about, stated plainly.
4. **Suggested PR description**: 3–5 sentences a reviewer can act on: what, why, how verified, what to scrutinize.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- No PASS without pasted evidence; every gap is explicitly NOT VERIFIED.
- Risks section is non-empty and specific.
- The PR description names what the reviewer should scrutinize.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: An intent check with quoted code, an evidence-backed checklist table (PASS/FAIL/NOT VERIFIED), 1–3 plainly stated self-identified risks, and a ready-to-paste PR description.

prompts.title: Fresh-Context Verifier for a Completed Change
prompts.description: Instructions for a fresh-context verification pass: assume the change is broken, check every spec requirement against the diff, and demand quoted evidence for every verdict.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Independently verify a completed change against its plan. Assume the change is broken until the diff proves otherwise.</goal>
<rationale>The implementer (human or AI) cannot see its own blind spots; this review runs with fresh context — the spec and the diff only — precisely so that intent, conversation history, and sunk effort cannot soften the verdict.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- You have ONLY the spec and the diff below. Do NOT assume any code, conversation, or intent beyond them.
- Every verdict requires evidence: quote the implementing code for COVERED; name the absent code for MISSING.
- Do NOT trust claims in commit messages or comments — verify against executable code only.
- If the spec is ambiguous on a point, flag the ambiguity as its own finding instead of guessing the intent.
- Do NOT fix anything; report only.
</boundaries>
</task>

<spec>
{{the plan / SPEC.md / ticket the change was built from, verbatim}}
</spec>
<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>

<output_contract>
1. **Coverage matrix**: | Requirement (quoted from spec) | COVERED / PARTIAL / MISSING | Evidence (quoted code, or what is absent) |
2. **Out-of-scope changes**: anything in the diff serving no spec requirement, quoted.
3. **Ambiguities**: spec points that admit two readings, and which reading the diff chose.
4. **Broken-assumption check**: spec invariants ("must preserve" items) — each PRESERVED / VIOLATED / UNKNOWN with evidence.
5. **Verdict**: verified / verified-with-gaps / not-verified, plus the top gap to fix first.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every COVERED verdict quotes implementing code; no bare assertions.
- Any MISSING requirement appears in the verdict's gap list.
- Out-of-scope and ambiguity sections are present even if empty (state "none").
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A spec-coverage matrix with quoted evidence, out-of-scope changes list, spec ambiguities, a per-invariant PRESERVED/VIOLATED/UNKNOWN check, and a verified/not-verified verdict with top gap.

prompts.title: Adversarial Self-Audit of Your Own Diff
prompts.description: Advanced pre-submit ritual: switch from author to hostile reviewer of your own change, hunt the three most likely defect classes, and produce an honest ship/no-ship audit.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit my own change as a hostile reviewer who wants it rejected. Find the defects I motivatedly stopped looking for, then give me an honest ship/no-ship recommendation.</goal>
<rationale>Author optimism is the strongest predictor of escaped defects; the only reliable counter is to explicitly invert my role and incentives before requesting review. This change ships to {{environment}} and the cost of a defect there is {{cost_of_failure}}.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Adopt the assumption that the diff contains at least one real defect, and hunt until you find it or can say exactly where you looked and found none.
- Do NOT pad the report with style nits or hypothetical best practices; only defects with a failure scenario.
- Do NOT soften findings because "you" wrote the code — address the author in the third person.
- Where a defect depends on code outside the diff, state the exact assumption and mark confidence accordingly; UNKNOWN is an acceptable conclusion, guessing is not.
</boundaries>
</task>

<intent>{{what the change is supposed to do}}</intent>
<diff>
{{paste_full_diff_here}}
</diff>
<change_context>{{what was hard, what was rushed, what was copied, what you skipped testing}}</change_context>

<output_contract>
1. **Hunt log**: the 3 most likely defect classes for this change (edge cases at boundaries, error paths, integration/ordering) — for each: where you looked (quoted code) and what you found or ruled out.
2. **Defects table**: | Severity | File:line | Defect | Quoted code | Failure scenario (concrete input or sequence) | Suggested fix | Confidence |
3. **Untested surface**: behaviors the diff changes that no shown test covers.
4. **Ship recommendation**: ship / fix-first / get-a-second-reviewer, with the honest reason — including "I cannot verify X" where true.
</output_contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- The hunt log covers all three defect classes with quoted code.
- Every defect has a concrete failure scenario, not a category name.
- The recommendation is consistent with the findings and names any unverifiable assumption.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A three-class hunt log with quoted code, a defects table with concrete failure scenarios, an untested-surface list, and a ship/fix-first/second-reviewer recommendation naming unverifiable assumptions.

prompts.title: Normalize a relational schema from a feature brief
prompts.description: Turn a plain-language entity/relationship brief into runnable 3NF DDL with per-table rationale and a rollback script.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Design a normalized relational schema (3NF) for {{application_domain}} covering exactly these entities and relationships: {{entity_list_and_relationships}}. Target: {{db_engine}} version {{db_version}}.</goal>
<rationale>A correct normalized schema up front prevents update anomalies and expensive re-migrations once production data exists.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT add entities, columns, or features beyond the brief. If the brief is ambiguous, list each ambiguity under "Assumptions" with the choice you made.
- Do NOT denormalize "for performance"; flag any candidate under "Future optimizations" instead.
- Use only standard DDL valid for the stated engine and version; no invented syntax, no extensions you cannot name.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. CREATE TABLE statements (primary keys, foreign keys, NOT NULL, CHECK constraints) runnable as-is on the stated version.
2. Per-table rationale: which normal form each table satisfies and why each non-key column belongs there.
3. A rollback script (DROP TABLE statements in correct dependency order).
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every many-to-many relationship has a junction table with a composite primary key.
- Every foreign key names its ON DELETE behavior explicitly, with a one-line justification.
- No repeating groups or comma-separated values in any column.
- The rollback script is a valid inverse of the DDL.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Runnable CREATE TABLE DDL for the stated engine/version, per-table normal-form rationale, assumptions list, and a dependency-ordered DROP TABLE rollback script.

prompts.title: Audit an existing schema for normalization violations
prompts.description: Evidence-backed audit of existing DDL for 1NF/2NF/3NF violations, with two correction options, tradeoffs, and migration plus rollback DDL.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit the provided schema DDL for normalization violations and design correction options that lose no data and keep the listed query patterns working.</goal>
<rationale>Update, insert, and delete anomalies in this schema are causing {{observed_symptom}}; fixing the root design beats patching symptoms in application code.</rationale>
<schema>{{existing_ddl}}</schema>
<workload>{{critical_queries_and_access_patterns}}</workload>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT propose renaming public-facing columns unless you also provide the compatibility view.
- Do NOT claim a violation without quoting the exact tables and columns involved.
- If the workload genuinely justifies keeping a violation, say so explicitly instead of forcing 3NF.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Violation table: | Object | Violated form (1NF/2NF/3NF) | Evidence (quoted DDL) | Anomaly it enables |
2. Two correction options (full normalization vs. targeted fix) with pros, cons, and how each fails.
3. Migration DDL for your recommended option plus a rollback script restoring the original structure.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every violation row quotes the implicated DDL verbatim.
- Both options preserve every query in the workload list, or explicitly name the query they break.
- The recommendation states the single criterion that decided it.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Violation table with verbatim DDL evidence, two-option comparison with failure modes, recommended migration DDL, and rollback script.

prompts.title: Deliberate denormalization decision review
prompts.description: Options-and-tradeoffs decision on whether/how to denormalize a hot read path, with weighted decision matrix, DDL, and rollback.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Decide whether and how to denormalize {{hot_read_path}} in our {{db_engine}} schema, given the workload and consistency requirements below.</goal>
<rationale>Denormalization trades write complexity and staleness risk for read latency; done casually it becomes an unmaintainable shadow schema.</rationale>
<context>
Current schema: {{relevant_ddl}}
Workload: {{read_write_ratios_qps_latency_targets}}
Consistency tolerance: {{how_stale_can_reads_be}}
</context>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT assume traffic numbers I did not give; flag every assumed volume as ASSUMPTION with a sensitivity note.
- Do NOT propose caching layers as a substitute for the schema decision; treat them as a separate option only.
- Stay within {{db_engine}} {{version}} features you can name precisely (e.g., materialized views, generated columns, triggers); no invented behavior.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
Enumerate 3 viable approaches (stay normalized and optimize reads / controlled denormalization via trigger or generated column / materialized view or read model). For each: pros, cons, and how it fails under write contention. Then a decision matrix weighted by {{criteria}}. End with one recommendation, the criterion that decided it, plus the DDL for the recommended design and its rollback. Push back if my constraints point elsewhere.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each approach states how writes stay consistent, or its staleness bound.
- DDL is valid for the stated engine version; no invented syntax.
- The decision matrix scores every option on every stated criterion.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Three-approach comparison with pros/cons/failure modes, weighted decision matrix, single recommendation with deciding criterion, valid DDL, and rollback.

prompts.title: Read and explain an EXPLAIN plan
prompts.description: Node-by-node reading of a pasted EXPLAIN plan that identifies the dominant cost driver without inventing planner behavior.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Explain what this query plan is doing and identify the most expensive step, so I can decide whether an index or a rewrite is warranted.</goal>
<rationale>I need to read plans reliably before I start changing queries or indexes.</rationale>
<environment>{{db_engine_and_exact_version}}</environment>
<query>{{sql_query}}</query>
<plan>{{verbatim_explain_output}}</plan>
<boundaries>
- Ground every claim in the pasted plan; cite the node (e.g., "Seq Scan on orders, rows=...") it comes from.
- Do NOT invent planner behavior not visible in the plan. If something cannot be determined from the output, say "cannot be determined from this plan" and name the extra output (e.g., EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on PostgreSQL, EXPLAIN ANALYZE on MySQL 8.0.18+) that would settle it.
- Do NOT recommend schema or index changes in this pass; diagnosis only.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Diagnosis table: | Plan node | What it does | Rows est. vs actual (if present) | Cost share | Concern? |
2. The single dominant cost driver in one sentence, with the plan line that proves it.
3. Up to 3 follow-up measurements that would sharpen the diagnosis.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every table row cites text present in the pasted plan.
- Estimated-vs-actual comparison appears only if the plan is an ANALYZE plan; otherwise it is explicitly marked unavailable.
- No claim exceeds what the plan evidence supports.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Plan-node diagnosis table quoting the pasted plan, one-sentence dominant cost driver with proving line, and follow-up measurement suggestions.

prompts.title: Optimize a slow query from EXPLAIN ANALYZE evidence
prompts.description: Ground slow-query optimization in pasted EXPLAIN ANALYZE output: diagnosis table, semantics-preserving rewrites, index DDL, and a before/after verification plan.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Reduce the execution time of the query below on {{db_engine}} {{version}} without changing its result set.</goal>
<rationale>This query runs {{frequency}} and currently takes {{observed_latency}}, violating {{slo_or_user_impact}}.</rationale>
<evidence>
Query: {{sql_query}}
Schema (relevant tables and existing indexes): {{ddl_and_existing_indexes}}
Plan: {{verbatim_explain_analyze_output}}
Approximate table sizes: {{row_counts}}
</evidence>
<boundaries>
- Ground every diagnosis in the pasted plan; quote the node that motivates each change. No invented planner behavior.
- Flag any recommendation whose benefit depends on data volume or distribution I have not provided as ASSUMPTION.
- Do NOT change query semantics: same rows, same order, same aggregates. State how you verified equivalence for each rewrite.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Diagnosis table: | Finding | Plan evidence (quoted) | Why it is slow |
2. Up to 2 query rewrites AND index recommendations (CREATE INDEX DDL valid for the stated engine/version), each with expected effect tied to a plan node plus its write and storage cost.
3. Verification plan: the exact EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) or EXPLAIN ANALYZE commands to run before and after, and the metric that proves improvement.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each recommendation maps to at least one quoted plan node.
- Index DDL notes concurrency-safe creation where the engine supports it (e.g., CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on PostgreSQL).
- Result-set equivalence is argued for every rewrite.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Evidence-quoted diagnosis table, semantics-preserving rewrites plus valid CREATE INDEX DDL with write-cost notes, and an exact before/after verification command plan.

prompts.title: Root-cause a query plan regression
prompts.description: Compare before/after plans, rank regression hypotheses by evidence strength with verification commands, and stage minimal remediations.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Root-cause a query plan regression: this query ran in {{before_latency}} and now takes {{after_latency}} on {{db_engine}} {{version}}.</goal>
<rationale>Something changed — statistics, data growth, an upgrade, a config value — and guessing wastes more time than measuring.</rationale>
<evidence>
Query: {{sql_query}}
Current plan: {{verbatim_current_explain_analyze}}
Prior plan (if available): {{verbatim_prior_plan_or_NOT_AVAILABLE}}
Recent changes I know of: {{upgrades_config_changes_deploys}}
</evidence>
<boundaries>
- Rank hypotheses by evidence strength; label each CONFIRMED-BY (quoted evidence), PLAUSIBLE, or SPECULATION.
- Do NOT assert a cause the provided evidence cannot support; name the diagnostic command that would confirm or kill each open hypothesis.
- Recommend configuration changes only with behavior you can state precisely for this engine/version; no invented planner knobs.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Plan-diff summary: the node(s) where the plans diverge, quoted from both plans (or state the prior plan is unavailable and what that costs the analysis).
2. Ranked hypothesis table: | Hypothesis | Status | Evidence / missing check | Verification command |
3. Minimal-remediation options, smallest first (statistics refresh, index, rewrite, config), each with tradeoffs and a rollback note.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every verification command is runnable on {{db_engine}} {{version}} (e.g., pg_stat_statements queries, ANALYZE, SHOW).
- At least one open hypothesis is testable with a command you list.
- Remediation #1 is the smallest change consistent with the evidence.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Quoted plan-diff summary, ranked hypothesis table with per-hypothesis verification commands, and staged minimal remediations with rollback notes.

prompts.title: Write a guarded migration with rollback
prompts.description: Produce a production-safe forward migration with per-operation lock annotations and guards, a true rollback, and a pre-flight checklist.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Produce a production-safe migration for {{change_description}} on {{db_engine}} {{version}}, managed with {{orm_or_tool}} (e.g., Alembic, Prisma, Drizzle, or raw SQL).</goal>
<rationale>This table holds ~{{row_count}} rows and serves live traffic; a naive migration will lock it or fail halfway.</rationale>
<schema>{{current_ddl}}</schema>
<boundaries>
- No destructive operations (DROP, type narrowing, NOT NULL without a default path) without an explicit guard: a pre-check query, lock_timeout / statement_timeout where the engine supports them, and a stated abort condition.
- Do NOT rely on ORM autogenerate output unexamined; write or annotate the operations yourself and note where autogenerate would get it wrong.
- One migration = one logical change. If the change needs multiple steps, say so and split it.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Forward migration in {{orm_or_tool}} format, each risky operation annotated: lock acquired, expected duration driver, and its guard.
2. Rollback migration restoring the prior schema; state explicitly if any step is irreversible and why.
3. Pre-flight checklist: queries to run before applying (row counts, active queries, lock contention, replication lag) with pass/fail thresholds.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Forward and rollback are syntactically valid for the stated tool and engine version.
- Every blocking operation names the lock it takes.
- A constraint added as NOT VALID is followed by a separate VALIDATE CONSTRAINT step where the engine supports it.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Annotated forward migration with lock/duration notes and guards, rollback migration with irreversibility statements, and a pre-flight checklist with thresholds.

prompts.title: Review an ORM-generated migration for production safety
prompts.description: Audit a Prisma/Drizzle/Alembic autogenerated migration operation-by-operation, rewrite only the unsafe rows with guards, and provide rollback.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review this ORM-generated migration for production safety and rewrite the unsafe parts before it ships.</goal>
<rationale>Autogenerated migrations (Prisma migrate, drizzle-kit, Alembic autogenerate) optimize for matching the schema diff, not for lock behavior or data preservation on a live table.</rationale>
<context>
Tool and version: {{tool_and_version}}
Engine and version: {{db_engine_version}}
Generated migration: {{migration_file_contents}}
Table sizes / traffic: {{row_counts_and_qps}}
</context>
<boundaries>
- Evaluate against the stated tool and engine versions only; verify whether each operation is online or blocking for those versions, not folklore.
- Do NOT rewrite operations that are already safe; annotate them SAFE with the reason.
- If you find issues outside the migration (schema design, missing indexes), list them under "Notes" but do NOT fix them.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Safety table: | Operation | Lock/blocking behavior on this version | Data-loss risk | Verdict: SAFE / REWRITE |
2. Rewritten migration containing only the REWRITE rows, with guards in place (timeouts, NOT VALID plus a separate validate step, batched backfills).
3. Rollback for the rewritten operations.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every generated operation appears exactly once in the safety table.
- No DROP or column retype ships without an explicit data-preservation argument.
- The rewritten migration is valid output for the stated tool and version.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Per-operation safety table with SAFE/REWRITE verdicts, a rewritten migration containing only the unsafe operations with guards, rollback, and a Notes section for out-of-scope finds.

prompts.title: Zero-downtime expand-contract migration plan
prompts.description: Multi-phase expand/backfill/switch/contract plan where every phase is safe with old and new app versions running, with per-phase guards, verification queries, and progress tracking.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Design a zero-downtime, multi-phase migration to {{change_description}} on {{db_engine}} {{version}} for a table with ~{{row_count}} rows serving {{qps}}.</goal>
<rationale>Deploys and schema changes must be independently safe: old and new application versions will run concurrently during rollout.</rationale>
<schema>{{current_ddl}}</schema>
<deploy_context>{{deployment_style_and_replication_setup}}</deploy_context>
<boundaries>
- Every phase must be safe with BOTH the old and new app version running; state the compatibility argument per phase.
- Index builds on large tables must use the concurrent/online options the stated engine version supports (e.g., CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on PostgreSQL, ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE where valid on MySQL); name the limitations (no transaction block, invalid-index cleanup).
- Backfills must be batched and throttled; specify batch-size reasoning and lock/IO impact. Do NOT invent engine behavior — flag anything uncertain as VERIFY.
- No destructive (contract) phase ships without a stated waiting condition.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Phase plan: | Phase | DDL/app change | Compatibility argument | Guard/abort condition | Rollback | covering expand, backfill, dual-write or read switch, and contract.
2. All migration DDL/scripts per phase, valid for the stated engine version.
3. Per-phase verification queries (replication lag, invalid indexes, constraint state) with pass/fail thresholds.
4. A state-tracking note format (phase, applied-at, verified-by-query) suitable for a MIGRATION_PROGRESS.md file.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- No phase leaves the system inconsistent if abandoned mid-way; each phase names its abort path.
- The contract phase is gated on an explicit condition, not "when convenient".
- Every locking/online-behavior claim is scoped to the stated engine and version.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Phase plan table (expand/backfill/switch/contract) with compatibility arguments and abort conditions, per-phase valid DDL, verification queries with thresholds, and a progress-file format.

prompts.title: Choose an index set for a query workload
prompts.description: Recommend justified indexes for a stated query workload: per-query mapping, column-order rationale, valid DDL, and a write-amplification tradeoff summary.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Recommend an index set for the query workload below on {{db_engine}} {{version}}.</goal>
<rationale>The workload runs against tables of ~{{row_counts}}; missing indexes cause {{observed_symptom}}, but every extra index also taxes writes.</rationale>
<workload>{{top_queries_with_frequency}}</workload>
<schema>{{table_ddl_and_existing_indexes}}</schema>
<boundaries>
- Recommend only index types the stated engine/version supports; default to B-tree and justify anything else.
- For each index, name the query it serves; an index serving no listed query must be argued separately or omitted.
- Do NOT claim an index will be used without stating the predicate/selectivity reasoning; flag selectivity as ASSUMPTION when data distribution is unknown.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Recommendation table: | Index (columns, order, type) | Serves query | Why this column order | Write cost |
2. CREATE INDEX DDL valid for {{db_engine}} {{version}}.
3. Tradeoff summary: total write amplification added, and which candidate index you deliberately excluded and why.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every listed query maps to at least one index, or to an explicit "sequential scan is fine because ..." note.
- Column-order rationale references equality-versus-range predicate placement.
- New index names do not collide with the existing indexes listed in the schema.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Recommendation table mapping indexes to queries with column-order rationale and write cost, valid CREATE INDEX DDL, and a tradeoff summary including a deliberately excluded candidate.

prompts.title: Audit indexes for unused and redundant entries
prompts.description: Evidence-gated index audit from live usage statistics: KEEP/DROP/MERGE verdicts with caveats, staged consolidation DDL, rollback, and a re-verification plan.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit the existing indexes on {{db_engine}} {{version}} using the statistics below: find unused, redundant, and overlapping indexes and propose a safe consolidation.</goal>
<rationale>Indexes consume write throughput and storage; dead indexes are pure cost, but dropping a used one causes an outage.</rationale>
<evidence>
Index usage statistics: {{pg_stat_user_indexes_or_equivalent_output}}
Index definitions and sizes: {{index_ddl_and_sizes}}
Query workload (if available): {{workload_or_NOT_AVAILABLE}}
</evidence>
<boundaries>
- Every DROP recommendation must cite the statistics evidence (e.g., idx_scan = 0) AND the caveats: stats reset time, replicas with different workloads, infrequent-but-critical jobs. If the stats observation window is unknown, mark the verdict NEEDS-VERIFICATION instead of DROP.
- Do NOT call two indexes redundant without comparing columns, column order, partial-index predicates, and included columns.
- Use only fields present in the pasted output; no invented catalog fields.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Audit table: | Index | Size | Scans | Verdict: KEEP / DROP / MERGE-INTO / NEEDS-VERIFICATION | Evidence + caveat |
2. Consolidation DDL in a safe order (replacement created before the original is dropped where applicable), plus rollback DDL.
3. Verification plan: the statistics query to rerun after {{observation_window}} to confirm each decision.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every verdict quotes at least one statistic from the pasted output.
- Each DROP is staged: observation window and rollback are stated.
- Total reclaimable storage is summed from the pasted sizes.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Audit table with KEEP/DROP/MERGE/NEEDS-VERIFICATION verdicts quoting statistics, staged consolidation DDL with rollback, and a re-verification statistics query plan.

prompts.title: Design composite, partial, and covering indexes for hot queries
prompts.description: Advanced index design grounded in pasted plans: composite vs single tradeoffs, partial-index predicate justification, covering-index heap-fetch argument, and measurable before/after verification.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Design an advanced indexing strategy for the hot queries below on {{db_engine}} {{version}}, using composite, partial, and covering indexes where they genuinely pay off.</goal>
<rationale>These queries dominate {{endpoint_or_job}} latency; naive single-column indexes have already failed to help (see plans).</rationale>
<evidence>
Queries with frequency: {{queries}}
Current plans: {{verbatim_explain_outputs}}
Table sizes and write rates: {{sizes_and_write_qps}}
Existing indexes: {{ddl}}
</evidence>
<boundaries>
- Ground each design choice in the pasted plans: quote the node each index removes or improves. No invented planner behavior.
- Justify any partial index with its exact predicate and row selectivity; flag selectivity as ASSUMPTION if not evidenced.
- Justify covering indexes (INCLUDE on PostgreSQL) with the columns the plan shows being fetched from the heap.
- Respect the write budget: total added write amplification must be quantified and compared against {{write_budget}}.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Design table: | Query | Proposed index (type, columns, predicate, INCLUDE) | Plan node it fixes | Write cost |
2. Alternatives considered per query (e.g., one composite vs. two single-column indexes) with the tradeoff that decided it.
3. DDL valid for the stated version, created concurrently/online where the engine supports it.
4. Before/after verification: exact EXPLAIN commands and the plan property (node removed, buffers reduced) that proves each index works.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every index maps to a quoted plan node.
- No duplicate or overlapping indexes versus the existing set; overlaps are explicitly resolved.
- Verification names a measurable plan change, not "should be faster".
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Design table tying each composite/partial/covering index to a quoted plan node, per-query alternatives with deciding tradeoffs, concurrent-safe DDL, and measurable verification plan.

prompts.title: Design a transaction boundary for a multi-write operation
prompts.description: Design transaction scope, weakest-safe isolation level, locking reads, and bounded retry handling for a multi-write operation in a stated ORM and engine.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Design the transaction boundary and concurrency control for {{operation_description}} in {{orm}} over {{db_engine}} {{version}}.</goal>
<rationale>{{operation_description}} writes to multiple rows/tables; partial completion or concurrent interleaving causes {{failure_scenario}}.</rationale>
<context>
Relevant schema: {{ddl}}
Concurrency profile: {{expected_concurrent_actors_and_contention}}
Current code (if any): {{code_or_NONE}}
</context>
<boundaries>
- Choose the weakest isolation level that prevents the stated anomaly; justify which phenomena (dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, lost update, write skew) matter here and why the chosen level covers them.
- Use only transaction features of the stated engine and ORM versions (e.g., SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, advisory locks, unique constraints); name the exact API. No invented syntax.
- Include retry handling for serialization failures and deadlocks; do NOT assume retries are free — bound attempts and backoff.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Boundary design: what is inside the transaction, what stays out, and why (lock duration versus consistency).
2. Implementation sketch in {{orm}} for the stated version: isolation level, locking reads, unique-constraint reliance, and the retry loop with engine-specific error-code handling.
3. Failure-mode table: | Interleaving/failure | Prevented by | Residual risk |
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every anomaly named in the rationale maps to a mechanism in the design.
- Retry handling names the engine's actual error codes (e.g., PostgreSQL 40001/40P01) explicitly.
- Nothing outside the transaction can leave state inconsistent if the process dies between writes.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Transaction boundary design with in/out justification, ORM implementation sketch with named error codes and bounded retries, and a failure-mode table with residual risks.

prompts.title: Diagnose deadlocks from verbatim logs
prompts.description: Reconstruct the lock cycle strictly from pasted deadlock logs, state the root-cause ordering problem, and stage smallest-first fixes that break the cycle.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Diagnose the deadlock/lock-timeout events below and propose the smallest changes that eliminate them.</goal>
<rationale>Deadlocks on {{db_engine}} {{version}} are killing {{affected_operation}} at {{frequency}}; retries mask but do not fix the ordering problem.</rationale>
<evidence>
Verbatim log/error output: {{deadlock_log_excerpt}}
Statements involved: {{sql_statements}}
Schema and indexes: {{relevant_ddl}}
</evidence>
<boundaries>
- Reconstruct the lock cycle strictly from the pasted log: which transaction held which lock and waited on which. Quote the log lines for each edge of the cycle.
- Do NOT propose rewrites of statements not implicated by the log. If the log is insufficient, name the exact logging setting to enable for better evidence next time (e.g., PostgreSQL log_lock_waits with deadlock_timeout, or MySQL innodb_print_all_deadlocks).
- Prefer ordering and consistency fixes (consistent lock-acquisition order, shorter transactions, indexes that reduce locked rows) over escalating isolation or heavier locking.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Lock-cycle reconstruction: | Transaction | Holds | Waits for | Log evidence (quoted) |
2. Root cause in one paragraph: the ordering or access pattern that makes the cycle possible.
3. Fix options, smallest first (index to reduce locked rows, statement reordering, lock-ordering convention, bounded retry policy), each with tradeoffs and the evidence that it breaks the cycle.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every edge of the cycle is backed by a quoted log line.
- At least one fix requires no application changes beyond the implicated code path.
- If a retry policy is recommended, it names the engine's deadlock error code and bounded attempts.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Lock-cycle table with quoted log evidence per edge, one-paragraph root cause, and smallest-first fix options with cycle-breaking evidence and bounded retry guidance.

prompts.title: Choose the weakest safe isolation level for a critical operation
