3. Acceptance criteria per story — mechanically checkable ('GET /orders returns 403 for non-owners', never 'secure and fast'); cover success, empty, error, and permission states
4. Non-goals (binding)
5. Constraints & dependencies
6. Open questions — each marked OPEN with an owner and the decision it blocks
7. Out of scope — what a reader might assume is included but is not

BOUNDARIES:
- Do NOT invent requirements, metrics, or user research — mark gaps OPEN.
- Do NOT design the solution here; requirements describe WHAT and WHY — interfaces belong in the design doc.
- Do NOT state success metrics without a measurement source.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: every story has at least one checkable criterion per state class; every ambiguity is answered or OPEN; no solution design has leaked into the document.
prompts.expectedOutput: A requirements document with an evidence-linked problem statement, prioritized user stories, state-covering checkable acceptance criteria, binding non-goals, and an OPEN-questions register with owners.

prompts.title: First GitHub Actions CI Pipeline (Lint + Test Gate)
prompts.description: Scaffolds a minimal, fast, secrets-free GitHub Actions CI workflow for a new project, with pinned actions, caching, and a failure-mode table so developers know where each breakage surfaces.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Create a GitHub Actions CI workflow for my {{language_and_framework}} application at {{repo_path}} that runs on every pull request and every push to {{default_branch}}, executing dependency install, lint, typecheck, and tests.</goal>
<rationale>We currently merge without automated checks and broken builds reach {{default_branch}} roughly {{incident_frequency}}. A minimal, fast pipeline is the first quality gate.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT add deployment, release, or notification jobs — CI only.
- Do NOT add new application dependencies or modify application code.
- Use actions/checkout@v4 and the official setup action for {{language_and_framework}} with dependency caching enabled.
- Pin every third-party action to an exact version tag or full-length commit SHA — never @main or @latest.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — complete, valid workflow YAML.
2. Stage rationale: one line per job explaining why it exists and what its failure blocks.
3. Failure-mode table: | Failure | Where caught | Signal to developer |, covering at least dependency install failure, lint failure, test failure, and runner flakiness.
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Workflow triggers on pull_request and push to {{default_branch}} only.
- Expected total runtime under {{runtime_budget_minutes}} minutes; tests run in a separate job from lint so failures localize.
- No secrets, tokens, or credentials anywhere in the file.
- YAML would pass `actionlint`; if you cannot run it, mark NOT VERIFIED and name the validation command.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

Use only current GitHub Actions syntax. If {{language_and_framework}} has no standard setup action, say so and use a plain run step instead of inventing one.
prompts.expectedOutput: A complete ci.yml workflow file, per-job stage rationale, and a failure-mode table; actionlint validity stated or marked NOT VERIFIED.

prompts.title: CI Pipeline Optimization: Caching, Scanning, OIDC Deploy Auth
prompts.description: Optimizes an existing GitHub Actions workflow for speed and security: dependency caching, parallel vulnerability scanning, and replacing long-lived cloud credentials with OIDC federation — without renaming branch-protection checks.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Optimize our existing GitHub Actions workflow: cut median runtime from {{current_runtime}} to under {{target_runtime}}, add dependency vulnerability scanning, and replace long-lived cloud credentials with OIDC federation for the deploy job.</goal>
<rationale>Slow CI delays every merge, and stored cloud secrets are our largest credential-leak exposure. Both problems compound as the team grows.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT change application source code or test logic.
- Do NOT remove existing jobs; you may parallelize, cache, or re-order them.
- Preserve the job names that branch protection requires, or explicitly list every rename so we can update branch rules.
- Flag any paid third-party action in a 'Cost notes' section before using it.
</boundaries>
</task>

<current_workflow>
{{current_workflow_yaml_verbatim}}
</current_workflow>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. Revised workflow YAML (full file, ready to commit).
2. Change summary table: | Change | Expected saving/benefit | Risk |.
3. OIDC setup notes: the trust-policy condition keys required for {{cloud_provider}} (e.g. token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub and :aud for AWS).
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Caching uses setup-action integrated caching or actions/cache with key plus restore-keys.
- {{scanner_tool}} runs in parallel with tests and fails the build only on severity {{severity_threshold}} or higher.
- Deploy job declares permissions: id-token: write; no AWS_/GCP_/AZURE_ secret env literals remain.
- Matrix strategy, if introduced, is justified in the change summary; otherwise omit it.
- Any claimed speedup that is not measured is labeled ESTIMATE.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Revised workflow YAML, a change/benefit/risk table, OIDC trust-policy notes, and clearly labeled ESTIMATE vs measured speedups.

prompts.title: CI Failure Triage from Verbatim Logs
prompts.description: Root-causes a red CI job using the verbatim job log and pipeline config, separating root cause from downstream symptoms and returning the smallest fix — never a blind retry or rewrite.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Diagnose the failing CI job below and produce the smallest fix that makes the pipeline green.</goal>
<rationale>{{pipeline_name}} has been red for {{duration}} and is blocking {{blocked_work}}. We need a root cause, not another retry.</rationale>
<environment>
- CI system: {{ci_system_and_version}}
- Runner image: {{runner_image}}
- Key tool versions: {{tool_versions}}
</environment>
<evidence>
Failing job log (verbatim, unedited):
{{verbatim_job_log}}

Pipeline config (verbatim):
{{pipeline_config}}

Last known-good commit: {{last_green_commit}}
</evidence>
</task>

<rules>
- Localize the root cause first; explicitly distinguish it from downstream symptoms in the log.
- Do NOT propose 're-run the job' or cache-clearing as the fix unless you explain the mechanism that makes it corrective.
- Do NOT rewrite the pipeline config beyond the minimal change.
- If the log implicates a package or API, state which installed version to verify (e.g. npm ls {{package}}, pip show {{package}}) before recommending a pin or upgrade.
- If the evidence is insufficient to isolate the cause, list the exact commands/output needed instead of guessing.
</rules>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Root cause (one paragraph) with the specific log lines quoted as evidence.
2. Minimal fix as a diff or exact file edit.
3. Verification command(s) to confirm the fix locally or in CI.
4. Detection note: one line on how to catch this failure class earlier.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every claim about the failure cites quoted log output; anything not present in the evidence is marked NOT VERIFIED.
- The fix touches no files outside {{in_scope_paths}}.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Root cause with quoted log evidence, a minimal diff, verification commands, and explicit NOT VERIFIED markers for unsupported claims.

prompts.title: Multi-Stage Production Dockerfile with BuildKit
prompts.description: Generates a lean, non-root, multi-stage Dockerfile plus .dockerignore for a given stack, with pinned base images, layer-cache ordering, and BuildKit build/verify commands.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Write a production Dockerfile for my {{language_and_framework}} application ({{app_description}}) using multi-stage builds and BuildKit features.</goal>
<rationale>Our current image is {{current_image_size}} and ships build tooling to production; we need a smaller, reproducible runtime image for {{deployment_target}}.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT use :latest or untagged base images — pin exact version tags and note where a digest pin would go.
- Do NOT run the application as root; create and switch to a non-root USER.
- Do NOT copy the whole build context blindly — pair the Dockerfile with a .dockerignore.
- No secrets, tokens, or credentials in any build ARG, ENV, or COPY layer.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. `Dockerfile` — build stage plus minimal runtime stage, one brief comment per stage.
2. `.dockerignore` — covering VCS data, dependency caches, local env files, and test artifacts.
3. Build & run commands using BuildKit (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build ...), the expected final image size class, and how to verify it (docker images, or dive for layer inspection).
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Dependency install layer is cached separately from source copy (manifest/lock files copied first).
- Final stage contains no compiler, package-manager cache, or dev dependencies.
- HEALTHCHECK is included, or you state explicitly why the orchestrator's probe replaces it.
- Any instruction you are unsure builds on Docker {{docker_version}} is marked NOT VERIFIED.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

Runtime stack: {{runtime_stack_details}}. Exposed port: {{port}}. Start command: {{start_command}}.
prompts.expectedOutput: Multi-stage Dockerfile, .dockerignore, BuildKit build/run commands, and image-size verification guidance with NOT VERIFIED markers where untested.

prompts.title: One-Command Docker Compose Dev Environment
prompts.description: Authors a docker-compose.yml that reproduces a multi-service stack locally with healthcheck-gated startup, named volumes, documented .env handling, and a failure-mode table for common onboarding breakage.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Author a docker-compose.yml that reproduces the {{app_name}} stack locally — {{service_list}} — so a new engineer runs one command and gets a working environment.</goal>
<rationale>Onboarding currently takes {{onboarding_duration}} of manual setup with frequent 'works on my machine' drift; the Compose file becomes our single source of truth for local dev.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Pin every image to an exact version tag — no latest.
- Do NOT hardcode credentials; reference a .env file and ship a .env.example with dummy values. Real secrets never enter version control.
- Do NOT add services beyond {{service_list}}.
- Local dev only: no restart policies, replicas, or resource limits unless flagged as optional comments.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. `docker-compose.yml` on the current Compose specification; state your assumption about the deprecated top-level `version:` key.
2. `.env.example` with every variable documented inline.
3. README section: start/stop/reset commands, a port-map table, and a failure-mode table: | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | covering port conflicts, stale volumes, and migration drift.
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- The app service waits on the database via depends_on with condition: service_healthy, and the database defines a real healthcheck (e.g. pg_isready for PostgreSQL).
- Named volumes hold stateful data; bind mounts are used only for live-reload source code.
- One-command startup: docker compose up --build.
- The file would pass `docker compose config`; if you cannot run it, mark NOT VERIFIED and name the command.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: docker-compose.yml with healthcheck-gated dependencies, .env.example, README with port map and failure-mode table; config validity stated or NOT VERIFIED.

prompts.title: Container Security Hardening Audit (Defensive)
prompts.description: Performs an authorized defensive audit of a Dockerfile and runtime config, producing a severity-ordered findings table with quoted evidence and minimal anchored fixes — no wholesale rewrites, no plaintext secrets.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit and harden the Dockerfile and runtime config below against container-security best practice for our own production workload {{workload_name}}. This is authorized defensive hardening of our own images ahead of the {{release_date}} release.</goal>
<rationale>A review flagged {{findings_summary}}; we need a prioritized, minimal-change hardening pass, not a rewrite.</rationale>
<artifacts>
Dockerfile (verbatim):
{{dockerfile}}

Runtime config (verbatim):
{{runtime_config}}

Scanner output, if any (verbatim):
{{scanner_output}}
</artifacts>
</task>

<rules>
DO NOT:
- Rewrite the Dockerfile wholesale — propose the smallest diff per finding.
- Add commercial scanners or subscriptions without flagging cost.
- Change application behavior or exposed ports beyond what a finding requires.
If you find issues outside container security (e.g. application bugs), list them under 'Notes' but do NOT fix them.
</rules>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Findings table: | Severity | Finding | Evidence (quoted line) | Minimal fix |, ordered by severity. Cover at minimum: running as root, privileged mode or added capabilities, latest/unpinned tags, secrets in ENV/ARG/layers, missing read-only root filesystem, and shell/package-manager bloat in the final image.
2. Patched Dockerfile/config expressed as anchored edits against the quoted originals.
3. Verification commands using free tooling only (hadolint, trivy, docker run --read-only smoke test).
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every finding quotes the offending line as evidence; scanner claims you could not reproduce are marked NOT VERIFIED.
- No privileged: true or USER root survives without a written justification.
- No secret values appear anywhere in your output.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Severity-ordered findings table with quoted-line evidence, anchored minimal fixes, and free-tool verification commands.

prompts.title: First Kubernetes Workload: Deployment, Service, Ingress
prompts.description: Generates plain, current-API Kubernetes manifests (Deployment, Service, Ingress) for a first workload with resources, probes, and a non-root securityContext, plus a kubectl failure-mode table.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Create Kubernetes manifests to deploy {{app_name}} (container image {{image_registry_path}}) into namespace {{namespace}} on our Kubernetes {{k8s_version}} cluster: a Deployment, a Service, and an Ingress.</goal>
<rationale>We are moving {{app_name}} from a single VM to Kubernetes; this is the first workload, so these manifests become the team's reference example.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Target Kubernetes {{k8s_version}} APIs only (apps/v1 Deployment, v1 Service, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress) — no deprecated API versions.
- Do NOT add Helm, Kustomize, or operators — plain YAML we can kubectl apply.
- The image tag must be an explicit immutable tag ({{image_tag}}), never latest.
- No secrets in plaintext: reference the existing Secret {{secret_name}} via envFrom/secretRef and assume it already exists.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. `deployment.yaml` — {{replica_count}} replicas, resource requests and limits with one-line justification each, readinessProbe and livenessProbe against {{health_endpoint}}, and a securityContext with runAsNonRoot and readOnlyRootFilesystem (flag anything the app cannot tolerate).
2. `service.yaml` — ClusterIP, port mapping documented.
3. `ingress.yaml` — host {{hostname}}, TLS via {{tls_secret_name}}.
4. Failure-mode table: | Symptom | kubectl command to inspect | Likely cause |, covering ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, and probe failures.
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- `kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f .` would accept all three files; if you cannot validate, mark NOT VERIFIED and name the validation command.
- No production-safety-relevant field (resources, probes, securityContext) is left to cluster defaults.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Three apply-ready manifest files with justified resources/probes/securityContext and a kubectl-based failure-mode table.

prompts.title: Production-Harden a Deployment: PDB, HPA, Topology Spread
prompts.description: Adds disruption and scaling hardening to an existing Kubernetes Deployment — policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudget, autoscaling/v2 HPA, graceful shutdown, topologySpreadConstraints — with a coherent PDB/HPA capacity story.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Harden our existing Deployment {{deployment_name}} in namespace {{namespace}} for production: add a PodDisruptionBudget, a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, graceful shutdown, and spreading across nodes/zones.</goal>
<rationale>During the last node-drain event {{incident_description}}, we dropped traffic. The workload must survive voluntary disruptions and scale on real load before {{traffic_event}}.</rationale>
<existing_manifest>
{{current_deployment_yaml}}
</existing_manifest>
<boundaries>
- Preserve the existing container spec, image, and probes unless a change is required for correctness — justify any such change.
- Workload-level only: do NOT introduce cluster-autoscaler, KEDA, or service-mesh changes.
- Do NOT set minAvailable/maxUnavailable so aggressively that node drains block; state the tradeoff you chose.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. `pdb.yaml` — policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudget with one line of rationale for the chosen minAvailable/maxUnavailable.
2. `hpa.yaml` — autoscaling/v2 HPA on {{scaling_metric}} with min/max replicas and scale-down stabilization; one line on why that metric over plain CPU.
3. Anchored edits to the existing Deployment: terminationGracePeriodSeconds and a preStop hook if the app needs drain time, plus topologySpreadConstraints.
4. Failure-mode table: | Event | Expected behavior | How to verify (command) |, covering node drain, traffic spike, and a slow-rolling deploy.
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- HPA minReplicas >= {{min_replicas}} and is consistent with the PDB so voluntary disruptions never take the service below serving capacity.
- The metrics-server (or Prometheus adapter) dependency of the chosen HPA metric is stated explicitly.
- Anything you could not validate against a live cluster is marked NOT VERIFIED with the command that would validate it.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: pdb.yaml, autoscaling/v2 hpa.yaml, anchored Deployment edits, and a verifiable failure-mode table with a coherent PDB/HPA capacity story.

prompts.title: Kubernetes Incident Diagnosis from Live Evidence
prompts.description: Drives an evidence-bound diagnosis of a live pod incident (CrashLoopBackOff, Pending, OOMKilled) from verbatim kubectl output and logs, separating mitigation from permanent fix and marking every unverifiable claim.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Diagnose why pods for deployment {{deployment_name}} in namespace {{namespace}} are in {{observed_state}} (e.g. CrashLoopBackOff, Pending, OOMKilled) and produce a minimal remediation plan.</goal>
<rationale>This is a live production incident declared at {{incident_time}} affecting {{impact_description}}; every remediation step must be justified by evidence, not guesswork.</rationale>
<evidence>
- kubectl get pods / kubectl describe output (verbatim): {{kubectl_describe_output}}
- Container logs, last 100 lines (verbatim): {{container_logs}}
- Recent events (verbatim): {{events_output}}
- Deployment spec (verbatim): {{deployment_yaml}}
- Cluster: Kubernetes {{k8s_version}}, CNI: {{cni}}, node pool: {{node_pool_details}}
</evidence>
</task>

<rules>
- State your hypotheses, then for each one quote the exact evidence lines that support or refute it.
- Explicitly separate root cause from downstream symptoms (e.g. readiness-probe failures caused by an OOMKill).
- Do NOT recommend a cluster upgrade, CNI change, or node replacement unless the evidence demands it — and say what additional output would be required to justify it.
- Any claim not directly supported by the pasted evidence is marked NOT VERIFIED together with the exact kubectl command needed to verify it.
</rules>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Root-cause statement with quoted evidence.
2. Two clearly separated lists: immediate mitigation (smallest blast radius first) and permanent fix.
3. Risk note per remediation step: what breaks if the diagnosis is wrong.
4. Detection gap: which alert or probe would have caught this earlier.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- No remediation step lacks either a quoted-evidence justification or an explicit NOT VERIFIED marker.
- Mitigation steps are ordered by reversibility (roll back / scale before delete / upgrade).
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Hypothesis-by-hypothesis evidence analysis, root cause with quoted lines, reversible-first mitigation list, per-step risk notes, and a detection-gap recommendation.

prompts.title: Reusable Terraform Module with Guardrails
prompts.description: Authors a standard-structure Terraform module (main/variables/outputs/versions/README) with pinned provider versions, validated variables, sensitive-output marking, and explicit cloud-cost flags on expensive defaults.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Write a reusable Terraform module at {{module_path}} that provisions {{resource_description}} on {{cloud_provider}}, following the standard module structure: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, versions.tf, README.md.</goal>
<rationale>Three teams are copy-pasting divergent configurations for {{resource_description}}; a versioned module with sane defaults is our consolidation point before {{deadline_context}}.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Require Terraform >= {{tf_version}} and pin provider {{provider_and_version}} in versions.tf — no floating version constraints.
- Do NOT hardcode environment names, account IDs, or CIDR blocks — expose them as variables with validation blocks.
- CIDR logic must be prefix-length-correct: test 172.16.0.0/12 membership by range (second octet 16-31) or via cidrhost/prefix arithmetic, never substring matching; derive subnet prefix lengths from the actual input CIDR (assert one expected prefix length, or compute newbits from it) — never assume /16 while validation admits other lengths.
- No credentials or secrets anywhere; mark sensitive outputs with sensitive = true.
- Module only: do NOT create the root module or backend configuration.
- Flag every cloud-cost-relevant default (instance sizes, NAT gateways, multi-AZ) in a 'Cost notes' section.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. The five module files, complete.
2. README.md with an inputs table (name/type/default/required), an outputs table, and one usage example calling the module via a pinned ref.
3. A validation block on at least {{critical_variable}} with a helpful error message.
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- `terraform init && terraform validate` and `terraform fmt -check` would pass; if you cannot run them, mark NOT VERIFIED and name the commands.
- Every resource name derives from a name_prefix variable — no collisions between module instances.
- Defaults favor the cheapest safe option; expensive defaults carry a written justification in Cost notes.
- Deletion behavior is explicit: document any prevent_destroy or deletion-protection choice and why.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Five module files, README with input/output tables and pinned-ref usage example, validation blocks, and a Cost notes section flagging expensive defaults.

prompts.title: Terraform Plan Review and Zero-Destroy Refactor Strategy
prompts.description: Reviews a verbatim terraform plan for a pure module refactor, classifies every destroy/create as genuine change or address move, and produces a moved-block-based apply strategy that converges to zero destroys.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Review this terraform plan output for {{environment}} together with the proposed module refactor, and produce a safe apply strategy that avoids unintended resource destruction.</goal>
<rationale>The refactor ({{refactor_summary}}) is pure code organization — no real infrastructure change is intended. A plan showing destroy/create means state-address drift, and a blind apply would cause {{destruction_impact}}.</rationale>
<evidence>
- terraform plan output (verbatim, complete): {{plan_output}}
- Refactored module layout summary: {{module_diff_summary}}
- Terraform {{tf_version}}, backend: {{backend_type}}
</evidence>
</task>

<rules>
- Go through every planned destroy/create pair in the plan output and classify each as a genuine change or an address move.
- Do NOT approve `terraform apply` while any unexplained destroy remains.
- Prefer `moved` blocks (Terraform >= 1.1) over `terraform state mv`; state the tradeoff when state surgery is genuinely needed.
- No backend-config changes, and no -target applies except as an explicitly justified last resort.
</rules>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Plan-verdict table: | Resource | Plan action | Genuine change or address move | Required action |.
2. The exact moved blocks (or state mv commands) needed, file-ready.
3. Ordered apply strategy: the sequence of commands with the expected plan result after each step (target: zero destroys for a pure refactor).
4. Rollback note: how to recover if an apply goes wrong (state backup, saved plan file via terraform plan -out).
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every destroy in the plan is accounted for in the verdict table — zero unexplained destroys.
- The stated end state is a plan showing 'No changes' or only the intended diffs; any deviation you cannot prove is marked NOT VERIFIED with the command to confirm it.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Per-resource plan-verdict table, file-ready moved blocks, an ordered apply sequence converging to zero destroys, and a rollback note.

prompts.title: IaC Tooling and Environment-Structure Decision (Terraform vs Pulumi)
prompts.description: Runs an options-and-tradeoffs decision between Terraform, Pulumi, and a wildcard option, plus environment structuring (directories vs workspaces vs separate state), delivered as a weighted decision matrix with a migration sketch.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Decide our infrastructure-as-code strategy for {{org_context}}: Terraform vs Pulumi, plus how to structure environments ({{environment_list}}) — directories vs workspaces vs separate state per environment.</goal>
<rationale>We are standardizing before provisioning {{upcoming_infrastructure}}; the choice is expensive to reverse once state files and modules accumulate, and the team is split.</rationale>
<context>
- Team: {{team_size_and_skills}}
- Clouds: {{cloud_providers}}
- Existing IaC: {{existing_iac_state}}
- Compliance needs: {{compliance_requirements}}
- CI/CD: {{ci_system}}
</context>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>
1. Enumerate 2-3 viable approaches (at minimum: Terraform with per-env directories; Pulumi in {{team_language}}; one wildcard such as Terraform workspaces or OpenTofu). For each: pros, cons, and how it fails — the concrete failure mode, not generic risk.
2. A decision matrix weighted by these criteria: {{weighted_criteria}} (e.g. team skill match, provider coverage, state-management maturity, testing story, hiring pool, license risk).
3. One recommendation naming the single criterion that decided it, and what evidence would flip the decision.
4. Migration sketch: the first three concrete moves from {{existing_iac_state}} to the recommended approach, with cost and risk notes.
</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- The matrix applies the stated weights and shows scores per option per criterion.
- Capability claims are version-aware (state assumed versions; mark anything beyond your certain knowledge NOT VERIFIED).
- If the constraints in {{org_context}} point away from the majority/fashionable choice, say so explicitly rather than hedging.
- No license or per-seat cost claims without flagging them as assumptions.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: 2-3 options with concrete failure modes, a weighted decision matrix, one recommendation with its deciding criterion, and a three-move migration sketch.

prompts.title: First Prometheus Alerting Rules for a Service
prompts.description: Writes a first Prometheus rules file covering up/down, error ratio, latency percentile, and saturation — using only metrics the caller actually has, with for: durations, severity labels, and runbook annotations.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Write Prometheus alerting rules for {{service_name}} covering the four basic signals — is the service up, error rate, latency, and resource saturation — in a rules file our Prometheus {{prometheus_version}} server can load.</goal>
<rationale>We currently discover outages from user reports; {{recent_missed_incident}} went unnoticed for {{detection_gap_duration}}. These first alerts page on-call before users notice.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Use only metrics we actually have: {{available_metrics}}. If a signal lacks a metric, state what instrumentation is missing instead of inventing a metric name.
- Do NOT alert on raw counts or single-sample blips — use rate() over a window plus for: durations to suppress noise.
- Every alert carries a severity label and summary/description/runbook annotations; no alert without an actionable message.
- Do NOT add recording rules beyond what the alerts need.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverables>
1. `alerts.yml` — one rule group in valid Prometheus rule syntax.
2. Per-alert rationale: one line each on threshold choice and expected false-positive behavior.
3. Failure-mode table: | Alert | What it misses | What makes it noisy |.
</deliverables>
<acceptance_criteria>
- `promtool check rules alerts.yml` would pass; if you cannot run it, mark NOT VERIFIED and name the command.
- The error-rate alert uses a ratio (errors / total requests) over {{error_window}} with threshold {{error_threshold}}.

prompts.title: Grafana Dashboard and SLO Specification

prompts.title: Multi-Window Burn-Rate Alerting Design

<rationale>Current alerts fire {{current_page_volume}} pages per week with {{false_positive_share}} noise and on-call is desensitized. Burn-rate alerting pages only when the error budget is genuinely threatened.</rationale>
<context>
- SLO: {{slo_target}} over {{slo_window}} (e.g. 99.9% over 30 days)
- Existing SLI PromQL: {{sli_promql}}
- Metrics: {{available_metrics}}; Prometheus {{prometheus_version}}, Alertmanager {{alertmanager_version}}
- On-call: {{oncall_structure}}
</context>
</task>

3. Alertmanager routing sketch: which severities page vs ticket, with grouping and inhibition rules to prevent double-notifying.
4. Failure-mode analysis: what this design misses (short full outages below the burn threshold, low-traffic services with unstable rates, budget reset behavior) and the compensating control for each.
</deliverable>

prompts.title: Bad-Release Rollback Runbook

prompts.prompt:
<task>

<rationale>During {{past_incident}}, rollback took {{actual_rollback_duration}} because the steps lived in a senior engineer's head. This runbook must make rollback a {{target_rollback_duration}} operation.</rationale>
<context>
- Deploy mechanism: {{deploy_mechanism}}
- Artifact versioning: {{artifact_versioning}}
- Database migrations: {{migration_approach}}
- Traffic shape: {{traffic_profile}}
</context>
<boundaries>

</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>

3. Rollback procedure — exact ordered commands for {{deploy_mechanism}} (e.g. kubectl rollout undo vs helm rollback, and which one applies here and why), with the expected output per step.
4. Database compatibility — how {{migration_approach}} constrains rollback; which releases are NOT rollback-safe and how they are tagged.

</deliverable>

</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

prompts.title: Deployment Strategy Decision: Rolling vs Blue-Green vs Canary

<<<< ANCHOR (verbatim existing lines)
{{exact current code}}
====
{{replacement}}
>>>> END

Evidence: the reasoning tied to specific pasted output, or 'NOT VERIFIED' where you could not verify. 3. Minimal fix: anchored diff (FILE / ANCHOR / ==== / END blocks). 4. Verification: the command or interaction that proves the fix, with its actual output. If you could not run it, say 'NOT VERIFIED' and describe what I should run.

prompts.title: WCAG audit with evidence
prompts.description: Audit a page or component against WCAG criteria with every finding grounded in a cited element or line of code — no generic 'could improve' advice.

Audit {{target: the pasted component/page code, or the URL/route to inspect}} for accessibility problems against WCAG 2.2 Level {{A|AA}}.

CONTEXT: {{framework, whether this is SSR or client-rendered, known assistive-tech targets, any existing a11y tooling/tests in the repo}}.

RULES:

| # | Severity (critical/major/minor) | WCAG criterion | Evidence (file:line or element) | Problem | Suggested fix (one line) |
Ordered by severity, violations before enhancements.

Then a '## Runtime checks needed' section listing what must be verified in a browser/screen reader and exactly how.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Every row cites evidence; zero rows of unattributed advice.
- Keyboard-only and screen-reader paths through {{key flow, e.g. 'the checkout form'}} are each either confirmed from code or listed as a runtime check.
prompts.expectedOutput: A severity-ordered findings table with WCAG criteria and file/line or element evidence for every row, plus a runtime-checks section. No fixes applied.

prompts.title: Fix keyboard and focus behavior
prompts.description: Implement or repair keyboard navigation and focus management for an interactive component (dialog, menu, tabs) with anchored diffs and a behavior checklist as the contract.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Make {{component, e.g. 'the modal dialog in components/Modal.tsx'}} fully keyboard-operable and focus-managed per the WAI-ARIA {{pattern, e.g. 'Dialog (Modal)'}} pattern.</goal>
<rationale>It currently fails: {{current broken behavior, e.g. 'Escape does nothing, focus escapes to the page behind, tab order traps'}}. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot complete {{the affected flow}}.</rationale>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Restyle anything or change visual appearance.
- Rework the component's props API unless the focus fix strictly requires it (justify if so).
- Add a dependency — use native behavior and React primitives.
If you find other a11y issues, list them under 'Notes' but do NOT fix them here.
DO:
- Keep the diff minimal and anchored; preserve all existing behavior for pointer users.
</rules>
</task>

REFERENCE: match the keyboard/focus approach already used in {{reference accessible component}}, if provided.

OUTPUT FORMAT: anchored edits —
FILE: {{path}}
<<<< ANCHOR (verbatim existing lines)
====
{{replacement}}
>>>> END

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (verify each; paste test output or describe the exact manual check):
- [ ] Tab/Shift+Tab cycle stays inside the component while open; focus returns to the trigger on close.
- [ ] {{pattern-specific keys, e.g. 'Escape closes; Arrow keys move between options; Home/End jump'}} work.
- [ ] Correct roles/attributes present (e.g. role, aria-modal, aria-labelledby) — cite the rendered markup.
- [ ] Existing tests pass unmodified; add focus-order tests only in {{test file}}.

Any criterion you could not verify = NOT VERIFIED; say so explicitly.
prompts.expectedOutput: Anchored diff blocks, a criterion-by-criterion verification checklist with evidence or explicit NOT VERIFIED markers, and a Notes section for out-of-scope finds.

prompts.title: Design an accessible composite widget
prompts.description: Decide between native elements, a headless library, or a custom ARIA implementation for a composite widget, weighing real accessibility risk before committing to code.
prompts.prompt:
We need a {{widget, e.g. 'combobox with async search and multi-select'}} in {{app/stack, e.g. 'React 19 + Tailwind design system, no headless UI lib installed'}}.

GOAL: choose and specify the implementation strategy that carries the least accessibility risk for our constraints — then produce the interaction specification, not the full component.

First enumerate 2-3 viable strategies: e.g. native element composition ({{native candidate, e.g. '<select> / <datalist>'}}), a headless library ({{candidate lib}}), or a custom ARIA-pattern implementation per the APG {{APG pattern name}}. For each: pros, cons, and how it fails for assistive-technology users specifically (which screen reader/browser combination breaks, what keyboard interaction is lost).

Then a decision matrix weighted by: {{criteria, e.g. 'AT support breadth 3x, mobile UX 2x, maintenance cost 2x, bundle 1x'}}.

OUTPUT CONTRACT:
1. Strategy options with AT-specific failure modes.
2. Decision matrix table and one recommendation with its deciding criterion; push back if my constraints point to the native option and I seem to be overlooking it.
3. Interaction specification for the recommended strategy: keyboard map (key -> behavior), focus rules (initial focus, return focus, typeahead), required roles/states/properties with exactly which element carries each, and announcements a screen reader should make per state change.
4. Acceptance criteria: checkable behaviors (e.g. 'NVDA + Chrome announces the selected option on ArrowDown'), each tagged manual-test or unit-test.

BOUNDARIES: do NOT write component implementation code; do NOT specify visuals beyond what affects accessibility; do NOT claim screen-reader behavior you cannot support from the APG pattern or cited evidence — mark unverifiable claims 'NEEDS AT TEST'.
prompts.expectedOutput: 2-3 strategy options with AT-specific failure modes, a weighted decision matrix, a full interaction specification (keyboard map, focus rules, ARIA placement, announcements), and testable acceptance criteria with NEEDS AT TEST markers where unverifiable.

prompts.title: Responsive layout matched to a mockup
prompts.description: Implement a responsive layout against a mockup using the project's styling system, then verify with screenshots at each breakpoint instead of claiming it looks right.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement the layout for {{page/component}} so it matches {{mockup: attached image / Figma link / description}} at breakpoints {{e.g. '375px, 768px, 1280px'}}.</goal>
<rationale>This is a customer-facing surface; visual drift between breakpoints is a shipping defect, not polish.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Use the project's styling approach: {{e.g. 'Tailwind v4 with our design tokens; no arbitrary values where a token exists'}}.
- Do NOT change any component logic, data fetching, or props — styling/layout only.
- Do NOT add CSS files, frameworks, or one-off inline styles outside the established pattern.
- Touch only {{files in scope}}.
</boundaries>
</task>

Reference for house style: {{reference styled component}}.

OUTPUT CONTRACT:
1. The modified file(s), anchored-diff format against current content.
2. Breakpoint behavior summary: what changes at each breakpoint and why that matches the mockup.
3. Visual verification: run the dev server, capture screenshots at {{breakpoints}}, and compare each against the mockup. For every mismatch you can see, iterate with the smallest diff and re-capture. Report a before/after pair per breakpoint as evidence — do not claim a match without the screenshot.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- No horizontal scroll or overflow at any listed breakpoint (verify, don't assert).
- {{specific requirements, e.g. 'nav collapses to hamburger below 768px; cards go 1/2/3 columns'}} each confirmed against a screenshot.
- If the mockup is ambiguous at some breakpoint, choose the simpler interpretation, flag it, and continue — do not invent extra breakpoints.
prompts.expectedOutput: Anchored style diffs, a per-breakpoint behavior summary, and before/after screenshot evidence per breakpoint with zero unchecked visual claims.

prompts.title: Convert component styling to design tokens
prompts.description: Migrate one component's hardcoded styles to the project's design-token system as a purely visual-neutral change, with a before/after screenshot check to prove no drift.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Convert the styling of {{component file}} to our design-token system ({{e.g. 'Tailwind theme tokens in tailwind.config / CSS variables in tokens.css'}}), replacing hardcoded values like {{examples, e.g. '#3b82f6, 13px, magic z-index: 999'}}.</goal>

- Do NOT restructure markup, rename classes for style, or touch logic.
- Do NOT modify the tokens file itself.
</boundaries>
</task>

Reference for the target pattern: {{component already on tokens}}.

OUTPUT CONTRACT:
1. Anchored edits (FILE / ANCHOR / ==== / END) for the component only.
2. Mapping table: old hardcoded value -> token used (or 'left as-is — gap').
3. Verification: run the dev server and capture a before/after screenshot of the component in default theme; confirm no visual drift or call out any intentional difference. If {{dark mode / alternate theme}} exists, capture one screenshot there too showing the component now follows the theme.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Zero remaining hardcoded values from my list except documented gaps.
- Screenshots attached as evidence; 'looks the same' without a screenshot does not count.
prompts.expectedOutput: Anchored diffs to the single component, an old-value-to-token mapping table with documented gaps, and before/after screenshot evidence including a theme check if applicable.

prompts.title: App Router route with loading and error states
prompts.description: Add a Next.js App Router route with correct server/client boundaries, streaming loading UI, and error handling as one bounded vertical slice with a checkable contract.

<rationale>Users currently {{pain point}}; this route completes the {{flow}} vertical slice.</rationale>
<boundaries>

</boundaries>
</task>

Reference conventions: follow {{existing route, e.g. 'app/dashboard/page.tsx'}} for data fetching, caching, and error handling patterns.

prompts.title: Vertical Slice Plan from a Feature Brief
prompts.description: Turns a one-line feature brief into a single tracer-bullet slice plan that crosses shared types, database, API, UI, and tests, explicitly blocking horizontal phasing and scope creep.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Produce an implementation plan for the feature "{{feature_name}}" as ONE vertical slice that crosses every layer: shared types, database, API, UI, tests.</goal>
<rationale>Horizontal phasing (all backend first, all frontend later) delays end-to-end feedback and hides contract mismatches between front and back. A thin tracer-bullet slice surfaces integration risk immediately.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT design beyond this one slice: no admin views, bulk operations, or settings pages unless listed here: {{allowed_extras}}.
- Do NOT invent endpoints, hooks, or components that "might be needed later".
- Do NOT write implementation code in this response; plan only.
- Stack is fixed: {{stack, e.g. "Next.js App Router + tRPC + Prisma + React Query"}}. No substitutions.
</boundaries>
</task>
<contract>
<deliverable>A slice plan in Markdown with exactly these sections:
1. Shared types - the request/response shapes binding front and back (exact field names, nullability, validation rules).
2. Data layer - schema change or query, stated as a diff against {{schema_file}}.
3. API layer - procedure/route signature, auth requirement, error cases with status codes.
4. UI layer - route path, component tree, loading/empty/error states.
5. Tests - one failing test per layer, named by file path.
6. Verification - one end-to-end check proving the slice works in a browser.</deliverable>
<format>Numbered sections; every file mentioned by full path; no code block longer than 10 lines.</format>
</contract>
Acceptance criteria:
- Every UI element in section 4 traces to an API field in section 1.
- Every error case in section 3 has a matching UI state in section 4.
- The plan names at least one thing explicitly OUT of scope.
If the brief is ambiguous, ask up to {{max_questions, e.g. 5}} questions before planning instead of guessing.
prompts.expectedOutput: A six-section Markdown slice plan (types, data, API, UI, tests, verification) with full file paths and an explicit out-of-scope list.

prompts.title: Implement One Vertical Slice (Next.js + tRPC + Prisma)
prompts.description: Implements a single pre-planned slice end-to-end with a type-safe path from form input to database and back, pinned to existing codebase conventions and gated on real verification evidence.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement the vertical slice defined in {{spec_or_plan_file}}: users can {{slice_outcome, e.g. "save a display name and see it rendered on /settings/profile"}}.</goal>
<rationale>This is the tracer-bullet slice for {{feature_name}}. It must work end-to-end - a type-safe path from form input to database row and back - because later slices build on this exact contract.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Follow the conventions in {{reference_files, e.g. "src/server/routers/project.ts and src/app/(app)/projects/page.tsx"}}: same naming, file layout, error handling. Introduce no pattern that appears in neither reference.
- Do NOT touch files outside: {{in_scope_paths}}.
- Do NOT add dependencies. Do NOT refactor unrelated code. If you find other issues, list them in a Notes section but do NOT fix them.
- The client must call the real tRPC procedure through {{api_client_path}}: no fetch stubs, no mock handlers, no hardcoded data.
</boundaries>
</task>
<contract>
<deliverable>Working slice: Zod input schema, tRPC procedure, Prisma query, page/component using React Query with loading, empty, and error states.</deliverable>
<files>{{files_to_create_or_modify, one per line}}</files>
<acceptance_criteria>
- {{typecheck_command, e.g. "pnpm tsc --noEmit"}} passes; paste output.
- {{test_command}} passes including one new test for the procedure; paste output.
- Every Zod-rejected input produces a visible form error, not a console-only failure.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
Before finishing, verify each acceptance criterion with an actual command and paste the output verbatim. Anything not executed is NOT VERIFIED; say so explicitly.
prompts.expectedOutput: A working end-to-end slice (schema, procedure, UI states) with verbatim typecheck and test output as completion evidence.

prompts.title: Interview-to-Spec for a Full-Stack Feature
prompts.description: Runs a structured requirements interview, then emits a self-contained SPEC.md (interfaces, data contract, out-of-scope, invariants, checkable criteria, E2E step) for a fresh implementation session.
prompts.prompt:
I want to build {{feature_brief, e.g. "a team-invite flow where admins email invitations to new members"}}.

Interview me before writing anything. Ask one batch of questions at a time about: the user journey from start to finish; what data exists and where it lives; the API surface (who calls what, with what permissions); UI states (loading, empty, error, success); edge cases ({{known_edge_cases, e.g. "expired invites, duplicate emails, revoked invitations"}}); and what is explicitly OUT of scope. If one of my answers conflicts with an earlier one, say so instead of silently picking one.

When the interview is done, write SPEC.md with exactly these sections:
- Goal and rationale
- Files and interfaces (named by path: types, API routes/procedures, pages, components)
- Data contract between front and back (exact request/response shapes)
- Out of scope (explicit list)
- Invariants (what must not change)
- Acceptance criteria (mechanically checkable, e.g. "{{example_check, e.g. "POST /api/invites with a duplicate email returns 409"}}")
- End-to-end verification step that proves the feature works in a running app

Boundaries: do NOT write implementation code; do NOT choose libraries I have not approved - propose options and wait; do NOT pad the spec with features I did not mention.

I will implement from SPEC.md in a fresh session, so it must be self-contained: nothing from this conversation may be assumed. Flag any section that still depends on an unresolved question instead of filling the gap with an assumption.
prompts.expectedOutput: A question-batch interview followed by a self-contained SPEC.md with named files, a front/back data contract, out-of-scope list, invariants, checkable criteria, and an E2E verification step.

prompts.title: Signup + Email Verification Slice with Security Tests First
prompts.description: Builds registration with signed, single-use verification tokens under strict anti-enumeration and anti-forgery invariants, gated on failing security tests before any implementation.
prompts.prompt:
Context: authorized defensive work on my own application, {{app_name}}. The goal is a signup flow that resists enumeration, token forgery, and replay.

<task>
<goal>Implement email/password signup with verification: a new user registers, receives a signed single-use verification link, and cannot sign in until verified.</goal>
<rationale>Registration is the highest-abuse endpoint in the app. Verification tokens and enumeration behavior are where real implementations leak.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Use {{auth_library, e.g. "better-auth"}} and {{email_provider}} exactly as already wired in {{auth_config_path}}; do NOT introduce a second auth library or hand-rolled crypto.
- Passwords hashed with {{hashing, e.g. "argon2id via the library's built-in hasher"}}; never store or log plaintext passwords or raw tokens.
- Responses must be identical for existing and non-existing emails (no user enumeration), with timing equalized.
- Do NOT build login UI, password reset, or OAuth - separate slices. If you notice gaps in them, list under Notes only.
</boundaries>
</task>
<contract>
<deliverable>Slice: schema change, signup mutation, token issuance/verification route, form with pending/verified/expired states.</deliverable>
<files>{{files}}</files>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Tests prove: duplicate email returns the same response shape as success; expired/used/tampered token returns 400 without revealing which; unverified sign-in is rejected.
- Tokens are single-use, expire after {{ttl, e.g. "24h"}}, and are stored hashed.
- {{test_command}} and {{typecheck_command}} pass; paste verbatim output.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
Phase 1 (this response): write the failing security tests only and paste the failing assertions verbatim. Phase 2 (after I confirm): implement the minimal change that makes them pass and paste the full suite result.
prompts.expectedOutput: Phase 1: failing security tests with verbatim failing assertions. Phase 2: the working slice with hashed single-use tokens, enumeration-proof responses, and green suite output.

prompts.title: Session Strategy Decision (Cookies vs JWT vs Hosted IdP)
prompts.description: Forces a three-option, weighted-matrix decision on session management across browser and backend(s), with concrete failure modes per option and an explicit push-back clause.
prompts.prompt:
Decision needed: how {{app_name}} should manage authenticated sessions across the stack.

Context: {{app_context, e.g. "Next.js App Router app with a FastAPI service behind it; mobile app planned within a year; 4-person team; SOC 2 audit expected"}}.

Enumerate exactly 3 viable approaches for session management across the browser client and backend(s) - for example: database-backed sessions with HttpOnly cookies; stateless JWT access tokens with refresh rotation; or a hosted identity provider ({{idp_candidate, e.g. "Clerk or Auth0"}}). For each approach give: pros, cons, the concrete way it fails (revocation latency, XSS/CSRF exposure, mobile compatibility, logout semantics), and its operational complexity.

Then produce a decision matrix weighted by these criteria: {{criteria, e.g. "team size, SSR needs, mobile plans, compliance burden, revocation requirements"}}. State the weight for each criterion before scoring, and score each option against it.

End with ONE recommendation, the criterion that decided it, and what evidence would change the recommendation. If my stated constraints contradict my implied preference ({{implied_preference, if any}}), push back explicitly rather than accommodating me.

Boundaries: do NOT write implementation code or config; do NOT recommend a hybrid of your own invention outside the 3 enumerated options; do NOT treat "industry standard" as an argument - tie every claim to my context above. If a criterion cannot be scored from what I have told you, mark it UNKNOWN and ask one targeted question.
prompts.expectedOutput: Three compared options with context-specific failure modes, a pre-weighted decision matrix, one recommendation with its deciding criterion, and explicit push-back where constraints conflict.

prompts.title: Adversarial Audit of an Existing Auth Flow
prompts.description: Reviews a live login/session flow end-to-end against named security invariants, returning a COVERED/PARTIAL/MISSING coverage matrix with quoted code evidence instead of generic advice.
prompts.prompt:
Context: authorized review of my own application's auth flow. The goal is prevention - find weaknesses before someone else does.

<task>
<goal>Audit the existing {{flow_name, e.g. "login + session refresh"}} flow end-to-end and verify each security invariant below against the actual code.</goal>
<rationale>Auth bugs live at layer boundaries: cookie flags set in one place and checked nowhere; error messages that differ by one word and leak account existence.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Review only: do NOT modify code. Output findings, not fixes - except minimal patch sketches where the fix is obvious.
- Scope is {{in_scope_paths}}. Issues spotted elsewhere go under "Out-of-scope observations" without analysis.
- No generic best-practice lists: every finding must cite a file and line from this codebase.
</boundaries>
</task>
Verify each invariant and mark it COVERED (quote the code), PARTIAL, or MISSING:
- Session cookie is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite={{samesite}}; rotation on privilege change.
- Login errors are identical for unknown user vs wrong password (check {{where_checked}}).
- Rate limiting on {{endpoints}}: where enforced, at what limit?
- Tokens/sessions revoked on {{revocation_events, e.g. "password change, logout-all"}}.
- Client-side auth state ({{client_auth_store}}) cannot drift from server truth; no authorization decisions made only in the browser.
Output: a coverage matrix (invariant, verdict, quoted evidence), then findings ranked by exploitability, each with a minimal patch sketch. Anything you could not verify from the provided code: mark NOT VERIFIED rather than guessing.
prompts.expectedOutput: A coverage matrix of auth invariants with quoted code evidence, exploitability-ranked findings with minimal patch sketches, and explicit NOT VERIFIED markers.

prompts.title: Realtime Transport Decision (SSE vs WebSockets vs Polling)
prompts.description: Decides the realtime transport for a concrete use case via a three-option tradeoff matrix grounded in the user's infrastructure, ending with a minimal proof-of-concept to validate the pick.
prompts.prompt:
Decision needed: which realtime transport for {{use_case, e.g. "live order-status updates in a support dashboard"}}.

Context: {{context, e.g. "Next.js hosted on Vercel, FastAPI backend on a container platform; ~200 concurrent viewers expected; updates originate from background jobs; corporate proxies in front of some users"}}.

Compare exactly 3 options: server-sent events, WebSockets, and short polling ({{polling_interval, e.g. "every 5s"}}). For each: pros, cons, and how it concretely fails in MY context - not in general. Address at minimum: one-way vs two-way needs, proxy/firewall behavior and HTTP/1.1 connection limits per browser, automatic reconnection semantics, infrastructure fit with {{hosting}}, and overhead per update.

Then a decision matrix weighted by {{criteria, e.g. "infrastructure fit, latency tolerance, implementation effort, debugging experience"}}. Declare weights before scoring; score each option.

End with ONE recommendation and the deciding criterion, plus the smallest proof-of-concept that would validate the choice: one route, a client snippet of roughly 20 lines, and exactly what to observe when running it.

Boundaries: do NOT write production code; do NOT introduce libraries beyond {{allowed_libs, e.g. "native platform APIs and the ws package"}}; do NOT hedge with "it depends" without a final pick. If a requirement I gave is ambiguous (for example, what "live" means in seconds), ask before deciding. If you are unsure of a platform limit, mark it UNVERIFIED and name the doc page to check instead of quoting a number.
prompts.expectedOutput: A three-way transport comparison with context-specific failure modes, a pre-weighted decision matrix, one recommendation, and a ~20-line proof-of-concept plan with observable success signals.

prompts.title: SSE Notification Stream End-to-End (FastAPI + React)
prompts.description: Implements a server-sent events slice from a real backend state change through StreamingResponse to an EventSource hook with distinct connection states, verified against the running app with curl evidence.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement realtime {{event_name, e.g. "document-processing status"}} updates: when {{trigger, e.g. "a background job changes a document's status"}}, connected clients see the change within {{latency_budget, e.g. "2 seconds"}} without polling.</goal>
<rationale>Users currently refresh manually and act on stale state. SSE fits this case: server-to-client only, automatic reconnection, plain HTTP through our proxies.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Transport is SSE (already decided): FastAPI StreamingResponse on the backend, native EventSource in the React client. Do NOT add socket.io or a WebSocket layer.
- Do NOT fake the event source: events must originate from {{real_event_source, e.g. "the existing job-status update path in workers/jobs.py"}} - no setInterval demo emitters.
- Do NOT build two-way messaging, presence, or filtering beyond {{auth_scope, e.g. "the authenticated user's own documents"}}.
- Follow the patterns in {{reference_files}} for routing, auth dependency injection, and hook structure.
</boundaries>
</task>
<contract>
<deliverable>Slice: typed event schema, SSE endpoint emitting on real state change, React hook ({{hook_name, e.g. "useDocumentStatus"}}) exposing connecting/open/error states, UI badge that updates live.</deliverable>
<files>{{files}}</files>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Endpoint responds with Content-Type: text/event-stream, keeps the connection open, and sends heartbeats every {{heartbeat, e.g. "15s"}} so proxies do not idle-kill it.
- EventSource reconnects after a dropped connection and resumes via Last-Event-ID without duplicate or missed events.
- Client renders connecting, live, and reconnecting as visually distinct states.
- {{test_command}} passes; paste output.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
Verify against the running app, not by reading code: paste the curl -N stream output showing a real event, kill the connection once, and describe the observed reconnect behavior. Anything not observed is NOT VERIFIED - say so.
prompts.expectedOutput: A working SSE slice (schema, endpoint with heartbeats, hook with connection states, live UI) verified with pasted curl -N stream output and an observed reconnect.

prompts.title: Harden a WebSocket Channel Against Real Networks
prompts.description: Closes reconnect, duplicate, backpressure, and zombie-connection gaps in an existing WebSocket feature with wire-compatible minimal diffs and one simulated-failure test per gap.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Harden the existing WebSocket feature {{feature_name, e.g. "the collaborative cursors + edits channel in ws/room.ts"}} against the failure modes below, without changing its happy-path behavior.</goal>
<rationale>The feature works on a good network and breaks silently on a real one: dropped messages, duplicated operations after reconnect, and unbounded server memory per room.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Must preserve: the current message protocol as consumed by {{client_path}}. Wire-compatible changes only (additive fields allowed; renamed or removed fields are not).
- Do NOT rewrite the module or swap libraries; {{ws_lib, e.g. "ws"}} stays. Smallest diffs that close each gap.
- Do NOT add CRDTs, multi-server pub/sub, or persistence - separate projects. Note them under "Deferred" if relevant.
</boundaries>
</task>
Address each failure mode; for each, name the mechanism and the test that proves it:
1. Reconnect: the client rejoins with its last-seen {{sequence_field, e.g. "seq"}}; the server replays missed messages or sends a snapshot - never silently skips.
2. Duplicates: redelivered messages are detected and dropped via {{dedupe_mechanism, e.g. "a per-client seen-set on message ids"}}.
3. Backpressure: a slow consumer cannot grow server memory unboundedly; define the drop-or-disconnect policy explicitly.
4. Zombie connections: heartbeat (ping/pong) with a timeout that actually closes dead sockets and frees room state.
<contract>
<deliverable>Diffs to {{files}}, plus one automated test per failure mode (simulate: killed socket, duplicated frame, slow reader, silent peer).</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each new test fails before your change and passes after; paste the failing assertion and the passing run verbatim.
- The existing happy-path suite stays green; paste it.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
For any failure mode you cannot reproduce in a test, mark it NOT VERIFIED and state what manual evidence would be needed.
prompts.expectedOutput: Minimal wire-compatible diffs closing four failure modes, each with a failing-then-passing simulated-failure test and verbatim runs, plus explicit NOT VERIFIED items where unproven.

prompts.title: Upload Pipeline Architecture Decision
prompts.description: Compares presigned direct-to-storage, server-mediated, and managed-service upload pipelines against the user's real constraints, producing a weighted matrix and a data-flow sequence for the winner.
prompts.prompt:
Decision needed: the upload pipeline architecture for {{use_case, e.g. "project attachments up to 200MB"}}.

Context: {{context, e.g. "Next.js on Vercel (serverless), S3-compatible storage already provisioned, files must be scanned before other users can download them, ~500 uploads/day expected"}}.

Enumerate exactly 3 viable pipelines - for example: direct-to-storage with presigned URLs; upload through the API server as multipart, proxied to storage; or a managed upload service ({{managed_option, e.g. "Uploadthing or Transloadit"}}). For each: pros, cons, and its concrete failure mode in my context - serverless body-size and duration limits, double-paying bandwidth through the server, where validation actually happens, how quarantine-before-public-access works, and upload-progress support.

Decision matrix weighted by: {{criteria, e.g. "file size ceiling, scanning requirements, infra effort, cost at 10x volume"}}. Declare the weights before scoring; score each option.

End with ONE recommendation, the deciding criterion, and the winner's data-flow sequence (client, then what, then storage, then what, then download authorization) stated as a numbered diagram.

Boundaries: no implementation code beyond the sequence sketch; no fourth "custom" option; no invented service limits - if a platform limit matters ({{platform_limit_example, e.g. "the hosting platform's request body cap"}}), state it as something to verify against current docs rather than quoting a number you are unsure of. If my constraints point away from my apparent preference ({{implied_preference, if any}}), say so directly.
prompts.expectedOutput: A three-option pipeline comparison with context-specific failure modes, a pre-weighted decision matrix, one recommendation, and a numbered data-flow diagram including the authorization gate.

prompts.title: Presigned Direct-to-Storage Upload Slice
prompts.description: Implements the presign → direct upload → confirm slice with authorization and content constraints enforced before signing, pinned SDK versions, and proof that a real file lands in the bucket.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement direct-to-storage uploads for {{artifact, e.g. "project attachments"}}: the browser requests a presigned URL from our API, uploads the file straight to {{storage, e.g. "S3 via @aws-sdk/client-s3 and @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner"}}, then calls confirm so the metadata row is created.</goal>
<rationale>Keeping file bytes out of the API server removes the body-size ceiling and the bandwidth cost; the presign/confirm pair keeps upload authorization and metadata under our control.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Use the AWS SDK packages already pinned in package.json - run npm ls and quote the installed versions. Do NOT add other upload libraries.
- Do NOT make the bucket public. Download authorization is out of scope except a 2-3 sentence design note.
- Do NOT build resumable/multipart-chunked uploads, image processing, or dropzone UI beyond {{ui_scope, e.g. "a plain file input with progress and error states"}}.
- The presign route must enforce {{constraints, e.g. "authentication, max 200MB, content-type allowlist [image/*, application/pdf]"}} BEFORE issuing a URL.
</boundaries>
</task>
<contract>
<deliverable>Slice: shared types, presign API route (validates, generates the object key, signs), confirm route (creates the row via {{orm, e.g. "Drizzle"}}), client upload function with progress, minimal UI wired to the real routes.</deliverable>
<files>{{files}}</files>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Presign rejects oversize or disallowed types with a 4xx before signing; paste the test output.
- Confirm rejects keys the user did not just upload ({{binding, e.g. "key prefix embeds the user id and a server-issued upload id"}}).
- A real file uploaded through the UI lands in the bucket at the expected key; paste verification evidence (aws s3 ls output or equivalent).
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
No stub routes returning canned URLs: every presign response must come from the real signer. Report any acceptance criterion you did not actually execute as NOT VERIFIED.
prompts.expectedOutput: A working presign/upload/confirm slice with enforced constraints, pinned-SDK version evidence, and pasted proof of a real object in the bucket.

prompts.title: Upload Pipeline Security Hardening
prompts.description: Hardens an existing pipeline so acceptance is based on what a file is rather than what the client claims: magic-byte sniffing, two-layer size enforcement, server-generated keys, and quarantine semantics, tests first.
prompts.prompt:
Context: authorized hardening of my own upload pipeline ({{pipeline_path}}). The goal is prevention: hostile files must be rejected or contained before they reach storage or other users.

<task>
<goal>Close the validation gaps in the upload pipeline so that acceptance is based on what the file IS, not what the client claims.</goal>
<rationale>The current implementation trusts {{current_trust, e.g. "the browser-sent Content-Type and the file extension"}} - both are fully attacker-controlled.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT change the happy-path UX or the storage layout; minimal diffs confined to {{in_scope_paths}}.
- Do NOT add a commercial scanning service; a documented hook point with a defined interface is enough.
- Keep the pinned dependencies; verify versions with npm ls or pip show and quote them before recommending anything.
</boundaries>
</task>
Address each vector; for each, state the mechanism and the test that proves it:
1. Content sniffing: validate magic bytes against the declared type using {{sniffing_tool, e.g. "the file-type package"}} - an executable renamed to .png must be rejected.
2. Size enforcement at two layers: the presign/upload constraint AND server-side verification ({{server_check, e.g. "HeadObject after upload, before confirm"}}) so a client lying about size is caught.
3. Filename handling: the stored key is server-generated; the original name is sanitized for display and never used as a path.
4. Quarantine semantics: new uploads are inaccessible to other users until {{gate, e.g. "post-upload validation passes"}}; state exactly where that gate lives.
5. Decompression/image bombs and polyglot files: state your mitigation, or mark NOT ADDRESSED with a reason.
<contract>
<deliverable>Minimal diffs plus one failing-then-passing adversarial test per vector.</deliverable>
</contract>
Write the adversarial tests first and paste the failing assertions verbatim; then implement and paste the passing runs.
prompts.expectedOutput: Five addressed attack vectors with mechanisms, minimal diffs, and verbatim failing-then-passing adversarial test runs per vector.

prompts.title: i18n Architecture Decision for Next.js App Router
prompts.description: Chooses the i18n library and locale-routing strategy for an App Router app via a weighted three-option matrix covering RSC support, SEO/hreflang, ICU MessageFormat, and translator workflow.
prompts.prompt:
Decision needed: the internationalization approach for {{app_name}}, a Next.js App Router application.

Context: {{context, e.g. "marketing site + dashboard, launching in English and German with Japanese within 6 months; SEO matters for the marketing pages; translators are non-developers who need a manageable file format"}}.

Compare exactly 3 viable options (candidates: {{option_a, e.g. "next-intl"}}, {{option_b, e.g. "react-i18next with i18next"}}, {{option_c, e.g. "react-intl / FormatJS"}}). For each: pros, cons, and how it concretely fails in my context. Cover App Router and React Server Component support, locale routing and SEO (hreflang, localized URLs), message format and ICU MessageFormat support, pluralization correctness, and the translator workflow.

Also decide, separately and in one paragraph: locale detection and routing strategy (subpath like /de/..., per-locale domain, or cookie-only) with the SEO and caching consequences of the choice.

Decision matrix weighted by {{criteria, e.g. "RSC compatibility, translator ergonomics, bundle impact, hiring familiarity"}}. Declare weights before scoring; score each option.

End with ONE library recommendation and ONE routing recommendation, each with its deciding criterion, plus what new fact would change each answer.

Boundaries: no implementation code; do NOT recommend building an in-house i18n framework; no invented feature claims - if you are unsure whether a library supports something at its current version, mark it UNVERIFIED and name the documentation page to check.
prompts.expectedOutput: A three-library comparison with RSC/SEO/ICU coverage, a separate routing-strategy verdict with SEO and caching consequences, a pre-weighted matrix, and two recommendations with deciding criteria.

prompts.title: End-to-End i18n Slice (Routing, Messages, Intl Formatting)
prompts.description: Implements one scoped locale slice across server and client components with locale routing, namespaced messages, correct plural forms, Intl-based date/number rendering, and grep-level proof no hardcoded strings remain.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Add end-to-end internationalization to {{scope, e.g. "the /dashboard section"}}: locale-aware routing, translated UI strings, and locale-correct date/number formatting, using {{library, e.g. "next-intl"}} as already decided in {{decision_ref}}.</goal>
<rationale>The scoped components hardcode English in roughly {{string_count}} places; the {{target_locale, e.g. "de"}} launch is blocked until routing, messages, and formatting work through both server and client components.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Locales for this slice: {{locales, e.g. "en, de"}} only. Config must not hardcode a two-locale assumption, but do NOT add more translations.
- Do NOT wrap strings outside {{in_scope_paths}}; sweeping the rest of the app is a later batch job.
- Do NOT introduce a second i18n library or a custom message-loading layer.
- Produce the {{target_locale}} messages yourself; where tone or context is ambiguous, add a FIXME comment instead of guessing.
</boundaries>
</task>
<contract>
<deliverable>Slice: locale routing config + middleware, message files ({{message_format, e.g. "JSON per locale, namespaced"}}), the listed components refactored to the library's APIs (server components via its async server APIs, client components via its provider/hooks), date/currency rendering through Intl-aware helpers, and a language switcher that preserves the current path.</deliverable>
<files>{{files}}</files>
<acceptance_criteria>
- {{build_command}} passes; paste output.
- {{sample_route, e.g. "/de/dashboard"}} renders German strings including a grammatically correct plural form ({{plural_example, e.g. "1 Einladung / 3 Einladungen"}}); paste the rendered evidence.
- No raw English string remains visible in the scoped components; paste the grep evidence.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
Verify against the running dev server where possible and paste what you observed; anything checked only by reading code is NOT VERIFIED.
prompts.expectedOutput: A working locale slice (routing, message catalogs, Intl formatting, switcher) with build output, rendered-plural evidence, and grep proof of zero remaining hardcoded strings.

prompts.title: i18n Catalog Quality Audit (Plurals, Interpolation, Fallbacks)
prompts.description: Audits message catalogs and call sites for correctness failures compilation misses: wrong ICU plural categories, mismatched interpolation contracts, broken fallback chains, and untranslated residue, every finding quoting its key.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit the i18n message catalog and its usage ({{catalog_paths}}) for correctness failures that compilation will not catch, and produce a prioritized fix list.</goal>
<rationale>Translated apps break subtly: plural categories that do not exist in the target language get forced into English shapes, interpolated values arrive undefined, and fallback chains silently render English in production.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Audit and report only; do NOT edit code or message files. Minimal patch sketches are allowed per finding.
- Scope: {{catalog_paths}} and the components in {{usage_paths}}. Anything else goes under "Out-of-scope observations."
- Every finding must quote the message key and the exact string or call site; no generic advice.
</boundaries>
</task>
Check at minimum:
1. Plural correctness: for each plural message, do the ICU categories used (zero/one/two/few/many/other) cover what {{target_locales}} grammatically requires? Flag English-shaped plurals in languages with richer category systems.
2. Interpolation contracts: every {variable} in every locale matches the base locale's set - no missing, extra, or differently-typed placeholders.
3. Rich-text/formatting tags: tag pairs balanced and identical across locales.
4. Fallback behavior: what actually renders when a key is missing in {{target_locale}} - trace the real fallback code path and quote it.
5. Untranslated residue: keys whose target-locale value equals the English source verbatim (likely untranslated rather than coincidentally identical).
6. Date/number/currency: any formatting done by string concatenation instead of Intl APIs.
<contract>
<deliverable>A findings table (severity, key/file, quoted evidence, minimal fix sketch), counts per category, and an explicit list of what you could NOT verify from the provided files.</deliverable>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A severity-ranked findings table across six check categories with quoted keys and fix sketches, category counts, and explicit unverifiable items.

prompts.title: Unified Cross-Stack Error Contract
prompts.description: Designs and pilots one typed error envelope from API to client mapping to deterministic UI states, with a two-candidate tradeoff comparison, no internal leakage, and per-category tests.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Design the error contract every layer of {{app_name}} speaks - one typed error envelope from the API, one mapping layer on the client, deterministic UI states - then implement it for the pilot slice {{pilot_slice, e.g. "the billing page plus its tRPC router"}}.</goal>
<rationale>Errors currently leak differently per layer: ORM exceptions reach toasts, validation messages differ between server and client, and users see raw HTTP text. Support cannot correlate reports because there is no shared error-code vocabulary.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- The contract must cover exactly these categories: validation (field-level), authentication, authorization, not-found, conflict, rate-limit, unexpected. Nothing else for now.
- Do NOT refactor error handling outside the pilot slice; produce the migration checklist for other slices instead.
- Do NOT expose stack traces, SQL, or internal paths in any client-visible payload.
- Keep {{stack, e.g. "tRPC errorFormatter + React Query"}}; no new error libraries.
</boundaries>
</task>
Before implementing, give exactly 2 candidate envelope shapes with pros, cons, and how each fails (for example: discriminated union with code + issues array, vs HTTP-status-only). Recommend one with the deciding criterion. If the two differ in client-visible shape, stop and wait for my approval; otherwise proceed and note the choice.
<contract>
<deliverable>Shared types ({{types_path}}), a single server-side mapping from throw site to envelope, client normalization in {{client_layer}}, UI states (field errors on the form; code-keyed messages for the rest; a correlation id on every unexpected error), and one test per category.</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- For each category: one test proving the envelope shape and one proving the UI state; paste the runs.
- An unexpected thrown error yields the generic code plus correlation id and never internals; paste that test's output.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A two-candidate envelope comparison with a recommendation, then the pilot implementation (types, server mapping, client normalization, UI states) with per-category test evidence and a no-internals leak test.

prompts.title: Full-Stack Bug Triage from Verbatim Evidence
prompts.description: Localizes a reported bug to exactly one layer (cache, state, API, data) from pasted evidence and code, requiring quoted citations per hypothesis and a named discriminating observation when evidence is insufficient.
prompts.prompt:
A bug report says: "{{bug_report, e.g. "the avatar sometimes shows the previous user's photo after switching accounts"}}".

<environment>
{{stack_and_versions, e.g. "Next.js 15.x, React Query 5.x, Fastify 5.x - pinned in package.json"}}
</environment>
<evidence>
{{verbatim_observations, e.g. "console errors, request/response pairs from the network tab, server log excerpts - pasted unedited"}}
</evidence>
<relevant_code>
{{suspect_files}}
</relevant_code>

<task>
<goal>Localize the root cause to ONE layer - cache, client state, API, or data - distinguishing it from downstream symptoms, then propose the minimal fix.</goal>
<rationale>Full-stack bugs get "fixed" at the wrong layer constantly: a stale cache-key bug patched by disabling the cache. The fix must address where the wrongness originates, not where it becomes visible.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT propose fixes for more than the one root cause; secondary observations go in a separate Notes list.
