<contract>
Per step: change → verification gate ({{test_command}}, {{typecheck_command}}, {{build_command}} green — verbatim output) → rollback (exact revert scope).
Evidence report: usage sites touched (grep before/after), migration-guide entries applied (quote each), and entries reviewed but NOT applicable (listed so review can confirm).
</contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- All gates green at every step with pasted outputs; every adapted call site traced to a quoted changelog entry; final `npm ls` shows {{target_version}} with no duplicate installed versions.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: Verbatim npm ls and quoted changelog entries, a four-step sequence with per-step gates and rollbacks, an applied/not-applicable migration-entry report, and a clean final npm ls.

prompts.title: Risk-Tiered Bulk Dependency Upgrade Campaign
prompts.description: Triage an outdated-dependency backlog into risk tiers and execute batch-verified upgrade PRs — security floor first, every breaking-change claim quoted, unknowns marked UNKNOWN.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Triage and execute the outdated-dependency backlog in {{repo_or_workspace}} (report: {{outdated_report}}) as a risk-tiered, batch-verified upgrade campaign — not a single mega-PR.</goal>
<rationale>Alert fatigue trained the team to ignore upgrades; the backlog now mixes security-critical and cosmetic updates, and indiscriminate bulk bumps have broken production twice.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Classify before upgrading: no version bumps during the triage phase.
- Never upgrade past the version the driver requires (the security floor) unless a quoted changelog justifies more; 'latest' is not a goal.
- Verify every claimed breaking change against the package's official changelog/release notes for the exact {{current_version}} → {{target_version}} range and paste the quoted entry. Changelog unverifiable? Mark the package UNKNOWN — do not invent its API changes.
- Dev/test-only dependencies and production dependencies are separate tiers with separate gates; unrelated majors never share a batch.
- The lockfile and CI matrix ({{ci_matrix}}) are the compatibility ground truth; green local tests alone do not justify a merge.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
1. Triage table: package | current → target | driver (CVE id / EOL / feature, with source) | risk tier (security-major / security-minor-patch / routine) | breaking-change evidence (quoted) | batch assignment.
2. Batch plan: per batch = packages → change → verification gate ({{install_command}}, {{test_command}}, {{build_command}}, {{ci_command}} green, verbatim outputs) → rollback (lockfile revert scope).
3. Execute batch 1 (lowest risk) only; close with a completion report table carrying evidence per check.
4. 'Blocked/unknown' list: packages whose changelogs could not be verified, with what is needed to unblock each.
</contract>

<acceptance_criteria>
- Every upgraded package traced to a quoted changelog; batch 1 green including CI; zero unverified 'should be safe' claims anywhere.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: A risk-tiered triage table with quoted breaking-change evidence, a batch plan with per-batch gates and lockfile rollbacks, batch-1 execution with a completion report, and a blocked/unknown list.

prompts.title: OWASP Top 10 Endpoint Surface Audit
prompts.description: Audit a specific route or controller in your own codebase against the OWASP Top 10 (2021), producing an evidence-cited findings table.
prompts.prompt: A defensive audit of {{route_or_controller, e.g. 'src/api/users.ts'}} in my own application against the OWASP Top 10 (2021), yielding verified findings I can remediate. This endpoint handles {{data_sensitivity, e.g. 'PII and payment metadata'}}; an unreviewed change shipped last sprint and I need evidence-based confirmation it is safe before release. - This is authorized defensive review of my own codebase. Remediation-focused only: do NOT provide exploitation payloads, bypass walkthroughs, or offensive tooling instructions. - Scope is limited to the files I paste below; do NOT speculate about code you have not seen — mark unseen dependencies as UNKNOWN. If a Top 10 category does not apply, say N/A with one line of why — do not pad. - Suggest fixes requiring dependencies not already in my project unless flagged as OPTIONAL. DO: - Cite file and line for every finding. - Justify each severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low) with the concrete impact on MY system. A Markdown findings table: | # | OWASP category (2021 ID) | Severity + justification | Location (file:line) | Evidence (quoted code) | Fix (minimal, in-place) | How to verify the fix | Follow with a short 'UNKNOWN / needs more context' list for anything you could not confirm from the pasted code. - Every finding cites file:line and quoted code. - Every severity includes a one-sentence impact justification. - UNKNOWN items listed explicitly rather than assumed safe. {{paste the route/controller and any middleware it calls, verbatim}}

prompts.title: Injection-Resistance Test Suite for a Form/API Handler
prompts.description: Generate defensive tests proving a handler in your own app rejects common injection and input-validation attacks (A03/A07 territory), failing-test first.
prompts.prompt: A test suite for my own {{handler, e.g. 'POST /api/comments'}} that proves it safely rejects malformed and malicious input classes (SQL injection, XSS payloads, oversized bodies, type confusion). We recently refactored input handling in {{module}} and have no regression coverage proving the endpoint still rejects hostile input; shipping without it risks a stored-XSS or injection incident. - Authorized defensive testing of my own application only. Payloads appear solely as test fixtures asserted to be REJECTED or safely stored-escaped; do NOT include working exploit chains or instructions for attacking third-party systems. - Write tests only in this response — do NOT modify implementation code yet. DO NOT: - Write tests that pass trivially (asserting a string is a string); every test must assert a concrete security property: 4xx rejection, parameterized-query usage, or escaped storage/output. - Add new test dependencies without flagging them. DO: - Follow the test conventions already present in {{reference_test_file}}. - Cover: SQL/NoSQL injection strings, stored + reflected XSS strings, path traversal in any filename/ID parameters, oversized payload, wrong content-type, and Unicode/confusable input relevant to {{field_list}}. Phase 1 (this response): failing tests in {{test_file}} using {{test_framework}}. Run them and paste the failing assertions verbatim as evidence. Phase 2 (only after I confirm): the minimal implementation fix, then full-suite output. - Each test names the attack class and the expected safe behavior. - At least one test fails against current code, with the verbatim failure pasted. - No implementation code in Phase 1. {{paste the handler and its validation layer verbatim}}

prompts.title: Security Headers & CSP Hardening Review

<boundaries>
- Defensive hardening of my own deployment only.
- Do NOT recommend removing functionality to satisfy a scanner; every tightening must keep {{critical_flows, e.g. 'checkout and embedded chat'}} working.
</boundaries>
</task>

<output_contract>

2. Complete replacement config block for {{config_format}} ready to paste.

4. Rollout note: which changes to ship behind Report-Only first.

- No 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' in the recommended policy.

prompts.title: AuthN Strategy Decision: Sessions vs Tokens vs Hybrid
prompts.description: Options-and-tradeoffs decision matrix for choosing an authentication architecture for a new app, with a recommendation and deciding criterion.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A defensible recommendation for the authentication architecture of my new {{app_type, e.g. 'B2B SaaS with web dashboard + public REST API'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Auth is expensive to migrate later; I need the decision made on stated criteria now, before scaffolding the user model and session layer.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- This is defensive design for my own application.
- My constraints: {{constraints, e.g. 'serverless deploy, 3-person team, must support SSO for enterprise customers within 6 months, EU data residency'}}.
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Recommend a pattern because it is fashionable; every option must be evaluated against MY constraints.
- Hand-wave security properties: state exactly where tokens live, how revocation works, and what happens on token theft for each option.
- Omit the 'how it fails' row — I need failure modes, not marketing.
DO:
- Enumerate 3 viable approaches (e.g., server-side sessions with opaque cookies; OAuth 2.1/OIDC with short-lived access tokens + refresh rotation; hybrid session-for-web/token-for-API).
- For each: pros, cons, token storage, revocation story, CSRF/XSS exposure, and operational burden for a {{team_size}} team.
- Respect current standards: OAuth 2.1 (PKCE everywhere, no implicit flow), Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookies, WebAuthn/passkeys as the phishing-resistant factor.
</rules>
<output_contract>
Decision table: | Option | Pros | Cons | Failure mode (how it breaks under attack or scale) | Weighted score vs my criteria: {{criteria_weights}} |
Then: one recommendation, the single criterion that decided it, and what evidence would change your mind. Push back if my constraints contradict my stated preference of {{my_leaning}}.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Exactly 3 options, each with a concrete failure mode.
- A single recommendation with the deciding criterion named.
- No option scored on criteria I did not provide.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: Three-option decision table with failure modes and weighted scoring, a single recommendation, and the deciding criterion.

prompts.title: Authorization Model Review (RBAC/ABAC/ReBAC)

We are adding {{new_capability, e.g. 'team-level guests and public share links'}} and I need to know whether the current model ({{current_model, e.g. 'role enum on the user row, checked in route middleware'}}) can express it safely before we build on it. - Defensive review of my own system. Describe attack paths only to the depth needed to justify a fix — no exploitation instructions. - Base every claim on the code/schema I paste; mark anything dependent on unpasted code as UNKNOWN. DO NOT: - Recommend a rewrite to a policy engine (OPA/Cedar/etc.) unless the pasted requirements demonstrably exceed the current model; prefer the smallest change that closes the gap. - Report theoretical issues with no reachable path in MY code — every finding needs a concrete route from an authenticated low-privilege user to the protected resource. DO: - Check: tenant-isolation on every query path, IDOR on resource IDs, privilege escalation via role/field mutation, mass-assignment on update endpoints, confused-deputy in service-to-service calls, and default-allow fallbacks. - Verify enforcement happens server-side at the data layer, not only in UI or middleware. 1. Model summary: actors, roles/attributes, resources, enforcement points (cite file:line). 2. Findings table: | # | Access path | Severity + justification | Location (file:line) | Evidence | Minimal fix | Verification test | 3. UNKNOWN list for enforcement points I didn't paste. 4. One-paragraph verdict: extend current model vs migrate, with the deciding factor. - Every finding traces a concrete path from low-privilege actor to protected resource. - Every enforcement claim cites file:line. - Extend-vs-migrate verdict includes a deciding factor. {{paste auth middleware, permission checks, and the data-access layer for the affected resources, verbatim}}

prompts.title: Login Flow Security Requirements Spec
prompts.description: Interview-to-spec prompt producing a complete security requirements spec for a login/signup/password-reset flow before any code is written.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A complete, implementation-ready SPEC.md for the security behavior of my {{flow, e.g. 'email+password login with MFA and password reset'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Login flows fail on edge cases (user enumeration, reset-token reuse, race conditions) far more than on the happy path; I want the security invariants written down and agreed before implementation keys on them.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- This session produces a spec only — no implementation code.
- Defensive design for my own application.
</boundaries>
</task>
<process>
Interview me in batches of at most 4 questions at a time. Cover: identifier strategy (email vs username) and enumeration resistance; rate limiting and lockout policy per endpoint; password policy and breach-list screening; MFA options (TOTP, WebAuthn/passkeys) and recovery codes; session issuance, fixation resistance, and idle/absolute timeouts; reset-link entropy, TTL, single-use, and invalidation-on-change; and audit logging of security events.
After my answers, write SPEC.md. Where I have no opinion, choose a sane default aligned with OWASP ASVS v4 Level 2 and mark it DEFAULT (changeable) rather than leaving it open.
</process>
<output_contract>
# SPEC: {{flow}} security requirements
## Goal & rationale
## Endpoints & flows (named)
## Security invariants (must-hold statements, e.g. 'reset tokens are single-use and expire in <= 30 minutes')
## Rate limits & lockouts (exact numbers per endpoint)
## Out of scope (explicit)
## Acceptance criteria (mechanically checkable, e.g. 'GET /reset with a reused token returns 400')
## End-to-end verification step proving each invariant
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every invariant is testable and has a matching acceptance criterion.
- ASVS-aligned defaults marked DEFAULT where I gave no answer.
- No implementation code anywhere in this session.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: SPEC.md with named endpoints, testable security invariants, exact rate limits, checkable acceptance criteria, and an E2E verification step.

prompts.title: Secrets-in-Repo Scan Triage & Remediation Plan
prompts.description: Triage a scanner's secrets report (gitleaks/trufflehog output) into true/false positives and produce a rotation-first remediation plan without ever reproducing the secrets.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Triage of the secrets-scan report for my own repository ({{scanner_and_version, e.g. 'gitleaks 8.24' output pasted below}}) into a deduplicated, severity-ranked remediation plan.</goal>
<rationale>The scan found {{finding_count}} candidate secrets across history; I need to know which are live credentials requiring rotation versus test fixtures, before I start rotating blindly.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Authorized defensive work on my own repository.
- NEVER reproduce a secret value in your output — refer to each finding by file:line, commit hash, and the last 4 characters only. If a fix requires naming the credential, use its variable/service name.
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Assume a match is live because the scanner flagged it; classify using the evidence available (file path, surrounding context, naming, entropy, whether it appears in tests/fixtures/examples).
- Recommend 'delete the file' as the whole fix for anything plausibly live — a committed credential is compromised until rotated, even after deletion.
- Inflate severity for committed-but-expired or obviously fake values.
DO:
- Deduplicate findings that are the same secret in multiple commits/paths.
- For each true positive, produce: rotation step (exact console/CLI location to rotate), code fix (move to {{secrets_store, e.g. 'env vars via our secrets manager'}}), history-rewrite decision (when git-filter-repo is worth it vs when rotation alone suffices), and a verification step.
</rules>
<output_contract>
1. Triage table: | ID | Location (file:line, commit) | Type | Verdict: LIVE/SUSPECT/TEST-FIXTURE/FALSE-POSITIVE + evidence | Severity | Rotation required? |
2. Remediation runbook ordered by severity: rotate -> remove from code -> purge history (if warranted) -> verify.
3. Prevention addendum: .gitignore / pre-commit hook / scanner CI config additions for this repo.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Zero secret values reproduced in output (last-4 only).
- Every verdict cites observable evidence, not vibes.
- Runbook is ordered and each step has a verification check.
</acceptance_criteria>
<scan_output>{{paste scanner JSON/SARIF output verbatim}}</scan_output>
prompts.expectedOutput: Deduplicated triage table with evidence-based verdicts, an ordered rotation-first runbook, and prevention config — with no secret values reproduced.

prompts.title: Secure Configuration Baseline Review (env, IaC, Docker)

prompts.title: Environment & Secrets Management Strategy (Design)

<rules>

<acceptance_criteria>

- No real secret values anywhere in the output.
</acceptance_criteria>

prompts.title: Dependency Audit Triage (npm audit / osv-scanner output)
prompts.description: Turn raw vulnerability-scanner output into a reachability-aware, deduplicated fix plan instead of a wall of CVEs.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>An actionable triage of the dependency vulnerability report for my own project ({{tool_and_command, e.g. 'osv-scanner -r .' / 'npm audit --json'}} output pasted below).</goal>
<rationale>The report lists {{count}} advisories; most audit output is noise (dev-only deps, unreachable code paths), and I need the 3-5 fixes that actually reduce risk, ordered correctly.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Defensive maintenance of my own project.
- Do NOT invent advisory details you cannot see in the pasted output or verify; if my knowledge of a CVE/GHSA may be stale, say so and tell me how to confirm (link to the GHSA/OSV ID, don't paraphrase from memory).
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Treat scanner severity as final: re-rank by reachability and exposure in MY app ({{app_context, e.g. 'public API, deps pasted in package.json below'}}). A critical in a dev-only test tool is not my top fix.
- Recommend blind 'npm audit fix --force' — assess each upgrade for breaking-change risk using the version delta shown.
- Dismiss findings without a reason; every downgrade in priority needs justification.
DO:
- Deduplicate advisories affecting the same package.
- For each kept finding: the dependency path (why it's installed), reachability assessment from the code/usage I provide, the minimal safe upgrade, and a verification step (test command or manual check).
</rules>
<output_contract>
1. Triage table: | Package | Advisory (GHSA/CVE ID) | Scanner severity | My-severity + reachability justification | Dependency path | Minimal fix | Verify |
2. Ordered fix plan (this week / next sprint / accept-risk-with-reason).
3. NOT-ACTIONABLE list with one-line justifications.
4. UNKNOWN list: advisories you cannot characterize from the pasted data alone.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every re-ranked severity has a reachability justification grounded in my pasted code/package.json.
- Fix plan ordered; accept-risk entries carry an explicit reason.
- No fabricated advisory details — unknowns routed to the UNKNOWN list.
</acceptance_criteria>
<scan_output>{{paste scanner output verbatim}}</scan_output>
<manifest>{{paste package.json / lockfile excerpt verbatim}}</manifest>
prompts.expectedOutput: Reachability-ranked triage table, ordered fix plan with accept-risk reasoning, NOT-ACTIONABLE and UNKNOWN lists.

prompts.title: New-Dependency Vetting Checklist (Supply-Chain Gate)
prompts.description: A repeatable vetting gate for evaluating a proposed new dependency before adding it, covering provenance, maintenance, and behavioral risk.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A go/no-go vetting report on {{package_name_and_version}} ({{ecosystem, e.g. 'npm'}}) before I add it to my own project for {{intended_use}}.</goal>
<rationale>Each dependency is supply-chain attack surface and maintenance debt; I want a repeatable gate so 'someone on the team liked the README' stops being the bar.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Assessment of a publicly available package for defensive purposes.
- My knowledge may be stale: for any factual claim you cannot verify from data I paste (registry metadata, repo stats), mark it UNVERIFIED and give me the exact command or URL to check (npm view, npm ls, deps.dev, OSV query) rather than asserting from memory. Never invent download counts, CVEs, or maintainer names.
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Hallucinate package facts; slopsquatting defense starts with not trusting recalled names. If the exact package name looks similar to a more popular one, flag the typosquat risk explicitly.
- Gate on vanity metrics alone (stars); a starred-but-abandoned package is worse than a quiet maintained one.
- Recommend adding the dependency 'just for' functionality we could implement in {{loc_threshold, e.g. '~30 lines'}} — run that comparison honestly.
DO:
- Evaluate: provenance (publisher identity, provenance attestations/sigstore if present, repo-to-registry link), maintenance (release cadence, open-issue hygiene, bus factor), transitive footprint (expected dep tree size — tell me how to measure it), permissions/behavior red flags (install scripts, network/filesystem access for its stated purpose), license compatibility with {{license_requirement}}, and the build-it-ourselves alternative.
</rules>
<output_contract>
Vetting report:
1. Identity check: exact name match, registry/repo link, UNVERIFIED flags with check commands.
2. Scorecard: | Dimension | Finding (evidence or UNVERIFIED + how to verify) | Pass/Concern/Fail |
3. Verdict: ADOPT / ADOPT-WITH-PINNING / VENDOR / REJECT, with the deciding factor.
4. If ADOPT: exact pinned install spec and the lockfile/CI controls to add.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Zero fabricated package facts; unverifiable claims marked UNVERIFIED with a check command.
- Verdict names a single deciding factor.
- Build-vs-adopt comparison included.
</acceptance_criteria>
prompts.expectedOutput: Identity check with UNVERIFIED flags, a dimension scorecard, an ADOPT/VENDOR/REJECT verdict with deciding factor, and pinning/CI controls.

prompts.title: SBOM & Lockfile Integrity Review
prompts.description: Review a project's lockfile/SBOM practices and CI pipeline for supply-chain weak points: unpinned deps, mutable sources, missing integrity checks.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A review of the dependency-install and CI pipeline for my own project ({{files, e.g. 'package.json, package-lock.json excerpt, .github/workflows/ci.yml, Dockerfile'}} pasted below) for supply-chain weak points.</goal>
<rationale>We pass audits but have never checked HOW dependencies enter the build — mutable tags, unpinned actions, and scripts running at install time are our blind spot.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Defensive review of my own pipeline.
- Minimal anchored fixes to pasted files only; no wholesale pipeline rewrites.
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Recommend locking everything to maximum paranoia regardless of cost; rank findings by realistic risk to a {{org_profile, e.g. 'small SaaS, public repo'}} team and say why.
- Flag a missing control without showing the exact pasted line that proves it is missing.
DO:
- Check: install command correctness in CI (npm ci vs npm install; --ignore-scripts where viable), lockfile presence and enforcement, integrity/hash verification, pinned GitHub Actions (full-length SHA vs mutable tag) and their permission scopes, base-image pinning strategy, install-time script execution, registry/proxy assumptions, and caching that could smuggle poisoned artifacts.
- For each gap: the realistic attack scenario in one sentence, then the minimal fix.
</rules>
<output_contract>
1. Findings table: | # | File:line | Weak point | Scenario + severity + justification | Minimal fix |
2. Fixes as anchored search/replace blocks against exact pasted content.
3. Hardened install-command spec for CI and local dev (one code block each).
4. Optional-upgrades list (SBOM generation, dependency review action, provenance checks) with effort estimates — clearly marked OPTIONAL.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every finding cites an exact pasted line.
- Every fix is an anchored edit.
- Severity rankings include org-context justification.
</acceptance_criteria>
<config>{{paste the pipeline and manifest files verbatim, with filenames as headers}}</config>
prompts.expectedOutput: Line-cited findings table with attack scenarios, anchored fixes, hardened install commands, and an optional-upgrades list.

prompts.title: Secure Code Review of a Single Diff (PR Gate)
prompts.description: A security-focused review of one pull-request diff with a COVERED/MISSING-style verdict table and evidence requirements — the standard PR security gate.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A security review of this diff to my own repository, deciding APPROVE / APPROVE-WITH-COMMENTS / REQUEST-CHANGES before merge.</goal>
<rationale>{{pr_context, e.g. 'This PR adds file-upload handling to the profile endpoint'}} — changes touching {{sensitive_surfaces, e.g. 'auth, file handling, or raw SQL'}} require a security pass, and rubber-stamping is how our last incident happened.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Authorized defensive review of my own codebase.
- Review ONLY the pasted diff plus the surrounding context I provide. Behavior of code outside the diff that you cannot see = UNKNOWN, not assumed safe or unsafe.
- Assume the diff is guilty until evidence shows otherwise: your job is to find what the author missed, not to summarize what they did.
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Produce a style/nitpick review; security-relevant findings only (a style note is allowed only if it creates a security ambiguity).
- Report a vulnerability class without showing the exact added/changed line that enables it and the concrete data-flow to the sink.
- Inflate severity because this is a security review; a theoretical issue requiring admin access is not High.
DO:
- Trace taint from each new input source (request body, params, headers, files, env) to its sinks (queries, shell, filesystem, HTML, redirects, deserialization).
- Check the diff against: injection, authz enforcement on new/changed endpoints, secret or PII exposure in logs/responses, unsafe defaults, TOCTOU on file operations, and error paths that leak internals.
</rules>
<output_contract>
1. Verdict: APPROVE / APPROVE-WITH-COMMENTS / REQUEST-CHANGES, one line.
2. Findings table: | # | Severity + justification | Location (file:line in diff) | Evidence (quoted line) | Data flow (source -> sink) | Minimal fix | Verification test |
3. UNKNOWN list: security-relevant behavior outside the pasted context, with the exact file I'd need to paste to resolve it.
4. Checked-and-clear list: vulnerability classes you explicitly traced and cleared, one line each with the evidence.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every finding quotes a diff line and traces source to sink.
- UNKNOWN items name the file needed to resolve them.
- Verdict follows from the findings, not despite them.
</acceptance_criteria>
<diff>{{paste the PR diff verbatim}}</diff>
<context>{{paste surrounding code the diff interacts with, verbatim}}</context>
prompts.expectedOutput: Verdict line, evidence-cited findings table with source→sink flows, UNKNOWN list naming needed files, and a checked-and-clear list.

prompts.title: Focused Review: Cryptography & Token Handling
prompts.description: A narrow, deep review of one file/module for cryptographic misuse: weak algorithms, bad randomness, key handling, token validation mistakes.
prompts.prompt: A deep-dive review of the cryptography and token-handling code in my own {{module, e.g. 'src/auth/tokens.ts'}} pasted below. This module issues and verifies {{artifacts, e.g. 'password-reset tokens and session JWTs'}}; subtle mistakes here (algorithm confusion, predictable randomness, missing expiry checks) are silent until exploited, so it gets its own review pass rather than a general one. - Authorized defensive review of my own code. - Review only the pasted module; dependencies you cannot see are UNKNOWN — but DO flag any call whose safe usage depends on parameters I haven't pasted, and name the file to paste. - Defensive depth only: describe weaknesses precisely enough to fix them, without exploitation walkthroughs. DO NOT: - Flag an algorithm as 'weak' without context: state what property is actually required here (collision resistance? preimage? unforgeability?) and whether the choice fails THAT requirement. - Recommend rotating to fashionable primitives without a migration story for existing tokens/sessions. - Assert library defaults you cannot verify; mark them UNVERIFIED with the doc/code location to check. DO: - Check: algorithm and key-size choices against current guidance; randomness sources (CSPRNG vs Math.random equivalents) for every security-relevant value; token validation completeness (signature, alg allowlist vs confusion, exp/nbf/aud/iss, key confusion between symmetric/asymmetric); timing-safe comparison for secrets; key storage and rotation; error messages that distinguish 'expired' from 'forged' to an attacker. Findings table: | # | Weakness | Severity + justification (required property vs actual) | Location (file:line) | Evidence | Minimal fix + migration note | Verification test | Then an UNKNOWN/UNVERIFIED list naming the exact files or docs needed. - Every 'weak' claim states the required security property and why the code fails it. - Fixes include a migration note for in-flight tokens/sessions. - No unverifiable library-default assertions presented as fact. {{paste the module verbatim}}
prompts.expectedOutput: Property-based findings table with migration-aware fixes, plus an UNKNOWN/UNVERIFIED list naming files/docs to resolve.

prompts.title: Regression Test for a Fixed Vulnerability
prompts.description: Convert an already-remediated vulnerability in your own app into a permanent regression test plus a prevention note, so it can't silently return.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A permanent regression test and prevention note for the vulnerability we just fixed in my own application: {{vuln_summary, e.g. 'IDOR on GET /api/invoices/:id allowed cross-tenant reads'}}.</goal>
<rationale>The fix (pasted below) was reviewed and merged, but nothing stops a future refactor from reintroducing it; I want the failure mode captured as an executable test while the context is fresh.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Defensive testing of my own application. The test asserts the SAFE behavior; include only the minimal attack input needed to prove the guard holds — no exploitation material beyond that.
- Write the test only; do NOT modify the fix itself in this response.
</boundaries>
</task>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Write a test that would pass even against the vulnerable version — the test must have failed pre-fix; say explicitly which assertion catches the old behavior and why.
- Re-test the whole endpoint; target the regression precisely (the guard condition, its bypass variant, and one adjacent case to prevent over-fitting the guard to the exact reported input).
DO:
- Follow the conventions in {{reference_test_file}}.
- Cover: the original failing input, the obvious bypass variant ({{bypass_hint, e.g. 'ID as string vs number, encoded delimiter'}}), and a legitimate-access control case that must still pass.
</rules>
<output_contract>
1. Test file {{test_path}} ({{test_framework}}), runnable as-is.
2. Pre-fix failure note: which assertion fails against the vulnerable code and the expected vs actual line.
3. Run evidence: paste the test run output verbatim showing green against current code.
4. Prevention note for our LESSONS.md: one line on the root-cause class and the code-review question that would have caught it.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- At least one assertion demonstrably fails against the pre-fix code (explained, or shown if I paste the old version).
- Legitimate-access control case included and passing.
- Verbatim test-run output provided as evidence.
</acceptance_criteria>
<fix>{{paste the merged fix diff verbatim}}</fix>
<endpoint_code>{{paste the current endpoint code verbatim}}</endpoint_code>
prompts.expectedOutput: Targeted regression test with bypass variant and control case, verbatim green-run evidence, and a LESSONS.md prevention note.

prompts.title: STRIDE Threat Model for a New Feature
prompts.description: Facilitate a STRIDE threat-modeling session for a planned feature, producing a component-by-component threat matrix with mitigations and acceptance gates.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A STRIDE threat model for the {{feature, e.g. 'public file-sharing links'}} feature we are about to build into my own {{system}}.</goal>
<rationale>Retrofitting security after build costs us 10x; I want threats enumerated and mitigation ownership assigned while the design is still changeable.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Defensive threat modeling of my own system.
- Describe threats concretely enough to prioritize and mitigate — abuse cases, not exploitation instructions.
- Scope: {{scope, e.g. 'link creation, access, and revocation flows'}}. Out of scope: {{out_of_scope}}. Threats against out-of-scope components go in a PARKING-LOT list, not the matrix.
</boundaries>
</task>
<process>
First, from my description below, reconstruct: components, data stores, external actors, and trust boundaries (numbered TB1..TBn). If the description is insufficient for any boundary, ask me up to 5 clarifying questions BEFORE producing the matrix — do not guess architecture.
Then enumerate threats per component per STRIDE category. Skip a cell only with a one-word justification ('no state', 'no authz decision'); no checklist theater.
</process>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Rate everything High: each threat's likelihood/impact must be justified against MY architecture ({{architecture_brief}}) and data sensitivity ({{data_sensitivity}}).
- Propose mitigations that don't map to a specific threat row, or that we demonstrably already have (I list existing controls below — read them first).
DO:
- Mark each threat: existing control (cite it), mitigation needed (concrete, minimal), or accepted risk (only if Low and I confirm).
</rules>
<output_contract>
1. Architecture summary + trust boundary list (TB1..TBn).
2. STRIDE matrix: | Component | S | T | R | I | D | E | — each non-empty cell: threat in one sentence.
3. Threat register: | ID | Component | STRIDE | Threat | Likelihood | Impact | Justification | Existing control / Mitigation | Owner | Verification test |
4. Top 3 design changes ranked by risk-reduction-per-effort, with the deciding reasoning.
5. PARKING-LOT list for out-of-scope observations.
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every matrix cell either contains a concrete threat or a skip justification.
- Every likelihood/impact rating carries a one-line justification.
- Top-3 list ordered by risk-reduction-per-effort, not severity alone.
</acceptance_criteria>
<description>{{feature description, data flows, and existing security controls, verbatim}}</description>
prompts.expectedOutput: Trust-boundary map, STRIDE matrix with skip justifications, justified threat register with mitigations/owners, top-3 design changes, and parking lot.

prompts.title: Lightweight Threat Model Check for an Architecture Change
prompts.description: A fast, repeatable threat-model pass for small architecture changes (new endpoint, new third-party integration, new data flow) — the 15-minute version of a full STRIDE session.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>A rapid threat assessment of a proposed change to my own system: {{change, e.g. 'adding a webhook receiver that GitHub will POST to'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Full threat-modeling sessions don't scale to every change; I need a lightweight gate that catches the 80% case — new trust boundaries and new attacker-reachable surface — before this merges.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Defensive review of my own system; abuse cases only, no exploitation instructions.
- This is a screen, not a full STRIDE model: if the change crosses a trust boundary you cannot assess from what I provide, say ESCALATE and name the missing information instead of guessing.
</boundaries>
</task>
<questions>
Answer these for the change, citing my description or marking UNKNOWN:
1. New attack surface: what new input does this expose to whom (unauthenticated internet? authenticated users? a third party)?
2. New trust boundary: does data cross from a less-trusted to a more-trusted zone, and is it validated at the boundary (at what file/function)?
3. New credentials/permissions: what secret or privilege does the change require, where is it stored, and what is its blast radius if leaked?
4. New failure mode: what breaks security-wise when this component is down, slow, or replayed (idempotency, retry storms, fail-open defaults)?
5. Abuse case: the single most likely way {{attacker_profile, e.g. 'an unauthenticated internet actor'}} abuses this, in two sentences max.
</questions>
<rules>
DO NOT:
- Pad: if a question's honest answer is 'no new risk', say exactly that with the reason — do not manufacture threats to fill the row.
- Propose mitigations for threats you rated negligible.
DO:
- Rate residual risk LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH with justification, and give the minimal mitigation for anything above LOW.
</rules>
<output_contract>
| Question | Answer (evidence or UNKNOWN) | Risk | Minimal mitigation (if > LOW) |
Then: one-line verdict — PROCEED / PROCEED-WITH-MITIGATIONS / ESCALATE (to full threat model, with the missing info named).
</output_contract>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every answer cites my description or is marked UNKNOWN.
- 'No new risk' answers allowed and justified; no manufactured threats.
- ESCALATE verdicts name the exact missing information.
</acceptance_criteria>
<change_description>{{describe the change, the components it touches, and any new external parties, verbatim}}</change_description>
prompts.expectedOutput: Five-question evidence-cited risk table with minimal mitigations and a PROCEED / PROCEED-WITH-MITIGATIONS / ESCALATE verdict.

prompts.title: Vitest unit tests for a pure utility module (AAA, behavior-first)
prompts.description: Generates a behavior-focused Vitest suite for an existing pure utility function or module, with strict anti-tautology rules and a runnable acceptance gate.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>{{source_file}} has a complete Vitest unit-test suite covering its documented behavior, including edge cases, in {{test_file_path (e.g. src/utils/date.test.ts)}}.</goal>
<rationale>These utilities sit on hot paths ({{where used}}); regressions here surface far downstream and are expensive to trace.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT modify {{source_file}} or any production code. If the tests reveal a bug, report it in a "Notes" section - do NOT fix it.
- Do NOT add dependencies; use the Vitest version already installed.
- Do NOT create files other than the one test file listed below.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>One Vitest test file, runnable with the project's existing config.</deliverable>
<files>{{test_file_path}}</files>
<format>TypeScript, Vitest (describe/it/expect). Each test uses Arrange-Act-Assert with a blank line between phases. describe blocks named after the unit under test; it() names state observable behavior ("returns empty array when input has no matches"), not implementation.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every public export of {{source_file}} has at least one behavioral test.
- Edge cases covered: {{list, e.g. empty input, boundary values, invalid input, locale/Unicode}}.
- Every test asserts a returned value, thrown error, or observable state change - never merely that the code ran.
- `npx vitest run {{test_file_path}}` passes; paste the verbatim summary output.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT:
- Mock the unit under test or any part of it.
- Write snapshot-only assertions (expect(...).toMatchSnapshot() with no explicit expect).
- Assert on internal call counts or private helpers.
- Duplicate the same assertion under renamed tests to inflate coverage.
DO:
- Follow the test style already present in {{reference_test_file}} (imports, naming, helpers).
- Prefer one focused assertion per test; use test.each for input/output tables.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A single Vitest test file with AAA-structured behavioral tests, plus verbatim `vitest run` output proving the suite passes and a Notes section for any discovered bugs.

prompts.title: React component tests with Testing Library (user-visible behavior only)
prompts.description: Writes Testing Library tests for a React component that assert what a user sees and does, with hard bans on implementation-detail testing.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>{{component_path}} has a Testing Library test suite that locks in its user-visible contract: rendering, interaction, and the states {{states, e.g. loading / empty / error / success}}.</goal>
<rationale>The component is being refactored soon ({{reason}}); tests that assert behavior instead of internals let the refactor proceed without rewriting the suite.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT modify the component or its children; render it as-is.
- Do NOT add dependencies beyond the already-installed @testing-library/react, @testing-library/user-event, and vitest.
- Do NOT create more than the single test file below.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>One test file proving the component's user-facing behavior.</deliverable>
<files>{{test_file_path (e.g. {{component_name}}.test.tsx, colocated)}}</files>
<format>TypeScript + Vitest + Testing Library. Arrange-Act-Assert per test. Query with screen.getByRole / getByLabelText / getByText in that preference order; drive interaction with await userEvent.setup() methods; async UI asserted with findBy* or waitFor.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each state in {{states}} is rendered and asserted from the user's perspective (visible text, enabled/disabled controls, ARIA attributes).
- Every interactive element listed in {{interactions, e.g. submit button, cancel link}} has at least one interaction test asserting its observable outcome.
- Zero assertions on component state, props passed to children, DOM class names, or snapshot output.
- `npx vitest run {{test_file_path}}` passes; paste verbatim output.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT:
- Use container.querySelector, testids (unless no accessible query exists - justify in a comment), or rerender-to-inspect tricks.
- Mock the component under test; mock only its external boundaries ({{allowed mocks, e.g. fetch via MSW, router}}).
- Assert that a mock "was called" as the sole proof of behavior - pair it with a visible outcome.
DO:
- Match conventions in {{reference_test_file}}.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: One colocated .test.tsx file asserting rendering, states, and interactions through accessible queries, with verbatim passing vitest output.

prompts.title: pytest suite for a service class with injected collaborators
prompts.description: Generates pytest unit tests for a Python service whose dependencies are injected, mocking only boundary collaborators and parameterizing behavior tables.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>{{service_module}} (class {{service_class}}) has a pytest suite covering each public method's contract: happy path, domain error cases, and collaborator-failure propagation.</goal>
<rationale>{{service_class}} orchestrates {{domain, e.g. billing retries}}; its branching logic is where money-affecting bugs would hide.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT modify {{service_module}}. Bugs found go in a "Notes" section only.
- Do NOT add dependencies; use pytest (already installed, version in pyproject.toml).
- Must preserve: the suite must run in under {{budget, e.g. 2 seconds}} - no I/O, no sleeps, no network.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>One pytest module unit-testing {{service_class}} in isolation.</deliverable>
<files>{{test_file_path (e.g. tests/unit/test_{{service}}.py)}}</files>
<format>pytest style: plain functions, Arrange-Act-Assert separated by blank lines, fixtures for repeated collaborator setup, @pytest.mark.parametrize for input/expected tables. Collaborators replaced with unittest.mock.Mock(spec={{collaborator_class}}) or hand-written fakes; the service under test is always the real instance.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>

- Each test asserts return values, raised exceptions (pytest.raises with match=), or observable calls on collaborators that change outcomes - never coverage-only calls.

</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT:
- Patch or mock {{service_class}} itself, its private methods, or anything inside the unit under test.
- Use @patch with string import paths when constructor injection is available.
- Write tests that only assert mock.call_count without asserting the resulting behavior.
DO:

</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A pytest module with parametrized behavioral tests per public method, real-instance service with mocked collaborators only, and verbatim passing pytest output.

prompts.title: Edge-case hunt: adversarial unit tests for a tricky pure function
prompts.description: Asks the model to attack a pure function's input space systematically - partition table first, then tests - to expose hidden defects rather than confirm happy paths.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Produce an adversarial Vitest suite for {{function_signature}} in {{source_file}} that maximizes the chance of exposing a real defect, not the chance of passing.</goal>
<rationale>Existing tests cover only the happy path; this function handles {{risky domain, e.g. date math / money rounding / Unicode}} where edge-case bugs are the norm.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT modify {{source_file}}. Every suspected bug is reported in a "Findings" section with the failing input and expected-vs-actual - do NOT fix anything.
- Do NOT add dependencies. Property-based testing is allowed only if fast-check is already installed (verify with `npm ls fast-check` first); otherwise use explicit cases.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>An input-partition analysis followed by one test file.</deliverable>
<files>{{test_file_path}}</files>
<format>First, a partition table in a comment at the top of the test file: input category | representative values | expected behavior. Then Vitest tests, one per partition row minimum, AAA structure. Where a property holds for all inputs (e.g. "output never exceeds input length"), express it as a property test if the library is available.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Partitions include at minimum: empty/absent input, single element, boundary values ({{boundaries_list, e.g. 0, -1, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER}}), malformed input, and {{domain_specific, e.g. DST transitions / surrogate pairs / negative zero}}.
- Every test asserts a concrete expected value or invariant - no expect(result).toBeDefined()-style non-assertions.
- The suite runs with `npx vitest run {{test_file_path}}`; paste verbatim output. Failing tests that expose genuine defects stay failing and are listed under "Findings".
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT weaken an assertion to make a test pass. DO NOT mock the function under test. DO state, for each failing test, whether you believe the code or your expectation is wrong, and why.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A partition-table-driven test file targeting boundaries and malformed inputs, verbatim run output, and a Findings list of any genuine defects left failing.

prompts.title: Integration tests for HTTP API route handlers against a real test database
prompts.description: Builds request-level integration tests for API handlers that exercise routing, validation, persistence, and serialization together against a real database.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>The endpoints {{route_list, e.g. POST /api/orders, GET /api/orders/:id}} have integration tests that send real HTTP requests through the framework stack and verify both the response and the resulting database state.</goal>

- Do NOT mock the database, the ORM, or the route handlers - that would defeat the purpose. Mocking is allowed only for {{external services, e.g. the payment gateway / email sender}} at its outermost client.

</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>Integration test file(s) plus any required seed/teardown helper.</deliverable>
<files>
- {{test_file_path, e.g. tests/integration/orders.api.test.ts}}
- {{helper_path, e.g. tests/helpers/db.ts (only if seeding requires it)}}
</files>
<format>{{framework_stack, e.g. Vitest + supertest against the exported Express app / Next.js route handlers invoked via Request}}. Each test: Arrange (seed known rows) -> Act (real request) -> Assert (status, JSON body shape, and rows actually written). Database reset between tests via {{reset_strategy, e.g. truncation in afterEach / wrapping transaction rollback}}.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Per endpoint: success case, each documented validation failure ({{status_codes, e.g. 400/422}}), auth/permission rejection, and not-found case.
- At least one test asserts the persisted database row, not just the HTTP response.
- No test depends on another test's leftovers; running with {{shuffle/isolation flag}} passes.
- `{{test_command}}` passes; paste verbatim output including timing.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>

</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: Integration tests issuing real HTTP requests with DB-state assertions, isolated reset strategy, verbatim passing output, and a Findings section for app bugs uncovered.

prompts.title: Frontend-backend contract integration tests via MSW from the OpenAPI spec

<rationale>The frontend and backend teams drift: the UI currently assumes fields ({{examples, e.g. `order.discountTotal`}}) that the API renamed; only contract-derived mocks make that drift a failing test instead of a production bug.</rationale>

<contract>

- {{test_file_path}}
</files>
<format>TypeScript + Vitest + Testing Library + msw (http.get/http.post with HttpResponse). Handlers typed/validated against the OpenAPI schema via {{approach, e.g. generated types / runtime schema parse}}. Tests render the full feature (no shallow rendering) and assert user-visible outcomes; server errors simulated with MSW error responses and asserted as visible error states.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every response body in a handler validates against the spec schema - a handler returning off-contract data fails its own test.
- Each flow in {{flows}} asserts at least one user-visible result, not merely that a request fired.

</rules>

prompts.title: First Playwright end-to-end test for a critical user flow

<rationale>This flow is the revenue/onboarding path; it has broken silently {{frequency, e.g. twice this quarter}} and nothing currently catches it before users do.</rationale>

- Do NOT add dependencies beyond @playwright/test (already configured in {{playwright_config_path}}).

</task>

<files>{{spec_path, e.g. e2e/{{flow-name}}.spec.ts}}</files>

Seed any required data via {{seed_mechanism, e.g. the existing API helper / test account}}, never via UI setup steps unrelated to the flow.</format>

prompts.title: Authenticated E2E matrix: role, state, and failure-path coverage
