prompts.title: Flake audit: stabilize an existing E2E suite with evidence
prompts.description: Diagnoses and fixes flakiness in an existing Playwright/Cypress suite by classifying root causes, applying minimal per-test fixes, and proving stability with repeated runs.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>The {{suite, e.g. e2e/ directory}} suite's flaky tests ({{flake_list_or_report, e.g. the 8 failures in last week's CI report}}) are diagnosed by root cause and stabilized with minimal diffs.</goal>
<rationale>The team now ignores E2E failures entirely - a suite that cries wolf is worse than no suite because real regressions get dismissed as flakes.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT rewrite specs wholesale; one bounded fix per test, reviewable as a small diff.
- Do NOT raise timeouts globally, add blanket retries, or wrap assertions in poll-until-pass loops - those hide causes instead of fixing them.
- Do NOT modify application code. If a flake traces to an app race condition, report it under "Findings" with the trace artifact and quarantine the test instead of fixing the app.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A root-cause table plus minimal per-test fixes.</deliverable>
<files>{{spec_files_touched - list explicitly}}</files>
<format>First output: a table | test | observed failure (from CI log) | root-cause class (hard wait / shared state / order dependence / animation timing / test-data collision / app race) | fix applied |. Then the diffs. Fixes use the framework's auto-waiting primitives ({{runner, e.g. Playwright web-first expect / Cypress retry-ability via cy.get().should()}}) and per-test data isolation.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every fixed test passes {{stability_gate, e.g. 10 consecutive local runs via `npx playwright test --repeat-each=10`}}; paste the verbatim final summary.
- Root-cause class is stated for every test; any test you could not stabilize is explicitly listed as QUARANTINED with its evidence, not silently deleted.
- No test lost an assertion during stabilization - if an assertion had to change, justify why the old one tested timing rather than behavior.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
Work from verbatim CI output and traces (paste the implicated error per test), never from paraphrased descriptions. On any fix attempt that fails, paste the exact new error and apply the smallest correction - do not rewrite the spec.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A root-cause classification table, small per-test diffs using auto-waiting primitives, verbatim repeat-run evidence of stability, and an explicit quarantine list for unfixable app races.

prompts.title: TDD gate: failing test first for new business logic
prompts.description: The signature two-phase gate: phase 1 delivers only a failing test with the failing assertion pasted verbatim; implementation is forbidden until the human confirms.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>The behavior {{behavior_spec, e.g. 'applying a percentage discount never reduces a line total below zero'}} is implemented test-first: a failing test exists and is verified failing before any implementation is written.</goal>
<rationale>Tests written after implementation tend to ratify whatever the code does (fake coverage). Forcing the red phase first proves the test can actually fail, so green later means something.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- PHASE 1 (this response): write ONLY the test in {{test_file_path}}. Do NOT create or modify any implementation file - not even a stub beyond what the test needs to compile/run.
- Do NOT touch {{off_limits, e.g. other modules, config, fixtures outside the test file}}.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>Phase 1: one failing test file plus evidence of failure. Phase 2 (only after I reply "confirmed"): the minimal implementation that turns exactly these tests green.</deliverable>
<files>Phase 1: {{test_file_path}} only. Phase 2: {{implementation_file_path}} only.</files>
<format>{{stack, e.g. TypeScript + Vitest / pytest}}. Arrange-Act-Assert; test names state the behavior from the spec, not the function you expect to write.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
Phase 1:
- The test encodes every rule in {{behavior_spec}}, including the edge cases {{edge_cases}}.
- Run `{{test_command}}` and paste the failing assertion output verbatim. Acceptable failure: assertion mismatch or not-yet-implemented error. NOT acceptable: syntax errors, import typos, or a test that fails for a reason unrelated to the missing behavior - fix the test if so.
Phase 2 (after my confirmation):
- Implement the smallest change that makes the new tests pass.
- Run the FULL suite and paste the result; no previously green test may regress.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT show me implementation code in Phase 1. DO stop after Phase 1 and wait - do not proceed on your own. If {{behavior_spec}} is ambiguous or contradictory, say so and list the interpretations instead of guessing.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: Phase 1: a behavior-named failing test plus verbatim failing assertion; then, only on confirmation, Phase 2: minimal implementation with full-suite green output.

prompts.title: Regression-gate: reproduce a bug as a failing test before the fix
prompts.description: Converts a bug report into a failing regression test first (with verbatim bug evidence), then the smallest fix, proving both directions: red before, green after.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>The bug {{bug_summary}} is locked in by a regression test that fails on the current code, followed by the smallest fix that makes it pass - so this exact bug can never silently return.</goal>
<rationale>Without a test that fails before the fix and passes after, there is no proof the fix addresses the actual defect rather than coincidentally changing behavior.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Phase 1 (this response): reproduce with a failing test only; do NOT modify implementation code.
- Phase 2 (after I confirm the red): the minimal fix in {{implementation_files}} - no refactoring, no drive-by cleanup.
- If you discover adjacent bugs, list them under "Notes" but do NOT fix them.
</boundaries>
</task>

<bug_report>
<environment>{{runtime / framework / dependency versions - pinned}}</environment>
<observed>{{verbatim error, log, or wrong behavior}}</observed>
<expected>{{correct behavior}}</expected>
<implicated_code>{{file(s) or snippet, unedited}}</implicated_code>
</bug_report>

<contract>
<deliverable>Phase 1: one regression test demonstrating the bug. Phase 2: minimal fix.</deliverable>
<files>Phase 1: {{test_file_path}}. Phase 2: {{implementation_files}} only.</files>
<format>{{stack, e.g. pytest / Vitest}}. The test name references the bug (e.g. test_{{slug}}_regression) and asserts the expected behavior from <bug_report>, not the current wrong behavior.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Phase 1: `{{test_command}}` fails for exactly the reason in <observed>; paste the failing output verbatim. If it fails differently, your reproduction is wrong - iterate on the test, not the code.
- Phase 2: the new test passes AND the full suite passes; paste both outputs. The diff is limited to {{implementation_files}}.
- State the root cause in one sentence, distinguishing it from downstream symptoms; if the fix touches more than ~{{line_budget, e.g. 15}} lines, justify why no smaller fix exists.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT paraphrase the error - work from the verbatim evidence above. DO NOT skip the red phase even if the fix looks obvious.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A failing regression test with verbatim red output, a minimal confined fix, full-suite green evidence, a one-sentence root cause, and a Notes list of adjacent issues left untouched.

prompts.title: Context-isolated TDD loop: spec-only test writer + adversarial verifier
prompts.description: An orchestration template where tests are written from the spec in an isolated context (no implementation knowledge), then a fresh verifier proves tests assert the spec, not the code.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>The feature defined in {{spec_path, e.g. SPEC.md}} is built through a gated TDD loop where test design and implementation never share context, and an independent verifier confirms the tests encode the spec rather than the implementation.</goal>
<rationale>When the same context writes tests and code, tests drift toward ratifying the implementation (fake coverage). Isolating the test writer and adversarially verifying the suite closes that hole for this high-stakes module ({{stakes, e.g. billing / authz}}).</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Agents A and V receive ONLY {{spec_path}} - never the implementation diff or this conversation.
- No agent may weaken or delete a test to reach green; a legitimately wrong test is fixed by reference to the spec, with the spec section quoted.
- Implementation scope: {{implementation_files}} only.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A complete red-green-verified cycle for the behaviors in {{spec_path}} section {{section}}.</deliverable>
<files>Tests: {{test_files}}. Implementation: {{implementation_files}}. Verifier report: returned in-conversation (no file).</files>
<format>Agent A (fresh context, spec only): writes failing tests per spec behavior; reports each failing assertion verbatim. Main agent: implements the minimal change to green; runs full suite. Agent V (fresh context, spec + test files only, NO implementation): adversarial review with an assume-the-tests-are-wrong stance.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- A's report contains verbatim failing assertions proving a real red phase.
- Full suite green after implementation; verbatim summary pasted.
- V returns a coverage matrix: | spec requirement | COVERED / PARTIAL / MISSING | test name + quoted assertion |. Any PARTIAL/MISSING loops back to A before the feature is marked done.
- V explicitly flags any test that would pass against a trivially wrong implementation (e.g. tautological or mock-echoing assertions).
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT let implementation details leak into A's or V's brief. DO halt and report if A and V disagree on what the spec means - that is a spec defect, not a test defect.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A three-role cycle: verbatim red-phase evidence from an isolated test writer, minimal green implementation, and an adversarial requirement-coverage matrix flagging tautological tests, looping until clean.

prompts.title: Test-data factories with safe defaults and overrides
prompts.description: Replaces copy-pasted fixture blobs with composable factory functions (or pytest fixtures) producing valid-by-default entities with per-test overrides.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Tests for {{domain_entities, e.g. User, Order, Invoice}} create their data through factory functions ({{factory_file_path}}) that return valid-by-default entities and accept per-test overrides - replacing the inline object literals currently duplicated across {{test_files}}.</goal>
<rationale>Duplicated literals make every schema change a 40-file edit and hide which fields each test actually cares about; factories make the relevant field the only one mentioned.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT modify production code or the assertions in existing tests; only how test data is constructed.
- Do NOT add a factory library dependency; plain functions (or pytest fixtures/factory pattern) are enough.
- Do NOT introduce randomness: defaults are deterministic; uniqueness comes from an internal counter, not Math.random/uuid.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A factory module plus the listed test files migrated to use it.</deliverable>
<files>
- {{factory_file_path, e.g. tests/factories.ts}}
- {{test_files to migrate}}
</files>
<format>{{language, e.g. TypeScript: `createUser(overrides?: Partial<User>): User` with an incrementing sequence for unique fields; Python: pytest fixtures wrapping a build() function}}. Defaults must satisfy the entity's invariants ({{invariants, e.g. email format, non-negative totals}}) so a no-argument call always yields a valid object.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each migrated test mentions only the fields it asserts on; everything else comes from the factory.
- Two calls to the same factory never produce colliding unique fields.
- Full suite `{{test_command}}` passes with zero assertion changes; paste verbatim summary.
- No test constructs {{domain_entities}} inline anymore (verify by search and report the command + result).
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT let factories silently build invalid states for convenience - invalid states are built via explicit overrides in the tests that need them. DO follow naming/layout of {{reference_test_file}}.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A deterministic factory module, migrated test files where each test names only asserted fields, verbatim full-suite green output, and a search proving no inline construction remains.

prompts.title: Deterministic fixtures: seeded fakes, frozen time, stable ordering
prompts.description: Removes nondeterminism from a test suite's data layer - seeded generators, frozen clocks, explicit ordering - and proves it with repeated and shuffled runs.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>The test suite in {{scope, e.g. tests/ or e2e/}} produces identical results on every run: all generated data is seeded, all time is frozen or injected, and no assertion depends on incidental ordering.</goal>
<rationale>Intermittent failures traced to unseeded generators and real clocks ({{examples, e.g. faker output, Date.now() comparisons, DST boundary failures}}) are eroding trust in CI.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT modify production code. If production code cannot be tested deterministically (e.g. time read deep inside a module), report it under "Findings" - do NOT refactor it in this task.
- Do NOT delete or weaken assertions to make runs pass; change only how data/time are controlled.
- Do NOT add dependencies unless listed here: {{allowed, e.g. none / @faker-js/faker already installed}}.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A determinism pass over the suite plus evidence of stable repetition and order-independence.</deliverable>
<files>{{files_touched - list explicitly; expected: shared setup/fixture files and the offending tests}}</files>
<format>Faker (if used) seeded once in {{setup_file}} with a fixed seed; time controlled via {{mechanism, e.g. vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.setSystemTime / freezegun / injected clock}}; unordered collections asserted with order-insensitive matchers (expect.arrayContaining / sorted comparison) or the query explicitly ORDER BY.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- `{{test_command}}` passes {{repeat_count, e.g. 10}} consecutive runs - paste the final summary verbatim.
- The suite passes under shuffled order ({{shuffle_command, e.g. pytest -p randomly / vitest --sequence.shuffle}}); paste output.
- A grep/search report shows no remaining unseeded randomness or bare real-clock reads in tests (paste the search command + result).
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
DO NOT freeze time globally in a way that breaks timeout/retry logic in integration tests - scope fake timers per test. DO list any test whose flakiness you could NOT attribute to data/time/ordering under "Open" rather than forcing a fix.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: Seeded generators and scoped clock control, verbatim evidence of 10 stable runs plus a shuffled-order pass, a search report of remaining nondeterminism, and Findings/Open lists for anything out of scope.

prompts.title: Coverage-gap triage: from coverage report to risk-ranked test backlog
prompts.description: Turns a raw coverage report into a risk x change-frequency backlog of tests worth writing, explicitly rejecting percentage-chasing and coverage theater.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Convert the coverage report {{coverage_report_path, e.g. coverage/lcov-report or coverage.xml}} into a prioritized backlog of the highest-value missing tests for {{system_scope}}, ranked by risk rather than by what would raise the percentage fastest.</goal>
<rationale>Coverage is currently {{current_state, e.g. 61% and rising via trivial getter tests}}; the number is improving while the genuinely dangerous paths ({{known_risks, e.g. payment retry logic, permission checks}}) stay untested.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT write any tests in this task - analysis and backlog only.
- Do NOT recommend tests for trivial code (getters, pass-through wrappers, config) even though they raise coverage cheaply.
- Do NOT set or endorse a global coverage-percentage target; the goal is risk reduction, not a number.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A ranked test backlog as a strategy matrix.</deliverable>
<files>No files. Return the matrix in-conversation.</files>
<format>A table: | rank | module/function | uncovered behavior (from the report) | failure impact (data loss / security / money / UX) | change frequency (from {{churn_source, e.g. git log --since=6m}}) | risk x churn score | proposed test layer (unit / integration / e2e) | one-line behavioral assertion it should make |. Top {{n, e.g. 10}} rows only, plus a short "Explicitly not testing" list with reasons.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every row cites concrete evidence: the uncovered lines/branch from the report and the churn data - no vibes-based ranking.
- Each row names a behavioral assertion that could actually fail, not "add tests for X".
- Known-risk areas {{known_risks}} each appear or are explicitly explained as already-covered (quote the covering test).
- The "not testing" list demonstrates deliberate exclusion of low-value code.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
If the coverage report or churn data is missing/unparseable, stop and say what you need rather than inventing numbers. DO flag any place where coverage data looks misleading (e.g. lines covered by tests that assert nothing) - covered-but-untested code is part of the gap.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: A risk x churn ranked matrix of the top missing tests with evidence per row, proposed layer and concrete assertion per item, an explicit not-testing list, and flags for covered-but-unasserted code.

prompts.title: Test strategy for a new feature: layer allocation with tradeoffs
prompts.description: Plans where each behavior of a new feature should be tested (unit / integration / e2e) using an options-and-tradeoffs comparison, producing a binding strategy before any test is written.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Before any test code is written for {{feature, e.g. 'team workspaces with role-based invites'}}, produce a test strategy that allocates every behavior in the spec to exactly one primary test layer, with the tradeoffs made explicit.</goal>
<rationale>Previous features ended up with duplicated e2e coverage of logic that unit tests would catch faster, and zero integration coverage where the seams actually break ({{past_failure, e.g. the invite-email transaction bug}}). Layer choice is an architecture decision and should be made deliberately.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT write test code in this task - strategy only.
- Do NOT default to "e2e everything" or "unit everything"; each layer earns its rows.
- Respect existing infrastructure: {{available_infra, e.g. Vitest + testcontainers + Playwright already in CI; no visual-regression tooling}}.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A strategy document returned in-conversation, ready to gate implementation.</deliverable>
<files>No files. (Optionally append to {{strategy_doc_path}} only if I confirm.)</files>
<format>Part 1 - compare 2-3 allocation approaches (e.g. pyramid-heavy vs integration-heavy vs e2e-heavy) for this feature: pros, cons, how each fails, then a decision matrix weighted by {{criteria, e.g. CI runtime budget, failure blast radius, team size}} and one recommendation with the deciding criterion. Part 2 - the allocation table: | behavior (from spec) | primary layer | why this layer catches its failure mode | what is deliberately NOT covered elsewhere |.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every behavior in {{spec_or_story_list}} appears exactly once in Part 2 - no orphans, no double-counting.
- Each e2e row justifies why a lower layer cannot catch that failure (e2e rows without justification are a red flag).
- The strategy names its own risks: what class of bug could still ship even if the plan is followed perfectly.
- Estimated CI runtime added is stated per layer against the budget {{runtime_budget}}.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>

<rules>
Push back if my criteria or budget make the recommended allocation incoherent - say so explicitly rather than smoothing it over. If the spec is missing behaviors a tester would expect ({{examples, e.g. concurrent invites, expired tokens}}), list them as spec gaps before allocating.
</rules>
prompts.expectedOutput: An options-and-tradeoffs comparison with a weighted decision matrix and recommendation, a complete behavior-to-layer allocation table with justifications, residual-risk analysis, and CI runtime estimates per layer.

prompts.title: Extract Design Tokens from Legacy Styles into CSS Custom Properties
prompts.description: Scans a component or stylesheet for hard-coded visual values and consolidates them into a named CSS custom-property token layer with a documented token table.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Replace hard-coded visual values in {{target_files}} with CSS custom properties defined in {{tokens_file}}, so {{surface_or_component}} derives all color, spacing, radius, and typography from one token layer.</goal>
<rationale>Hard-coded values drift apart over time; a token layer is the prerequisite for theming, dark mode, and consistent spacing. This change must be purely mechanical: zero visual difference after the refactor.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT change any visual value (no rounding, no "improvements" to spacing or color).
- Do NOT touch files outside {{target_files}} and {{tokens_file}}.
- Do NOT rename selectors, reorder rules, or reformat unrelated code.
- Do NOT add a build step, preprocessor, or dependency.
- If two hard-coded values look similar but differ (e.g. #334155 vs #334158), keep them as separate tokens and flag the near-duplicate in Notes - do NOT merge them yourself.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) Updated {{tokens_file}} with a :root token block. 2) Updated {{target_files}} where every hard-coded value is replaced by var(--token-name). 3) A token table in your reply.</deliverable>
<format>Token table columns: Token name | Value | Used in (selectors) | Source value replaced. Naming: --{{prefix}}-{category}-{scale-step}, e.g. --{{prefix}}-color-surface-1, --{{prefix}}-space-4.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every color, spacing, radius, and font-size literal in {{target_files}} maps to exactly one token (grep shows no remaining hex/px literals in the four token categories except inside {{tokens_file}}; whitelisted structural values outside those categories — e.g. 1px borders, z-index, media-query breakpoints — may remain and are listed in Notes).
- Rendered output is pixel-identical: no computed value changed.
- Token names follow the stated convention; no token is defined but unused.
- Notes section lists any near-duplicate values and any value you could not classify as DECISION NEEDED instead of guessing intent.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A :root token block, refactored stylesheets using var() references, and a token table (Token name | Value | Used in | Source value) plus a Notes list of near-duplicates and DECISION NEEDED items.

prompts.title: Choose a Design Token Architecture (Primitive / Semantic / Component Tiers)
prompts.description: Options-and-tradeoffs prompt for deciding how many token tiers a design system needs and how they map to CSS custom properties or Tailwind theme tokens before any code is written.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Recommend a token architecture for {{product_name}}: how many tiers (primitive / semantic / component), how they reference each other, and how they surface in {{stack, e.g. 'CSS custom properties + Tailwind theme'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Token architecture is expensive to change once components consume it; the decision must be made against our real constraints, not a generic best practice.</rationale>
<context>Team: {{team_size_and_frontend_experience}}. Brands/themes: {{number_of_themes, e.g. 'light+dark, one brand'}}. Consumers: {{component_count_and_platforms}}. Existing: {{current_state, e.g. 'scattered hex values, Tailwind default palette'}}.</context>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT write the token files yet - this is a decision deliverable only.
- Do NOT assume we need three tiers by default; a two-tier or single-tier system is a valid answer if our scale justifies it.
- Do NOT invent requirements; if a deciding fact is missing (e.g. whether white-labeling is on the roadmap), mark it DECISION NEEDED and say how the answer changes either way.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A comparison of 2-3 viable architectures, a weighted decision matrix, and one recommendation.</deliverable>
<format>For each option: tier structure, an example chain (e.g. --blue-500 -> --color-surface-brand -> button background), pros, cons, and how it fails (what breaks at 2x themes or 5x components). Decision matrix weighted by: {{criteria, e.g. 'team size 30%, theming needs 40%, migration cost 30%'}}.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Exactly one recommendation, with the single criterion that decided it named explicitly.
- Each option's failure mode is concrete, not generic ("hard to maintain" is not acceptable).
- Recommendation accounts for dark mode and states (hover/disabled) living at the semantic tier, not the primitive tier.
- Migration cost from {{current_state}} is estimated per option.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: 2-3 token architecture options with example reference chains, pros/cons/failure modes, a criteria-weighted decision matrix, one recommendation with its deciding criterion, and DECISION NEEDED flags for missing facts.

prompts.title: Bulk Token Migration Across a Component Library
prompts.description: Plans and executes a large-scale migration of many components to a new token naming scheme using anchored diffs, a per-file manifest, and an explicit must-preserve invariant list.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Migrate all components under {{components_dir}} from the old token names ({{old_scheme, e.g. '--color-primary, --gray-100'}}) to the new scheme defined in {{new_tokens_file}}, with zero visual or behavioral change.</goal>
<rationale>The token rename unblocks {{reason, e.g. 'multi-brand theming'}}; doing it file-by-file by hand is error-prone, so the migration needs a machine-checkable plan and per-file evidence.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- MUST PRESERVE: every computed visual value, every selector, all public class names, and all component APIs.
- Do NOT touch files outside {{components_dir}}; do NOT create new components; do NOT 'fix' unrelated styling you notice - list such findings in Notes instead.
- Do NOT regenerate whole files from scratch; express each edit as an anchored change against the existing content so the diff stays reviewable.
- If a file references a token with no equivalent in {{new_tokens_file}}, do NOT invent a mapping - flag it DECISION NEEDED and skip that declaration.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) A migration manifest: JSON array of {path, action, tokenMappings, status}. 2) The per-file edits as anchored search/replace blocks (FILE / ANCHOR / replacement). 3) A completion report.</deliverable>
<format>Manifest first, then edits grouped per file, then report.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Manifest covers every file under {{components_dir}} that references an old token; count stated and verified by grep.
- After edits, `grep -r '{{old_token_pattern}}' {{components_dir}}` returns zero matches (paste the command and its output).
- {{build_or_test_command}} passes; paste verbatim output.
- Completion report table: Check | Status | Evidence; any unverified check is marked NOT VERIFIED, not asserted.
- Notes lists skipped DECISION NEEDED declarations and any out-of-scope issues found.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A JSON migration manifest, anchored per-file edit blocks, and an evidence-backed completion report proving zero remaining old-token references and a passing build.

prompts.title: Make a Single Component Responsive with a Breakpoint Behavior Spec
prompts.description: Converts a fixed-width component into a responsive one by first defining per-breakpoint behavior, then implementing it with the project's existing styling approach.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Make {{component_name}} in {{file_path}} usable and correctly laid out at {{breakpoint_set, e.g. 'mobile <640px, tablet 640-1024px, desktop >1024px'}}.</goal>
<rationale>The component currently {{current_problem, e.g. 'overflows horizontally below 640px'}}, which blocks {{user_impact}}.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Fix ONLY {{component_name}} and its direct children; do NOT restyle sibling components or global layout.
- Do NOT introduce pixel values that are not already in the project's spacing scale ({{spacing_source, e.g. 'Tailwind spacing scale / --space-* tokens'}}).
- Do NOT add dependencies; use {{styling_approach, e.g. 'Tailwind responsive prefixes'}} consistent with {{reference_component}}.
- Do NOT hide content on mobile unless the spec below says so; if the design intent for a breakpoint is not given, flag it DECISION NEEDED rather than guessing.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) A breakpoint behavior spec BEFORE the code. 2) The updated component.</deliverable>
<format>Spec table: Breakpoint | Layout (stack/row/grid) | What changes (order, visibility, sizing, typography) | Token/utility used. Then the code.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- No horizontal overflow at any viewport from 320px upward.
- Touch targets remain >= 44x44px at mobile widths.
- Content order stays logical for keyboard/screen-reader users at every breakpoint (no visual reorder that breaks focus order unless aria-flow is handled).
- Every responsive value comes from the project scale - no arbitrary one-off values.
- Spec table and implementation match; any breakpoint behavior you had to infer is listed as DECISION NEEDED.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A breakpoint behavior spec table (Breakpoint | Layout | Changes | Token used) followed by the updated component code, with DECISION NEEDED flags for unspecified breakpoint behavior.

prompts.title: Refactor Media-Query Components to Container Queries
prompts.description: Decides where container queries beat viewport media queries for reusable components, then refactors the chosen components with explicit containment and fallback rules.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Refactor {{component_list}} in {{directory}} so their internal layout responds to their container's width (CSS container queries) instead of the viewport, so they render correctly in any parent context (sidebar, modal, full-width).</goal>
<rationale>Viewport media queries make components context-blind: {{component_list}} breaks when placed in {{problem_context, e.g. 'a 380px sidebar on a desktop screen'}}. Container queries make the components portable.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- MUST PRESERVE: the rendered result of each component in every context where it is currently used (list the current usages first and treat them as regression cases).
- Do NOT convert components whose layout genuinely depends on the viewport (e.g. sticky bars, full-bleed sections) - say which and why instead.
- Do NOT add a polyfill or dependency unless {{browser_support_floor}} requires it; if it does, state the tradeoff first and wait for confirmation.
- Keep the existing breakpoint values as container breakpoints unless one is clearly viewport-derived; flag any ambiguous value as DECISION NEEDED.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) A usage inventory: where each component renders today and at what widths. 2) Refactored components using container-type / @container with named containment contexts. 3) A behavior table per component.</deliverable>
<format>Behavior table: Container width range | Layout | What changes. Name every container (container-name) and document where the containment context is established.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each refactored component renders correctly at its documented current usages AND inside a {{test_widths, e.g. '320px and 480px'}} test wrapper.
- No remaining viewport media queries inside the refactored components' internal layout rules.
- container-type: inline-size is set at a deliberate wrapper, never on the component's own root in a way that breaks width measurement.
- Fallback behavior for {{browser_support_floor}} is stated explicitly.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A usage inventory of each component, refactored code using container-type/@container with named containment contexts, per-component behavior tables, and explicit fallback statements.

prompts.title: Full-Page Responsive Audit with Screenshot Evidence
prompts.description: Audits a page across a viewport matrix using screenshot evidence, classifies each defect, and fixes them in small verified diffs with a visual verification loop.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit {{page_or_route}} at {{viewport_matrix, e.g. '320, 375, 768, 1024, 1440px widths'}} and fix every responsive defect found, verifying each fix with a fresh screenshot.</goal>
<rationale>{{business_reason, e.g. 'a third of traffic is mobile and the checkout page overflows'}}. Fixes must be evidence-driven: every claim of 'fixed' must be backed by an actual re-render, not by reading the CSS and assuming.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Fix ONLY responsive/layout defects: overflow, clipped content, broken stacking, unreadable type, unreachable controls. Do NOT redesign, re-theme, or refactor component internals.
- Do NOT fix a defect by hiding content (display:none) unless I approve it; propose it and wait.
- One defect per change; do NOT batch unrelated fixes into one edit.
- If a defect's correct behavior is a design decision (e.g. table -> cards on mobile), mark it DECISION NEEDED with 2 options instead of choosing silently.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) A defect register. 2) One small fix per defect. 3) A verification table.</deliverable>
<format>Defect register: ID | Viewport(s) | Element | Defect (observed, from screenshot) | Severity (blocks-use / degrades / cosmetic). Verification table: Defect ID | Fix summary | Before/after evidence | Status.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every defect in the register cites observed evidence (screenshot or measured overflow), never 'this probably breaks'.
- Zero horizontal scroll at every audited viewport after fixes (state how you measured it).
- Every interactive element remains reachable and operable by keyboard at all audited widths; focus outlines are not clipped by overflow containers.
- Each fix's after-evidence is a re-captured screenshot or measurement; anything not re-verified is marked NOT VERIFIED.
- Final report marks the page DONE or NOT DONE per viewport, honestly.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A defect register with severity ratings, one small diff per defect, and a verification table where every fix is backed by re-captured screenshot/measurement evidence or explicitly marked NOT VERIFIED.

prompts.title: Add a Reduced-Motion-Safe Micro-Interaction
prompts.description: Adds a single hover/press micro-interaction to a component with a compact motion spec and mandatory prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Add a {{interaction_type, e.g. 'hover lift + press compress'}} micro-interaction to {{component_name}} in {{file_path}} that makes the control feel responsive without changing its layout footprint.</goal>
<rationale>Motion here signals interactivity and acknowledges input; but motion that shifts layout or ignores reduced-motion settings causes jank and accessibility harm.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Animate ONLY compositor-friendly properties (transform, opacity). Do NOT animate width, height, top/left, margin, or padding.
- Do NOT let the animation change the element's box size or push neighbors.
- Do NOT add an animation library for this single interaction; use CSS transitions consistent with {{reference_component}}.
- If the design intent for timing/easing is not specified anywhere in {{design_source}}, propose values from the scale below and mark them as proposals, not facts.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) A motion spec. 2) The CSS/utility changes.</deliverable>
<format>Motion spec: Trigger (hover/focus/active) | Property | Duration (120-250ms range) | Easing (name or cubic-bezier) | Reduced-motion behavior.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- prefers-reduced-motion: the transition resolves instantly (or to opacity-only) via a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule.
- Focus-visible triggers the same visual treatment as hover, so keyboard users get the feedback too.
- Duration stays within 120-250ms; easing is named, not 'smooth'.
- No layout shift: element's bounding box before/after is identical (state how you checked).
- Any value you chose without a design source is listed as PROPOSED for designer sign-off.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A motion spec table (Trigger | Property | Duration | Easing | Reduced-motion behavior) plus CSS changes limited to transform/opacity with a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.

prompts.title: State-Transition Animation Spec and Framer Motion Implementation
prompts.description: Designs enter/exit/variant transitions for a stateful component (modal, toast, accordion) as a motion spec first, then implements with Framer Motion including AnimatePresence and reduced-motion handling.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement enter, exit, and state-change animations for {{component_name}} (states: {{states, e.g. 'closed -> open -> dismissing'}}) using Framer Motion, driven by a written motion spec.</goal>
<rationale>State changes without motion feel abrupt; ad-hoc animation values across the codebase feel inconsistent. A spec first keeps this component aligned with the product's motion language and makes the a11y behavior explicit.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Use Framer Motion (already in the project at {{fm_version}}); do NOT add other animation libraries and do NOT hand-roll requestAnimationFrame.
- Animate transform/opacity for movement; layout animations (layout prop) only if listed in the spec below - justify any use.
- Exit animations must not block content removal from the accessibility tree longer than the animation duration.
- If {{design_source}} does not specify a duration/easing for a transition, use the product scale {{motion_scale, e.g. 'fast:150ms, base:250ms, slow:400ms / ease-out standard'}} and mark it PROPOSED.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) Motion spec table. 2) Updated component with variants + AnimatePresence. 3) Reduced-motion strategy note.</deliverable>
<format>Motion spec: State transition | Properties | Duration | Easing | Delay/stagger | Reduced-motion variant. One row per transition.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every state transition in {{states}} has exactly one spec row and matching implementation - no orphan animations.
- useReducedMotion (or MotionConfig reducedMotion) produces an instant or opacity-only variant for every transition.
- Unmount/exit completes via AnimatePresence; no setTimeout-based removal that can desync.
- Focus management on open/close is preserved or implemented (focus moves into modal on open, returns on close).
- No animation runs on elements while they are display:none or aria-hidden without a reason stated.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A motion spec table covering every state transition, a Framer Motion implementation using variants and AnimatePresence, and a reduced-motion strategy note with focus-management handling.

prompts.title: App-Wide Motion System: Durations, Easings, and View Transitions
prompts.description: Establishes a shared motion token layer (durations, easings, distances) plus cross-route view transitions, with performance budgets and a global reduced-motion strategy.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Create a motion token layer ({{motion_tokens_file}}) defining the app's duration/easing/distance scale, and wire {{route_transition_scope, e.g. 'primary route changes'}} through the View Transitions API (or {{framework_router}}'s equivalent), replacing today's ad-hoc animation values.</goal>
<rationale>Motion is currently inconsistent: {{evidence, e.g. '14 distinct durations across 9 components'}}. A tokenized scale plus standardized route transitions makes the product feel cohesive and keeps 60fps budgets enforceable.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- MUST PRESERVE: current interaction behavior and timing feel of {{critical_flows, e.g. 'checkout modal, nav drawer'}} - flag any change to these for approval before applying.
- Do NOT animate layout properties anywhere in the system; transform/opacity only. Do NOT introduce an animation dependency without asking.
- Do NOT retrofit every component in one pass; convert only {{initial_component_set}} and leave the rest on their current values with a migration note.
- Unspecified timings are DECISION NEEDED; propose from the scale, never invent silently.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) Motion token table. 2) Token definitions (CSS custom properties, e.g. --duration-fast/--ease-standard). 3) View-transition wiring for {{route_transition_scope}} with named view-transition-name rules. 4) Conversion of {{initial_component_set}} to tokens.</deliverable>
<format>Token table: Token | Value | Intended use | Replaces (old ad-hoc values). Include a reduced-motion mapping for every tokenized effect.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Scale has =< {{max_scale_steps, e.g. '4 durations, 3 easings'}}; each token has a stated intended use.
- Global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule collapses durations and disables route cross-fades.
- View transitions degrade gracefully where the API is unsupported (feature-detected, no errors).
- No animated property triggers layout/paint (verify via DevTools rendering info or code inspection; state which).
- Old ad-hoc values in converted components: zero remaining (grep evidence pasted).
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A motion token table and CSS custom-property scale, View Transitions wiring with feature detection and reduced-motion collapse, conversion of an initial component set, and grep evidence that ad-hoc values are gone.

prompts.title: Add Dark Mode to One Component via Semantic Tokens
prompts.description: Makes a single component theme-aware by routing all its colors through semantic tokens with light and dark values, including contrast verification.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Make {{component_name}} in {{file_path}} render correctly in both light and dark themes by routing every color it uses through semantic tokens defined in {{tokens_file}}.</goal>
<rationale>The app switches themes via {{theme_switch_mechanism, e.g. 'a data-theme attribute on <html>'}}, but {{component_name}} hard-codes colors and breaks in dark mode ({{observed_problem}}).</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Replace ONLY color values (background, text, border, shadow, icon fills); do NOT change spacing, sizing, typography, or layout.
- Do NOT introduce new semantic tokens if a fitting one already exists in {{tokens_file}} - reuse first; list any new token as PROPOSED with the gap it fills.
- Do NOT set dark styles by overriding selectors ad hoc per component; dark values belong in the token layer under {{dark_scope, e.g. '[data-theme="dark"]'}}.
- If a color has no obvious semantic role, mark it DECISION NEEDED rather than inventing a name.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) Token usage map. 2) Any PROPOSED new tokens with light+dark values. 3) The refactored component.</deliverable>
<format>Token usage map: Element/part | Semantic role | Token | Light value | Dark value.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Zero hard-coded colors remain in the component (hex, rgb, hsl, named colors) - paste grep evidence.
- Text/background pairs meet WCAG 2.2 contrast: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text and UI component boundaries - compute each pair in BOTH themes and show the ratios.
- Focus indicator is visible in both themes with >= 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors.
- The component is verified rendered in both themes (screenshot or stated manual check); unverified = NOT VERIFIED.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A token usage map (Element | Role | Token | Light | Dark), PROPOSED new tokens if any, the refactored component, and computed WCAG contrast ratios for both themes.

prompts.title: Choose a Theming Strategy (CSS Variables vs Tailwind dark: vs Attribute-Based Tokens)
prompts.description: Options-and-tradeoffs decision prompt for selecting the theme-switching mechanism for an app before committing to an implementation.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Recommend a theming strategy for {{app_name}}: how themes are defined, switched, and persisted, given {{stack, e.g. 'Next.js App Router + Tailwind'}}.</goal>
<rationale>The mechanism chosen here determines flash-of-wrong-theme behavior, SSR compatibility, and how painful a third theme (e.g. high-contrast or brand B) will be. Reversing it later touches every component.</rationale>
<context>Themes required: {{themes, e.g. 'light, dark, system-follows-OS'}}. SSR: {{ssr_yes_no}}. Token state: {{current_tokens, e.g. 'semantic tokens exist / only Tailwind defaults'}}. Persistence: {{persistence, e.g. 'user preference in profile + localStorage'}}.</context>
<boundaries>
- Do NOT write implementation code; this is a decision deliverable. Example snippets of =<15 lines per option are allowed to make mechanics concrete.
- Do NOT dismiss an option for fashion reasons; every con must be a concrete cost (FOUC risk, specificity wars, bundle, SSR edge case).
- If a deciding fact is missing, mark it DECISION NEEDED and state how it flips the recommendation.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>A comparison of these three candidate mechanisms - (A) semantic CSS custom properties scoped by [data-theme], (B) Tailwind dark: variant utilities, (C) hybrid: Tailwind utilities backed by token variables - plus a weighted decision matrix and one recommendation.</deliverable>
<format>For each: how a theme is defined, how switching works at runtime, SSR/first-paint behavior, effort to add a third theme, pros, cons, failure mode. Matrix weighted by {{criteria, e.g. 'SSR correctness 35%, multi-theme future 35%, migration effort 30%'}}.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Each option explicitly addresses: no-flash first paint on SSR, system-preference detection, and persistence.
- Exactly one recommendation with the deciding criterion named; push back if my weighting is wrong for the stated context.
- Migration sketch from {{current_tokens}} to the recommended option: rough file/effort scope, not code.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: Three theming mechanisms compared on definition/switching/SSR/third-theme cost, a criteria-weighted decision matrix, one recommendation with deciding criterion, and a rough migration sketch.

prompts.title: Multi-Brand Theming Architecture Spec
prompts.description: Produces a binding SPEC.md for white-label/multi-brand theming - token tiers, theme definition format, runtime switching, asset overrides - before any implementation begins.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Produce a binding specification ({{spec_path, e.g. 'docs/SPEC-theming.md'}}) for multi-brand theming: {{brand_count}} brands x light/dark, selectable at {{switch_point, e.g. 'build time per tenant / runtime per subdomain'}}.</goal>
<rationale>We are about to onboard tenant brands and theming is currently single-brand. Writing code before agreeing on the token contract, theme file format, and override rules would lock in the wrong abstractions. This spec will be the artifact implementation sessions are held to.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- This session produces the SPEC ONLY - no implementation code beyond illustrative snippets.
- Do NOT design for hypothetical requirements; every feature in the spec must trace to a requirement I gave or be listed under Open Questions.
- Do NOT prescribe a styling-solution migration (e.g. 'rewrite everything in Tailwind') as a prerequisite; the architecture must work with {{current_stack}}.
- Where requirements conflict or are underspecified, write them into an Open Questions section as DECISION NEEDED with options - do NOT resolve them by assumption.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>{{spec_path}} with these sections: Goal & rationale; Token tier model (primitive/semantic/component and what brands may override at each tier); Theme definition format (file shape, naming, validation rules); Switching & loading strategy (runtime vs build-time, FOUC handling, per-tenant asset overrides such as logos/fonts); Out of scope (explicit); Invariants (must-preserve list); Acceptance criteria (checkable); End-to-end verification step (a concrete procedure proving a second brand renders correctly).</deliverable>
<acceptance_criteria>
- A reader can implement without asking me anything except the listed Open Questions.
- Every acceptance criterion is mechanically checkable ('build emits dist/themes/brand-b.css' - not 'themes work well').
- Spec states which tier each brand override lives at and forbids primitive-tier overrides by consumers, with rationale.
- Contrast responsibility is assigned: how a brand-supplied palette is validated against WCAG 2.2 minimums, and what happens when it fails.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A binding SPEC.md covering token tiers, theme file format, switching/loading strategy, out-of-scope, invariants, checkable acceptance criteria, an E2E verification step, and an Open Questions / DECISION NEEDED section.

prompts.title: Build a Complete Component State Matrix
prompts.description: Generates the full interaction-state matrix for a component (default/hover/focus/active/disabled/loading/error) and implements every cell, flagging unspecified designs instead of inventing them.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement the complete state matrix for {{component_name}} in {{file_path}}: {{state_set, e.g. 'default, hover, focus-visible, active/pressed, disabled, loading, error'}} x {{variant_set, e.g. 'primary, secondary, danger'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Missing states are the top source of 'unpolished' UI and a11y failures (invisible focus, clickable-when-disabled). The matrix makes completeness explicit and reviewable before code.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Source of truth for visuals: {{design_source, e.g. 'Fable library file / existing tokens'}}. If a cell of the matrix has no specified design, mark it DECISION NEEDED and style it from the closest specified state - do NOT invent a novel treatment.
- Do NOT change the component's props/API, markup structure, or behavior - styles and state attributes only.
- Every state must be reachable by the means users actually trigger it: focus-visible via keyboard (:focus-visible, not :focus), disabled via the disabled attribute (never pointer-events:none on a focusable element without aria-disabled handling).
- No inaccessible div-buttons: if the component is not already a real <button>/<a>, STOP and flag it instead of styling a div.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) State matrix table. 2) Updated styles. 3) A11y verification list.</deliverable>
<format>Matrix rows = states, columns = variants; each cell: token(s) used or DECISION NEEDED.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Every matrix cell is filled; no state falls through to an unintended default.
- Focus indicator >= 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors in every variant (WCAG 2.2).
- Disabled state: not focusable/activatable via keyboard or pointer, and conveyed programmatically.
- Loading state: announced appropriately (aria-busy or live region) and control is not double-submittable.
- {{test_command, e.g. 'storybook stories render each cell'}} covers every matrix cell.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A state x variant matrix with tokens per cell (or DECISION NEEDED), the implemented styles, and an a11y verification list covering focus contrast, disabled semantics, and loading announcement.

prompts.title: Design a Variant API for a Component (CVA / data-attributes)
prompts.description: Chooses and implements a type-safe variant API (intent/size/tone) for a component family, with compound variants and a variant x state coverage check.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Refactor {{component_family, e.g. 'Button + IconButton'}} to a declarative variant API: props like {{variant_axes, e.g. 'intent: primary|secondary|danger; size: sm|md|lg'}} driving styling via {{variant_tech, e.g. 'CVA (class-variance-authority) / data-attributes + CSS'}}.</goal>
<rationale>Styling is currently {{current_pain, e.g. 'stringly-typed className overrides at 20+ call sites'}}, so variants drift and states get lost. A constrained variant API makes invalid combinations unrepresentable.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- First pick the mechanism: if {{variant_tech}} lists two, compare them in =<10 lines (type safety, runtime cost, specificity behavior) and recommend one before implementing.
- MUST PRESERVE: every existing call site's rendered output. Inventory all usages of the family first and treat each as a regression case.
- Do NOT add a dependency without stating it; CVA only if not already present.
- Do NOT expose a generic className-escape-hatch that bypasses variants unless one exists today - note it if it does.
- Compound variants (e.g. danger+sm) without a specified design: DECISION NEEDED, fallback to base variant styling.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) Usage inventory. 2) Mechanism choice with =<10-line rationale. 3) Refactored component(s) with typed variant props + variant definitions. 4) Migrated call sites.</deliverable>
<format>Variant definition table: Axis | Values | Tokens per value. Compound variant table where designs exist.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Type system rejects invalid axis values ({{type_check_command}} passes).
- All interaction states from the existing component still work within every variant (state coverage noted per variant).
- Every call site from the inventory renders unchanged (visual check or snapshot test result pasted; unverified = NOT VERIFIED).
- No visual value lives outside the token layer.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A usage inventory, a mechanism recommendation, typed variant props with a variant/token definition table, migrated call sites, and evidence that type-checking and existing rendering are preserved.

prompts.title: Component Library State-Coverage Audit with Verifier Pass
prompts.description: Audits every exported component in a library for state and variant coverage against a required matrix, then has a fresh-context verifier confirm each COVERED claim with quoted evidence.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit every exported component in {{library_dir}} for coverage of the required state set {{required_states, e.g. 'hover, focus-visible, disabled, loading, error, empty'}} and variant set {{required_variants}}, producing a coverage matrix and fixing the gaps you own.</goal>
<rationale>Consumers hit missing states in production ({{example_incident}}). An honest, evidence-backed matrix is the deliverable; inflated 'all good' claims are worse than no audit.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Audit ALL exported components; do NOT sample.
- Fix ONLY gaps that are mechanical (missing disabled styling, missing focus ring, missing aria-busy on loading). Gaps requiring design input (an error-state visual that does not exist) are DECISION NEEDED - do NOT invent the design.
- Do NOT change component APIs, rename exports, or restyle anything that is already covered.
- Ground every verdict in the actual code: quote the selector/attribute that implements a state. No verdict from memory or from a component's name.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) Coverage matrix: rows = components, columns = required states/variants; cell = COVERED (quoted evidence) / PARTIAL / MISSING / N-A (justified) / DECISION NEEDED. 2) Fixes for mechanical gaps. 3) Verifier instructions block (below).</deliverable>
<format>Markdown matrix + fix diffs + verifier brief.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Matrix covers every exported component x every required state; totals row stated (N covered, M missing, K decision-needed).
- Every COVERED cell carries quoted code evidence; assertions without quotes are invalid.
- Mechanical fixes keep diffs minimal and pass {{test_command}} (paste output).
- Final step: hand the matrix + diffs to a fresh-context verifier with ONLY this task and the library code; its brief: 'Assume verdicts are wrong. Re-check each COVERED cell against the code; report CONFIRMED or WRONG with evidence.' Include its findings verbatim and correct any WRONG cells.
- Closing status: DONE / NOT DONE per component, honestly.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A full component x state coverage matrix with quoted evidence per COVERED cell, minimal diffs for mechanical gaps, and a verbatim fresh-context verifier report with corrections applied.

prompts.title: Implement a Screen from a Design Screenshot with Honest Deviation Report
prompts.description: Builds a screen from a provided screenshot/mockup, mapping visuals to tokens, then iterates with rendered screenshots and reports every deviation instead of claiming a match.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Implement {{screen_name}} at {{route_or_file}} so the rendered result matches the provided design ({{design_artifact, e.g. 'attached screenshot / Fable export'}}) as closely as our token system allows.</goal>
<rationale>This screen is {{priority_reason}}. Fidelity matters, but invented precision does not: the design shows rendered pixels, not specs, so every value must be either mapped to a token or explicitly flagged.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- Use ONLY tokens from {{tokens_file}} and primitives from {{component_library}}. A design value with no matching token: use the nearest token and log it as a deviation - do NOT introduce one-off pixel values.
- Do NOT build anything not visible in the design (no extra buttons, placeholder features, or 'improvements').
- Do NOT invent states the design does not show; list them (hover, focus, error, loading, empty, mobile widths) as DECISION NEEDED in the report.
- Match structure semantically: headings, lists, nav, buttons as real elements - no div-soup reconstruction of the pixels.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>1) The screen implementation. 2) A token-mapping table. 3) A deviation report.</deliverable>
<format>Token mapping: Design element | Observed value | Token used | Exact match / nearest. Deviation report: Element | Expected (from design) | Actual | Reason (token gap / unspecified / constraint).</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Render the result and compare against the design (screenshot vs screenshot); iterate smallest diffs until remaining deviations are all token-level or flagged.
- Every deviation appears in the report with a reason - the report must never be empty-by-assertion ('matches perfectly' is not acceptable without evidence).
- Keyboard focus visible on all interactive elements; tab order matches visual order.
- Text contrast >= WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 / 3:1 large) using actual token values, computed, not eyeballed.
- Anything you could not verify rendered = NOT VERIFIED.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: The implemented screen, a design-element-to-token mapping table, and a deviation report where every mismatch carries a reason (token gap / unspecified / constraint), plus contrast and focus verification.

prompts.title: Design Fidelity Audit: Implemented UI vs Spec
prompts.description: Independent audit comparing an already-implemented screen against the design spec/screenshot, producing a graded deviation list with evidence and smallest-fix suggestions - no silent rewrites.
prompts.prompt:
<task>
<goal>Audit the implemented {{screen_or_component}} ({{code_path}}, rendered at {{route}}) against {{design_reference}} and produce an evidence-backed deviation report with a prioritized fix list.</goal>
<rationale>{{reason, e.g. 'design review flagged the shipped page as off-spec'}}. The team needs ground truth on what actually diverges - not a rewrite, and not reassurance.</rationale>
<boundaries>
- This is an AUDIT: produce the report and, only for items marked [safe-fix], the smallest correcting diff. Do NOT restructure the component, rename anything, or fix unlisted issues - note those under Observations instead.
- Judge against the design reference ONLY; do not impose your own taste. If the design is ambiguous on a point, the verdict is SPEC GAP, not a defect.
- Every deviation must cite observed evidence: computed value, measured px, or screenshot region - never 'looks wrong'.
- Respect the token system: a mismatch caused by an intentional token constraint is CLASSIFY: token-constrained, not a bug.
</boundaries>
</task>

<contract>
<deliverable>Deviation report + fix list (+ diffs for [safe-fix] items only).</deliverable>
<format>Table: # | Element | Spec says (source: screenshot region/spec line) | Implementation does (evidence: computed value/px) | Class: defect / token-constrained / spec-gap / decision-needed | Severity: blocks-use / visible / polish | Fix: [safe-fix] smallest change, or [needs-design] question for designer.</format>
<acceptance_criteria>
- Coverage stated: which regions/elements of the design were compared (header, nav, card grid, footer...) - nothing silently skipped.
- Every 'defect' row has both sides evidenced (spec source + computed/measured actual).
- Each [safe-fix] diff is applied and re-verified rendered; result pasted or marked NOT VERIFIED.
- Fix list is severity-ordered; estimated scope (S/M/L) per item.
- Closing verdict: N defects, M token-constrained, K spec-gaps, J decision-needed; page status SHIP / FIX-FIRST honestly stated.
</acceptance_criteria>
</contract>
prompts.expectedOutput: A severity-ordered deviation table classifying each mismatch as defect / token-constrained / spec-gap / decision-needed with evidence on both sides, plus applied [safe-fix] diffs and an honest SHIP / FIX-FIRST verdict.
